But the flat surfaces of glass vessels are pure, even according to the Rabbis, for the Rabbis made a distinction (a somewhat different law) regarding glassware (see Tractate Shabbat 16a) for just as they don’t burn upon them heave offering and Holy Things.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:3)


**מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא.** אֲבָל לֹא חָזְרוּ לְטֻמְאָתָן יְשָׁנָה, דְּלֹא גַזּוּר רַבָּנָן שֶׁאִם עָשָׂה מֵהֶם כֵּלִים חָזְרוּ לְטֻמְאָתָן יְשָׁנָה אֶלָּא בִּכְלֵי מַתָּכוֹת בִּלְבַד:


מקבלין טומאה מכאן ולהבא – but they don’t return to their old defilement, for the Rabbis did not decree that if he made from them [new] vessels they return to their old defilement, but rather only a metal utensils/vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:4)


**כְּלֵי נֶתֶר.** כֵּלִים הָעֲשׂוּיִין מֵאֲדָמָה שֶׁחוֹפְרִים מִמֶּנָּה צָרִיף, אלומ"י בְּלַעַ"ז:


כלי נתר (vessels made from alum crystals)– vessels that are made from earth that they dig from it alum crystals. ALUMI in the foreign language.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:5)


**מִטַּמְּאִין וּמְטַמְּאִין בַּאֲוִיר.** אִם נִתְלֵית טֻמְאָה בַּאֲוִיר הַכְּלִי, נִטְמָא הַכְּלִי. חָזַר וְתָלָה אֳכָלִים בַּאֲוִירָן, מְטַמְּאִין אֶת הָאֳכָלִים אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָגְעוּ, דִּכְתִיב (ויקרא יא) כָּל אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹכוֹ יִטְמָא. וַאֲפִלּוּ מָלֵא חַרְדָּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ נוֹגֵעַ בְּדָפְנוֹת הַכְּלִי:


מיטמאין ומטמאין באויר (they are both unclean and convey uncleanness through their contained airspace) – it the defilement is suspended in the airspace of the vessel, the vessel is unclean. If he went back and suspended food in their airspace, he defiles the food, even though they did not touch, as it is written (Leviticus 11:33): “[And if any of those falls into an earthen vessel,] everything inside it shall be pure [and – the vessel – itself you shall break].” And even the size of a mustard seed that does not touch the walls of the vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:6)


**וּמִטַּמְּאִין מֵאֲחוֹרֵיהֶן.** כֵּלִים שֶׁחֲקַק בֵּית מוֹשָׁבָם מִבַּחוּץ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁעוֹשִׂים לְכוֹסוֹת שֶׁל כֶּסֶף, וּפְעָמִים כּוֹפִין אוֹתָן עַל פִּיהֶן וּמִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁין בְּבֵית קִבּוּל שֶׁבַּאֲחוֹרֵיהֶן. אִם נָגְעָה טֻמְאָה בְאוֹתוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל, נִטְמָא הַכְּלִי חֶרֶס. וּמִדְּלֹא עַרְבִינְהוּ וְתַנִּינְהוּ, מִטַּמְּאִין וּמְטַמְּאִין מֵאֲוִירֵיהֶן וַאֲחוֹרֵיהֶן, שְׁמַע מִנַּהּ דְּאֵין מִטַּמֵּא מֵאֲוִיר אֲחוֹרָיו, דְּלָא חֲשִׁיב תּוֹךְ שֶׁל אֲחוֹרָיו תּוֹךְ גָּמוּר דְּאוֹרַיְתָא לִטַּמֵּא מֵאֲוִירוֹ, אֲבָל מִטַּמֵּא אִם נָגְעָה טֻמְאָה בְּאוֹתוֹ חֲקָק שֶׁל אֲחוֹרָיו:


ומיטמאין מאחוריהן (they impart uncleanness from their outer sides) – vessels that hollowed out/shaped a receptacle from their place of sitting in the manner that they make for silver cups, and sometimes they turn them upside down on their mouths and use their receptacles from their outer side. If it came in contact with defilement with that receptacle, the earthenware utensil is defiled. But if they did not mix them and repeat it they are defiled and defile from their airspace an from their outer sides, we learn from it that they are defiled from the airspace from the outer side, for we don’t consider the inside that is on the outer side as a complete inside of the Torah, to be defiled from its airspace, but it is defiled if it the defilement came in contact with the same hollowing out that is on its outer side.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:7)


**וְאֵין מִטַּמְּאִין מִגַּבֵּיהֶן.** דִּכְתִיב (שם) וּכְלִי חֶרֶשׂ אֲשֶׁר יִפֹּל מֵהֶם אֶל תּוֹכוֹ, מִתּוֹכוֹ הוּא מִטַּמֵּא וְאֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא מִגַּבּוֹ. וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַכֵּלִים חוּץ מִכְּלֵי חֶרֶס וּכְלֵי נֶתֶר אֵין מִטַּמְּאִין מֵאֲוִירָן עַד שֶׁתִּגַּע הַטֻּמְאָה בְעַצְמוֹ שֶׁל כְּלִי, וּכְשֶׁנָּגְעָה הַטֻּמְאָה בְעַצְמוֹ שֶׁל כְּלִי בֵּין מִגַּבּוֹ בֵּין מִתּוֹכוֹ טָמֵא. וְהַיְנוּ דִתְנַן בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּחֻלִּין, הַטָּהוֹר בִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס טָמֵא בְכָל הַכֵּלִים, הַטָּהוֹר בְּכָל הַכֵּלִים טָמֵא בִכְלֵי חֶרֶס:


ואין מיטמאין מגביהן – as it is written (Leviticus 11:33): “Any if any of those falls into an earthen vessel (i.e., an article of wood, a cloth, a skin, or a sack), [everything inside it shall be impure and – the vessel- itself you shall break],” from inside it becomes defiles but it does become defiled from outside it. But all of the other vessels excluding an earthenware vessel and a vessel of alum crystal are not defiled from their airspace until the defilement touches/comes in contact with the essence of the vessel, but when the defilement touches the essence of the vessel, whether from the outside or from the inside, it is impure, as is taught in the Mishnah in the first chapter of [Tractate] Hullin (Chapter 1, Mishnah 6): “What is clean (insusceptible to uncleanness[ in the case of earthenware vessels is unclean [susceptible in the case of all [other] vessels. What is clean in the case of all [other utensils] is unclean in the case of the earthenware utensils.”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:1:8)


**וּשְׁבִירָתָן הִיא טָהֳרָתָן.** וְכֻלְּהוּ כֵּלִים נַמִּי שְׁבִירָתָן הִיא טָהֳרָתָן. אֶלָּא כְלֵי חֶרֶס וּכְלֵי נֶתֶר שְׁבִירָתָן בִּלְבַד מְטַהֲרָתָן, שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם טָהֳרָה בִטְבִילָה אֶלָּא בִשְׁבִירָה בִּלְבַד:


ושבירתן היא טהרתן = all of vessels/utensils, breaking them is their purification, but earthenware vessels and vessels of alum crystal breaking them alone purifies them, but they have no purification through ritual immersion other than through breaking [them] alone.



### Mishnah 2

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:1)


**הַדַּקִּין שֶׁבִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס.** כְּלֵי חֶרֶס הַדַּקִּין וּקְטַנִּים, בֵּין שֶׁהֵן עַצְמָן אֵינָן מַחֲזִיקִין אֶלָּא כְדֵי סִיכַת קָטָן, בֵּין שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ וְנִשְׁאֲרוּ קַרְקְרוֹתֵיהֶן, פֵּרוּשׁ, כְּמוֹ קַרְקְעוֹתֵיהֶן דְּהַיְנוּ שׁוּלַיִם שֶׁכְּלַפֵּי הַקַּרְקַע, אוֹ נִשְׁאֲרוּ דָפְנוֹתֵיהֶן וִיכוֹלִים לְבַדָּן לֵישֵׁב בְּלֹא סְמִיכָה, עֲדַיִן כֵּלִים הֵן. וְאִם מַחֲזִיקִין שֶׁמֶן כְּדֵי סִיכַת קָטָן, כְּלוֹמַר כְּדֵי סִיכַת אֶצְבַּע קְטַנָּה שֶׁל קָטָן בֶּן יוֹמוֹ, טְמֵאִין. וְהָכִי מְפֹרָשׁ בְּמַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת, סִיכַת קָטָן, אֵבָר קָטָן שֶׁל קָטָן בֶּן יוֹמוֹ:


הדקין שבכלי חרס – thin and small earthenware vessels, whether they themselves cannot support/hold other than only up the anointing of a small [finger of a child] or whether they were broken and their rimmed bottom remained, an explanation: like their rimmed bottoms of a vessel, that is the rim that is towards the ground, or their walls/sides which remained and alone are able to sit without supports, are still vessels. And if they hold enough oil to anoint a small thing, that is to say, the anointing of a small finger of a day-old baby, they are impure. And this is explained in the Tractate Shabbat [77b] (and also Tractate Eduyot, Chapter 4, Mishnah 6 – as explained by Tosefot Yom Tov), the anointing of a minor, one small limb of a minor of the age of one-day old.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:2)


**עַד לֹג.** שִׁעוּר זֶה שֶׁל סִיכַת קָטָן, לְשִׁבְרֵי כְלִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ אֶלָּא לֹג. דְּאִם הָיָה תְחִלָּתוֹ יוֹתֵר מִלֹּג, בָּעִינַן שִׁעוּר גָּדוֹל לִשְׁבָרָיו יוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי סִיכַת קָטָן:


עד לוג – this measurement of the anointing of a minor, for the shards of a vessel that had not been from its outset other than a LOG (i.e., a LOG is the equivalent of the liquid displaced by six eggs). But if there was from the outset more than a LOG, we need a larger measure for the shards, more than in order to anoint [the small limb of] a minor [who is one day-old].


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:3)


**מִלֹּג וְעַד סְאָה.** כְּלִי שֶׁהָיָה מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ מַחֲזִיק מִלֹּג וְיוֹתֵר מִלֹּג עַד סְאָה, שִׁעוּר שְׁבָרָיו בִּרְבִיעִית הַלֹּג. וּלְיָתֵר מִסְּאָה עַד סְאָתַיִם, שִׁעוּר שְׁבָרָיו בַּחֲצִי לֹג. וְכֵן כֻּלָּם:


מלוג ועד סאה – a vessel that would at its outset hold from a LOG and more than a LOG until a SESAH, the measure of its shards is one-quarter of a LOG. And for more than a SEAH until two SEAH, the measurement of its shards is one-half a LOG and similarly for all of them.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:4)


**אֲנִי אֵינִי נוֹתֵן בָּהֶם מִדָּה.** לְפִי גֹדֶל הַכְּלִי וְקָטְנוֹ, אֶלָּא לְפִי הַמְּקוֹמוֹת שֶׁרְגִילִין לַעֲשׂוֹתָן וּלְפִי צוּרַת הַכֵּלִים:


אני איני נותן בהם מדה – according to the largeness of the vessel or its smallness, but according to the places where it is customarily done and according to the structure/form of the utensils.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:5)


**אֶלָּא הַדַּקִּין שֶׁבִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס וְכוּ'.** שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם צוּרַת קְדֵרוֹת וְהֵם קְטַנִּים בְּיוֹתֵר, שִׁעוּר שִׁבְרֵיהֶן כְּדֵי סִיכַת קָטָן. וּמִשֶּׁהִגִּיעוּ לִהְיוֹת כְּתַבְנִית קְדֵרוֹת קְטַנּוֹת, שִׁעוּרָן בִּרְבִיעִית:


אלא הדקין שבכלי חרס וכו' – that they don’t have the form of pots and they. But when the reach to be like the form of small pots, their measure is one-quarter of a LOG.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:6)


**חָבִיּוֹת לוּדִיּוֹת.** חָבִיּוֹת שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוֹת בְּלוֹד:


חביות לודיות – jugs that are made in Lod/Lydda.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:7)


**לַחְמִיּוֹת.** שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוֹת בְּבֵית לֶחֶם. וְהֵן גְּדוֹלוֹת מֵאוֹתָן שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוֹת בְּלוֹד:


לחמיות – [jugs] that are made in Bethlehem. But they are larger than the ones that are made in Lod/Lydda.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:2:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:8)


**חֲצָבִים גְּדוֹלִים.** כַּדּוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת כָּל מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר:


חצבים גדולים (stone pitchers/earthen jugs) – large pitchers all that is possible.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:2:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:9)


**הַפַּכִּין הַגְּלִילִים.** שֶׁנַּעֲשִׂים בְּאֶרֶץ הַגָּלִיל:


הפכים הגלילים (flasks/jars with a narrow neck) – that are made in the land of the Galilee.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:2:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:10)


**וְהֶחָבִיּוֹנוֹת.** חָבִיּוֹת קְטַנּוֹת. וְהַיְנוּ דַקִּין שֶׁבִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס:


והחביונות (small vessel, flask with flat sides) – small jugs, and these are thin ones of earthenware vessels.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:2:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:2:11)


**וְאֵין לָהֶן דְּפָנוֹת.** דְּדַוְקָא הַשּׁוּלַיִם טְמֵאוֹת אִם נִשְׁאַר בָּהֶן כְּדֵי סִיכַת קָטָן, אֲבָל הַדְּפָנוֹת טְהוֹרוֹת. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:


ואין להן דפנות – that specifically their rims are impure if there remains in them the amount of oil to anoint the small finger of a child, but their sides are pure And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Akiva.



### Mishnah 3

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:1)


**הַטְּהוֹרִים שֶׁבִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס.** פְּשׁוּטֵי כְלֵי חֶרֶס שֶׁהֵן טְהוֹרִים, דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ (ויקרא יא) אֲשֶׁר יִפֹּל מֵהֶם אֶל תּוֹכוֹ, אֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תּוֹךְ טָמֵא, אֶת שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ טָהוֹר:


הטהורים שבכלי חרס – flat earthenware vessels (without a receptacle) which are pure, as it is written concerning them (Leviticus 11:33): “And if any of those (i.e., an article of wood, or a cloth, or a skin, or a sack – see previous verse) falls into [an earthen vessel, everything inside it shall be impure and -the vessel – itself you shall break],” that which has an inside is impure; that which lacks an inside is pure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:2)


**טַבְלָה שֶׁאֵין לָהּ לִזְבֵּז.** לוּחַ חָלָק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שָׂפָה סָבִיב:


טבלא שאין לו לזבז (a tray without a rim/edge) – a smooth board that lacks a rim around it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:3)


**וּמַחְתָּה.** שֶׁחוֹתִים בָּהּ גֶּחָלִים:


ומחתה (a coal-pan) – that they take coals out with a pan.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:4)


**פְּרוּצָה.** שֶׁאֵין לָהּ דְּפָנוֹת:


פרוצה (the rims of are broken off) – that it does not have sides/walls.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:5)


**אַבּוּב שֶׁל קַלָּאִים.** כְּלִי חֶרֶס שֶׁקּוֹלִים בּוֹ קִטְנִיּוֹת עַל גַּבֵּי הָאֵשׁ. וּפָשׁוּט הוּא בְלֹא בֵית קִבּוּל, וּמְנֻקָּב כִּכְבָרָה בְשׁוּלָיו כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא הָאוּר שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ:


אבוב של קלאים (an iron tube for roasting grain) – earthenware vessel that they roast pulse/peas over a fire. And it is flat/plain without a receptacle and is perforated like a basket used as a sieve on its rims in order that the heat [of the fire] can have power over it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:6)


**קַלָּאִים.** כְּמוֹ קָלוּי בָּאֵשׁ:


[The word] קלאים/parched ears is parched by fire.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:7)


**וְסִילוֹנוֹת.** מַרְזֵבוֹת:


סילונות – tubes/spouts.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:8)


**אַף עַל פִּי כְפוּפִין.** אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכְּפוּפִין מִשְּׁנֵי צִדֵּיהֶן. וְהוּא שֶׁלֹּא חָקַק בָּהֶן בֵּית קִבּוּל צְרוֹרוֹת:


אף על פי כפופין – even though they are bent from their two sides. And this is which they did not shape a receptacle surrounding them.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:9)


**כַּבְכָּב.** כְּלִי שֶׁמְּכַסִּים בּוֹ סַלִּים שֶׁל פַּת. וְיֵשׁ גּוֹרְסִין כַּפְכַּף. שֶׁכּוֹפִין אוֹתוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הַסַּל. וַאֲפִלּוּ יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּית קִבּוּל, טָהוֹר. שֶׁכָּל הַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ כָּפוּי בִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס, טָהוֹר:


כבכב (an arched round vessel) – a vessel in which they cover bread baskets (but not as a receptacle). And there are those who have the reading of כפכף – that they cover it on top of the basket. But even if it has a receptacle, it is [ritually] pure for all who use something bent with an earthenware vessel is [ritually] pure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:10)


**וְהַטְּפִי.** הוּא כְּלִי חֶרֶס שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל וּמְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, דְּהָכִי מוֹכַח לְקַמָּן בְּאִידָךְ פִּרְקָא. וְהַאי דְטָהוֹר הָכָא, מִשּׁוּם דְּהִתְקִינוֹ לַעֲנָבִים וְעָשָׂה בּוֹ שִׁנּוּי, מוֹכִיחַ דִּלְכַסּוֹת בּוֹ עֲנָבִים קָא בָּעֵי לֵיהּ וְלֹא נַעֲשָׂה לְקַבָּלָה:


והטפי (vessel with a narrow neck – made with intention of using it for grapes) – it is an earthenware vessel that has a receptacle and is susceptible to receive defilement, and this is proven further on in the other chapter (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 3, Mishnah 2). But this is [ritually] pure here, because they (i.e., the Rabbis) prepared it as a cover for grapes and they made a change in it, which proves that they require it for covering graves and it was not made for reception.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:11)


**חָבִית שֶׁל שַׁיָּטִין.** כְּמִין חָבִית חֲלוּלָה, וּסְתוּמָה הִיא וְאֵין לָהּ פֶּה, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְהֵא נִשְׁקַעַת בַּמַּיִם. וְנִשְׁעָנִים עָלֶיהָ וּלְמֵדִין לָשׁוּט בָּהּ. וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל, אֵינָהּ עֲשׂוּיָה לְקַבָּלָה. וְכָל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי לְקַבָּלָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל אֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה:


חבית של שייטין (swimmers’ bottle used for practicing) – like a hallowed out jug, and it is closed and doesn’t have a mouth (i.e., opening), in order that It would not sink in the water. And they lean upon it and learn to swim by it. But it even though it has a receptacle, it is not designed for receiving anything And anything which is not made for receiving anything even though it has a receptacle is not susceptible to receiving defilement.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:12)


**וְחָבִית דְּפוּנָה בְשׁוּלֵי הַמַּחַץ.** מַחַץ הוּא כְלִי גָדוֹל שֶׁל חֶרֶס, וּכְעֵין חָבִית עָשׂוּי לוֹ בְשׁוּלָיו שֶׁאָדָם מֵשִׂים יָדוֹ לְתוֹכָהּ כְּשֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהַגְבִּיהַּ הַמַּחַץ. וּלְפִי שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשֵׂית חָבִית זוֹ לְקַבָּלָה, אֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה:


וחבית דפונה בשולי המחץ (an attachment in the shape of a jar fitted into the projecting rims of a vessel – to serve as a handle) – a ladle for filling vessels out of the well or wine or oil-pit which is a large earthenware vessel and it is a kind of jar made at its rim that a person can place his hand into it when he wants to lift the ladle, and because of this, the jar was not made for reception, and is not susceptible to receive defilement.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:13)


**דְּפוּנָה.** טְמוּנָה:


דפונה – fitted into.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:14)


**וְהַמִּטָּה וְהַכִּסֵּא וְהַסַּפְסָל.** כָּל אֵלּוּ אֵין עֲשׂוּיִין לְקַבָּלָה:


המטה והכסא והספסל – all of these are not designed for reception.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:15)


**וְהַסְּפִינָה.** אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעֲשׂוּיָה לְקַבָּלָה וַאֲפִלּוּ הִיא שֶׁל חֶרֶס, טְהוֹרָה. וּבְמַסֶּכֶת שַׁבָּת יָלְפִינַן לַהּ דִּכְתִיב (משלי ל) דֶּרֶךְ אֳנִיָּה בְלֶב יָם, וּפְשִׁיטָא דָאֳנִיָּה בַיָּם הִיא, אֶלָּא לוֹמַר לְךָ מַה יָּם טָהוֹר אַף אֳנִיָּה טְהוֹרָה:


והספינה – and even though it was made for reception and even though it is earthenware, it is pure. And in the Tractate Shabbat 9b, we derive it, as it is written (Proverbs 30:19): “[How an eagle makes its way over the sky; How a snake makes its way over a rock;] How a ship makes its way through the high seas; [How a man has his way with a maiden],” and it is obvious that a ship is on the high seas, but rather to inform you that just as the high seas are [ritually] pure, so also the ship is [ritually] pure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:3:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:3:16)


**כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תוֹךְ בִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס אֵין לוֹ אֲחוֹרָיִם.** חֲכָמִים גָּזְרוּ עַל מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין שֶׁיְּטַמְּאוּ כֵלִים, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִטְמְאוּ הַמַּשְׁקִין אֶלָּא מֵחֲמַת שֶׁרֶץ, דְּהַשְׁתָּא הֵן רִאשׁוֹן לַטֻּמְאָה, מְטַמְּאִים כֵּלִים מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים, וְאִם נָגְעוּ בַאֲחוֹרֵי הַכְּלִי נִטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרָיו וְלֹא נִטְמָא תוֹכוֹ. וְהַשְׁתָּא קָא מַשְׁמַע לָן דְּאֵין טֻמְאַת אֲחוֹרַיִם נוֹהֶגֶת אֶלָּא בִּכְלִי חֶרֶס שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תּוֹךְ. אֲבָל כָּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תּוֹךְ אֵין לוֹ טֻמְאַת אֲחוֹרַיִם, וְאִם נָגְעוּ מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִים מֵאֲחוֹרָיו לֹא נִטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרֵי הַכְּלִי:


כל שאין לו תוך בכלי חרס אין לו אחוריים – And the Sages decreed on [ritually] impure liquids that defile vessels, and even though the liquids were not defiled other than on account of an unclean reptile, for now they are first-degree of ritual impurity, they defile vessels/utensils from the words of the Scribes, and if they came in contact with/touched the back of the vessel, its outside is defiled, but the inside is not defiled. But now we hold that the defilement of the outside does not take effect other than with an earthenware vessel that has an inside. But all that lacks an inside, there is no defilement of the outside, שsand if impure liquids came in contact with it from the outside, they did not defile the outside of the vessel.



### Mishnah 4

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:1)


**פַּנָּס.** כְּמִין עֲשָׁשִׁית שֶׁל חֶרֶס עֲשׂוּיָה נְקָבִים בְּדָפְנוֹתֶיהָ שֶׁמֵּהֶן הָאוֹרָה יוֹצֵאת, וּמַנִּיחִים הַנֵּר בְּתוֹכָהּ שֶׁלֹּא יְכַבֶּנָּה הָרוּחַ:


פנס – a kind of earthenware lantern that is perforated in its walls/sides that from them the light goes out, and we place the candle inside it so that wind does not extinguish it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:2)


**שֶׁאֵין לוֹ.** בֵּית קִבּוּל שֶׁמֶן. אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל נֵר:


שאין בו – a receptacle for oil. Even though it has a receptacle for a candle.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:3)


**טָהוֹר.** שֶׁבֵּית קִבּוּל נֵר אֵין לוֹ תוֹךְ, אֶלָּא הַנֵּר מֻנָּח עָלָיו:


טהור – for a receptacle for a lantern has no inside other than the candle/lantern that is laid upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:4)


**מְגוּפַת הַיּוֹצְרִים.** כְּעֵין אָבְנַיִם שֶׁל חֶרֶס שֶׁהַיּוֹצְרִים עוֹשִׂים הַכֵּלִים עֲלֵיהֶן:


מגופת היוצרים (potter’s mould) – it is similar to stones of earthenware that the potters make the vessels upon them.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:5)


**אֶת שֶׁהוּא פוֹתֵחַ בָּהּ.** כְּלוֹמַר הַמְּגוּפָה שֶׁהַיּוֹצֵר מַשְׁלִיךְ עָלֶיהָ הַטִּיט וּמְפַתֵּחַ עָלֶיהָ בְּיָדָיו צוּרַת הַכְּלִי:


את שהוא פוחת בה (begins to shape the clay) – meaning to say, the mould that the potter casts upon it the plaster and engraves upon it with his hands the form of the vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:6)


**טְהוֹרָה.** לְפִי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ שָׂפָה סָבִיב וְאֵין כָּאן תּוֹךְ:


טהורה – because it lacks a rim/border around it and there is no inside here.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:4:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:7)


**וְשֶׁהוּא גוֹמֵר בָּהּ.** וְהַמְּגוּפָה שֶׁמַּעֲמִיד עָלֶיהָ הַכְּלִי לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּגְמְרָה צוּרָתוֹ יֵשׁ לוֹ תוֹךְ, וּלְכָךְ הִיא טְמֵאָה. וְרַבּוֹתַי פֵּרְשׁוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ כְּלִי לַיּוֹצְרִים שֶׁנִּקְרָא מְגוּפָה, וְיֵשׁ מֵהֶן שֶׁפִּתְחֵיהֶן צַר וְיֵשׁ שֶׁפִּתְחֵיהֶן רָחָב, אֶת שֶׁהוּא פּוֹתֵחַ בָּהּ, כְּלוֹמַר שֶׁעָתִיד לְהַרְחִיב פִּתְחָהּ, טְהוֹרָה, שֶׁעֲדַיִן לֹא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּה וְהַוְיָא כְגָלְמֵי כְלֵי חֶרֶס. וְשֶׁהוּא גּוֹמֵר בָּהּ, שֶׁמַּנִּיחָהּ כָּךְ בְּפֶתַח צַר, טְמֵאָה. וּמַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא דְּאָמַר כְּלֵי חֶרֶס מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁנִּגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּן. וְלֹא כְרַבָּנָן דְּאָמְרֵי מִשֶּׁיִּצָּרְפוּ בַכִּבְשָׁן. וּפֵרוּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן נִרְאֶה לִי עִקָּר:


ושהוא גומר בה – and the stopper that he places upon the vessel after its form has been completed has an “inside,” and therefore, it is impure. But my Rabbis/teachers explained, that that there is a vessel/utensil for potters that is called a מגופה/stopper or bung and some of them have narrow openings and some have wide openings; that which he opens it by, meaning to say, that he will eventually widen its opening, is pure, that its work has not yet been completed, and it is like the lump/shapeless earthenware vessel. But when he completes it, that he places as such at the narrow opening, it is impure. But our Mishnah is according to Rabbi Meir who stated (Tractate Betza 32a and Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma, Chapter 3, Halakha 13) : When do earthenware vessels become susceptible to receiving impurity? From the time when their manufacture is complete.” But not according to the Rabbis who state (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 4, Mishnah 4): “from when they are fired in the furnace.” And the first explanation appears to me to be essential.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:4:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:8)


**מַשְׁפֵּךְ.** כְּלִי שֶׁנּוֹתְנִין עַל פִּי חָבִית אוֹ עַל פִּי הַנּוֹד כְּשֶׁרוֹצִין לְמַלְּאוֹתוֹ יַיִן אוֹ שֶׁמֶן:


משפך – a vessel/utensil that we place on the mouth of a jug or on the mouth of a leather bottle/skin when we want to fill it with wine or oil.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:4:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:9)


**וְשֶׁל רוֹכְלִין.** שֶׁהוּא קָטָן וְעָשׂוּי לְהַכְנִיס שֶׁמֶן לְפַכִּין קְטַנִּים, וּמַחֲזִיק לֹג אוֹ שְׁנֵי לֻגִּים, וְהָרוֹכֵל מֵנִיחַ אֶצְבָּעוֹ מִתַּחְתָּיו כְּנֶגֶד הַנֶּקֶב וּמוֹדֵד בּוֹ שֶׁמֶן, וּמֵסִיר אֶצְבָּעוֹ וְהַשֶּׁמֶן יוֹרֵד לְכֵלָיו שֶׁל לוֹקֵחַ. וְעָשׂוּי לְקַבָּלָה הוּא וּמְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה:


ושל רוכלין – which is small and made to bring in oil to small flasks. And it holds a LOG or two LOGS and the peddler places his finger from underneath it corresponding to the hole/perforation and measures with it the oil, and removes his finger and the oil descends to the vessels of the purchaser. And it is made for reception and is susceptible to receive impurity.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:4:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:4:10)


**רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַטֵּהוּ עַל צִדּוֹ.** כְּלוֹמַר אֲפִלּוּ אֵינוֹ שֶׁל מִדָּה, מַשְׁפֵּךְ שֶׁל רוֹכְלִים לְעוֹלָם [מִטַּמֵּא], מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּטֵּהוּ עַל צִדּוֹ לְקַבֵּל בּוֹ מְעַט כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּרִיחַ בּוֹ הַלּוֹקֵחַ, וְנִמְצָא עָשׂוּי לְקַבָּלָה. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:


רבי עקיבא אומר מפני שמטהו על צדו – that is to say even if it is not of a measure, the funnel of a peddler always is defiled because he turns it on its side to receive in it a bit in order that the purchase can smell from it m and it is found that it is made to [be susceptible to] receive defilement. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Akiva.



### Mishnah 5

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:5:1)


**כִּסּוּי כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכוּ'.** וְכָל הַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ כִּסּוּי בִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס, טָהוֹר, דְּתוֹכוֹ כְּתִיב, וְהַאי לָאו תּוֹךְ דִּידֵיהּ הוּא:


כיסוי כדי יין וכו' – and all who use the covering with earthenware vessels, is pure, for it is written (Leviticus 11:33): “And anything on which one of them (i.e., an article of wood, or a cloth, or a skin or a sack) falls into/תוכו an earthenware vessel, everything inside it shall be unclean,” but this is not inside it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:5:2)


**וְכִסּוּי חָבִיּוֹת נְיָרִיּוֹת.** עַל שֵׁם מְקוֹמָן. וְלִרְבוּתָא נַקְטִינְהוּ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה לְכִסּוּי חָבִיּוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶן בֵּית קִבּוּל. וְאִית דְּגָרְסֵי וְהַנְּיָרוֹת, כְּלוֹמַר, הַנְּיָרוֹת שֶׁמְּכַסִּים בָּהֶן פִּי הַצְּלוֹחִית:


וכיסוי חביות נייריות (and covers of a papyrus jars) – for the sake of their place, and for something remarkable it was taken, because it was for a covering of their jars a receptacle, and there are those who have the reading "והניירות"/and for the papyrus, that is to say, the papyrus that they bring into them the mouth of the flask (i.e., bottle with a wide belly and a narrow neck).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:5:3)


**הַלְּפָס.** כְּמוֹ אִלְפָּס. מַחֲבַת גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁמְּבַשְּׁלִים בָּהּ בָּשָׂר וְיָרָק, וְעוֹשִׂים לָהּ כִּסּוּי שֶׁל חֶרֶס. וּכְשֶׁהוּא נָקוּב אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לִכְלוּם, וַאֲפִלּוּ אֵינוֹ נָקוּב וְיֵשׁ לוֹ חִדּוּד אֵין יָכוֹל לֵישֵׁב מִפְּנֵי הַחִדּוּד, אֲבָל כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקוּב וְאַף אֵין לוֹ חִדּוּד, טָמֵא, שֶׁרָאוּי לְהָפְכוֹ וּלְהוֹשִׁיבוֹ, וְאִשָּׁה נוֹתֶנֶת בְּתוֹכוֹ יָרָק לְסַנְּנוֹ לְהִמָּצוֹת מִמֶּנּוּ הַמַּיִם:


הלפס – like a tightly-covered stew-pot/אלפס. A large pan that they cook meat and vegetables in it. And they use it as a covering for earthenware. But when it is perforated, it is not appropriate for anything, and even when it is not perforated, but it (i.e., the lid) has a pointed knob (which prevents the use of it separately as a receptacle) it is not able to sit because of the pointed knob, but when it is not perforated, even if it doesn’t have a pointed knob, it is impure, for it is appropriate to turn it over and to cause it to stand, and a woman places into it vegetables to filter/drain it and to drain the water from it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:5:4)


**הָרוּנְקִי.** הַיְרָקוֹת לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלוּ וּדְבוּקִים זֶה בָזֶה וְנַעֲשִׂים גּוּף אֶחָד נִקְרָאִים רוּנְקִי. וְהִיא מִלָּה יְוָנִית:


הרונקי (contents of a pot upturned and emptied – on a flat vessel to cool off) – the vegetables after they have been cooked and attached to each other and they have become one body, are called רונקי, and it is a Greek word.



### Mishnah 6

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:6:1)


**גִּסְטְרָא.** שֶׁבֶר כְּלִי חֶרֶס. וְדָבָר שֶׁנֶּחְלָק לִשְׁנַיִם קָרוּי גִּסְטְרָא. וּלְשׁוֹן גִּסְטְרָא, גִּיסֵי תְרֵי:


גסטרא (a defective vessel – handles broken off or cracked) – fragments/broken earthenware vessels. And the thing divided into two, it is called גיסטרא /defective vessel (see Tractate Kelim, Chapter 4, Mishnah 3 for a definition: כל שנטלו אזניה/when its handles are split/broken off. And the language of גיסטרא is divided into two.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:6:2)


**שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת בַּכִּבְשָׁן.** וְלֹא יָדְעִינַן אִם נִשְׁבַּר קֹדֶם שֶׁנִּצְרַף בַּכִּבְשָׁן וּבְשָׁעָה שֶׁנִּגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ לֹא הָיָה תּוֹרַת כְּלִי עָלָיו וְתוּ לֹא מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם גִּסְטְרָא, אוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ נִשְׁבַּר וּמִטַּמֵּא. וְכֵיצַד מְבָרְרִים אֶת הַדָּבָר, רוֹאִין אִם הָיוּ שְׁבָרֶיהָ שָׁוִין וְתוֹכָהּ מַאֲדִים, בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁנִּגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִשְׁבְּרָה, וּמִטַּמְּאָה, דַּעֲבִיד לְקִבּוּל, שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ לָתֵת גִּסְטְרָא תַחַת הֶחָבִית לְקַבֵּל הַמַּשְׁקֶה הַנּוֹטֵף מִמֶּנָּה:


שנמצאת בכבשן – and we don’t know if it was broken prior to its being baked in the kiln/furnace and at the time when its manufacture was complete it did not have the status of a utensil/vessel upon it and not further on, it does defile because it is a defective vessel, or afterwards it was broken and defiles. But how do we verify the matter? We see if its shards are equivalent and its inside grows red, it is known that its manufacture was completed [first] and afterwards it became broken, and it defiles, for it was made to be a receptacle, for it is the manner to place a defective vessel underneath the jug/arched, pouched vessel to receive the liquid that drips from it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:6:3)


**טִיטְרוֹס.** כְּלִי שֶׁהוּא מְנֻקָּב מִלְּמַטָּה נְקָבִים הַרְבֵּה דַקִּים כִּמְלֹא נֶקֶב מַחַט וּמִלְּמַעְלָה נֶקֶב אֶחָד כִּמְלֹא כוּשׁ, דְּהַיְנוּ פֶלֶךְ שֶׁהַנָּשִׁים טֹווֹת בּוֹ, וּכְשֶׁמְּמַלְּאִים אוֹתוֹ מַיִם וְאָדָם מֵשִׂים אֶצְבָּעוֹ בַנֶּקֶב מִלְּמַעְלָה שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁלֹט בּוֹ הָרוּחַ אֵין טִפָּה אַחַת יוֹצֵאת מִן הַנְּקָבִים דַּקִּים שֶׁלְּמַטָּה, וּכְשֶׁמֵּסִיר אֶצְבָּעוֹ הַמַּיִם יוֹצְאִים:


טיטרוס (a perforated vessel, strainer, sprinkler) – a vessel which is perforated from below with many thin holes like the size of the hole of a needle and from above one hole like the size of a reed, that is a spindle that the women spin on, and when they fill it with water and a person places his finger in the hole from above so that the wind will not reach it no drop of water goes out from the small holes from below, but when he removes his finger, the water comes out.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:6:4)


**רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר צָדוֹק מְטַהֵר.** לְפִי שֶׁנָּקוּב בְּכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה:


ר' אלעזר בר צדוק מטהר – because it is perforated where the liquid enters.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:6:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:6:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:6:5)


**וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא.** שֶׁכָּךְ הוּא דֶרֶךְ תַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ, וַחֲשִׁיב בֵּית קִבּוּל הוֹאִיל וְהַמַּיִם עוֹמְדִים עַל יְדֵי הֲנָחַת אֶצְבַּע, וַאֲפִלּוּ בְלֹא הֲנָחַת אֶצְבַּע אֵין הַמַּיִם יוֹצְאִים אֶלָּא כְמוֹצִיא פְרוּטוֹת מְעַט מְעַט טִפָּה אַחַר טִפָּה, וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי לָא חֲשִׁיב נָקוּב כְּכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה לִטָּהֵר בְּכָךְ. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:


ורבי יוסי מטמא – for this is the manner of how it is used, and it is considered a receptacle since the waters stand through the placing of the finger, but even without the placing of the finger, the water doesn’t leave other than like removing coins little by little, drop after drop., and because of this, it is not considered perforated like when brings in liquid to be purified through this And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yossi.



### Mishnah 7

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:1)


**טַבְלָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ לִזְבֵּז וּמַחְתָּה שְׁלֵמָה.** שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ דְּפָנוֹת, טְמֵאִים, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן בֵּית קִבּוּל. וּמֵרֵישָׁא דְּהַטְּהוֹרִים שֶׁבִּכְלֵי חֶרֶס הָוֵי שָׁמְעִינַן דְּהָנָךְ טְמֵאִים, אֶלָּא אוֹרְחֵיהּ דְּתַנָּא הָכִי, כְּדִתְנַן בְּפֶרֶק וְאֵלּוּ טְרֵפוֹת [דַּף מג] וְאֵלּוּ כְשֵׁרוֹת, וְהָכִי אִיכָּא טוּבָא בַמִּשְׁנָה:


טבלא שיש לה לזבז ומחתה שלימה (a tray which has a rim and a complete firepan) – that it has sides/walls, they are impure, that they have a receptacle. But from the first clause [of the Mishnah] that the pure things are in an earthenware vessel, we would learn that these are impure, but it is the manner that they taught it as such, as is taught [in the Mishnah] in the Chapter “These are the Terefah [carcasses] among Cattle”/אלו טרפות (Chapter 3 in Tractate Hullin) [43a] and there are many in the Mishnah.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:2)


**טַבְלָה.** שֶׁל חֶרֶס:


טבלא – of earthenware.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:3)


**שֶׁהִיא מְלֵאָה קְעָרוֹת.** שֶׁהִיא עֲשׂוּיָה קְעָרוֹת קְעָרוֹת, וְהַקְּעָרוֹת הֵן מִגּוּפָהּ וּמְחֻבָּרִין בָּהּ:


מלאה קערות (which is full of plates) – that is made of plate after plate, and the plates/dishes are from its body and are attached to (i.e., the tray).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:4)


**וְאִם יֶשׁ לָהּ לִזְבֵּז עוֹדֵף.** אִם שְׂפַת הַטַּבְלָא סָבִיב עוֹדֵף וְעוֹלֶה לְמַעְלָה יוֹתֵר מִפִּיהֶן שֶׁל קְעָרוֹת:


ואם יש לה לזבז עודף (overhanging rim) – if the rim of the tray surrounding the overhang and rises up beyond the lip of the plates/dishes.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:7:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:5)


**נִטְמְאָה אַחַת מֵהֶן נִטְמְאוּ כֻלָּן.** דִּכְשֶׁנִּכְנָס הַשֶּׁרֶץ בְּפִי הַקְּעָרָה כְּבָר נִכְנַס בַּאֲוִיר הַלִּזְבֵּז הָעוֹדֵף סָבִיב, וְנִטְמֵאת כָּל הַטַּבְלָא, דִּכְלִי חֶרֶס מִטַּמֵּא מֵאֲוִירוֹ, וּכְשֶׁנִּטְמֵאת הַטַּבְלָא כֻלָּהּ נִטְמְאוּ כָל הַקְּעָרוֹת שֶׁהֵן מִגּוּפָהּ:


נטמאת אחת מהן נטמאו כולן – that when the unclean reptile/creeping thing enters into the lip of the dish, it has already entered the airspace of the overhanging rim all around, and all of the tray is defiled, for earthenware vessels are defiled from its airspace, and when the entire tray is defiled, all of the plates which are part of it are defiled.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:7:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:6)


**בֵּית הַתְּבָלִין.** כְּלִי חֶרֶס עָשׂוּי רִבּוּעִים רִבּוּעִים, לָתֵת בְּכָל רִבּוּעַ וְרִבּוּעַ מִין אֶחָד שֶׁל תְּבָלִין וְלֹא יִתְעָרְבוּ זֶה בָזֶה:


בית התבלין (spice pot) – earthenware vessel made squarely, to give in each square one species of spaces so that they will not become combined with each other.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:7:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:7)


**קַלְמָרִים הַמְתֹאָמוֹת.** כְּלִי עָשׂוּי לָתֵת בְּתוֹכוֹ הַדְּיוֹ וְהַקֻּלְמוֹס וְהַכֵּלִים הַצְּרִיכִים לַסּוֹפֵר. וְעָשׂוּי גַּם הוּא רִבּוּעִים רִבּוּעִים תְּאוֹמִים, וּבְאַרְצֵנוּ מֵהֶם הַרְבֵּה, וְקוֹרִים לָהֶם בְּלַעַ"ז קלמר"י:


קלמרים המתואמות (the double inkstand) – a vessel that is made to place in it the ink and the reed/writing utensil and the utensils that the scribe needs. And it is also made as a double square, and in our lands, there are many of them, and we call them KALMARI in the foreign tongue.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:7:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:8)


**בֵּית תְּבָלִין שֶׁל עֵץ.** שֶׁעָשׂוּי גַּם הוּא רִבּוּעִים רִבּוּעִים וְאֵין לוֹ לִזְבֵּז עוֹדֵף:


בית תבלין של עץ – that is also made squarely, but it does not have an overhanging rim.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:7:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:9)


**שֶׁנִּטְמָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּמַשְׁקֶה.** דְּרַבָּנָן גָּזְרוּ עַל הַמַּשְׁקִים הַבָּאִים מֵחֲמַת שֶׁרֶץ לְטַמֵּא כֵּלִים, גְּזֵרָה מִשּׁוּם מַשְׁקֶה זָב וְזָבָה, שֶׁהֵם מְטַמְּאִים כֵּלִים דְּאוֹרַיְתָא. וְדַוְקָא כְשֶׁנִּטְמָא בְמַשְׁקֶה לֹא נִטְמָא חֲבֵרוֹ, שֶׁכְּלִי שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרָיו בְּמַשְׁקִים לֹא נִטְמָא תוֹכוֹ, הִלְכָּךְ כְּשֶׁנִּטְמָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן בְּמַשְׁקִין הָוֵי דֹּפֶן שֶׁל הַטָּמֵא אֲחוֹרָיו שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ וְלֹא נִטְמָא חֲבֵרוֹ. אֲבָל בְּטֻמְאַת שֶׁרֶץ דְּאוֹרַיְתָא דְּכָל הֵיכָא דְּנָגַע בִּכְלִי עֵץ בֵּין מֵאֲחוֹרָיו בֵּין מִתּוֹכוֹ נִטְמָא כֻלּוֹ, אִם נִטְמָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן נִטְמָא חֲבֵרוֹ, שֶׁהַטֻּמְאָה נוֹגַעַת בּוֹ מֵאֲחוֹרָיו. וּבִכְלִי חֶרֶס דְּאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה מִגַּבּוֹ אֶלָּא מִתּוֹכוֹ, אֲפִלּוּ בְטֻמְאַת שֶׁרֶץ אִם נִטְמָא אֶחָד מֵהֶן לֹא נִטְמָא חֲבֵרוֹ, דְּתוֹכוֹ שֶׁל זֶה נַעֲשֶׂה גַב לַחֲבֵרוֹ, וּכְלִי חֶרֶס אֵין מִטַּמֵּא מִגַּבּוֹ. אֲבָל כְּלִי עֵץ מִטַּמֵּא מִגַּבּוֹ בְטֻמְאַת שֶׁרֶץ, אֲבָל לֹא בְטֻמְאַת מַשְׁקִין לִהְיוֹת נִטְמָא כֻלּוֹ:


שנטמא אחד מהן במשקה – for the Rabbis decreed on liquids that come on account of a creeping thing/unclean reptile to defile vessels as a decree because of the liquid of the man and/or woman with a flux, who defile vessels according to the Torah. And especially when it was defiled with liquids, its fellow is not defiled, for when a vessel that its outsides/backsides were defiled by liquids, its inside is not defiled, therefore when one of them with liquids, there is a wall/side of impurity on its backside of its neighbor but its neighbor is not defiled. But with the regarding the defilement of a creeping thing/unclean reptile according to the Torah, wherever it came in contact with/touched the vessel whether from its backside or whether from its inside, all of it is defiled, if one of them is defiled, its neighbor/fellow is defiled, for the defilement touches it from its outside/backside. But an earthenware vessel is not susceptible to receive defilement from its outside, but only from its inside, even with the defilement of a creeping thing/unclean reptile, if one of them was defiled, its neighbor is not defiled, for the inside of this one becomes the backside/outside of its neighbor for earthenware vessels are not defiled from its outside but not regarding the defilement of liquids that all of it is defiled.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:7:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:7:10)


**חוֹלְקִים אֶת עָבְיוֹ.** דֹּפֶן עָב וְרָחָב שֶׁבֵּין שְׁנֵי הָרִבּוּעִים, רָמִינַן פַּלְגָּא לְהַאי גִּיסָא וּפַלְגָּא לְהַאי גִּיסָא בְטֻמְאַת מַשְׁקִים דְּרַבָּנָן, וַחֲצִי עֳבִי הַדֹּפֶן שֶׁלַּצַּד הַטָּהוֹר טָהוֹר. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי:


חולקין את עוביו (they divide its thickness) – a thick and wide wall that is between two squares, we cast half to this side and half to that side with the defilement of liquids according to the Rabbis, but the half of the thickness of the wall that is from the side that is pure is pure. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri.



### Mishnah 8

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:8:1)


**הַלַּפִּיד.** כְּעֵין קְעָרָה שֶׁל חֶרֶס מְחֻדֶּדֶת מִלְּמַטָּה וְתוֹחֲבִים חִדּוּדָהּ בְּרֹאשׁ קוּנְדֵּס, וּבְתוֹךְ אוֹתָהּ קְעָרָה נוֹתְנִים חֲתִיכוֹת בֶּגֶד וְשֶׁמֶן וְעִטְרָן, וּמַדְלִיקִין וּמַגְבִּיהִין לְמַעְלָה וְהִיא מְאִירָה לְמֵרָחוֹק. וּמִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא מְחֻדֶּדֶת וְאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמֹד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אֲמֵינָא שֶׁלֹּא תִטַּמֵּא, קָא מַשְׁמַע לָן דְּהוֹאִיל וּמְקוֹם מוֹשָׁבָהּ מְתֻקָּן וּמְיֻחָד לְהוֹשִׁיבָהּ בְּרֹאשׁ הַקּוּנְדֵּס הֲרֵי זוֹ מִטַּמְּאָה:


הלפיד – it is similar to a dish of earthenware sharpened at the bottom and they insert pointed projections/prongs at the top of a pole and it enlightens from afar, but because it is sharpened/pointed and is not able to stand on its own, you might think I would say that it is not defiled. It comes to tell us that since it is a prepared and designated place for sitting to place at the top of the pole, this would be defiled.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:8:2)


**וּבֵית שִׁקְעוֹ שֶׁל נֵר.** כְּלִי חֶרֶס עָשׂוּי לִהְיוֹת הַנֵּר יוֹשֵׁב וּמְשֻׁקָּע בּוֹ:


ובית שקעו של נר (reservoir of the lamp) – an earthenware vessel made to be the torch is sitting and sunk within it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:8:3)


**מִטַּמֵּא בַאֲוִיר.** דַּחֲשִׁיב כְּתוֹךְ לִטַּמֵּא בַאֲוִיר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין כָּל הַנֵּר מְשֻׁקָּע בּוֹ כִּי אִם מְעַט מִמֶּנּוּ:


מטמא באויר – that it is considered like the inside to defile by airspace, even though the entire torch is not sunk within it other than only a small amount of it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 2:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/2:8:4)


**הַמַּסְרֵק שֶׁל צַרְצוּר.** כְּלִי חֶרֶס שֶׁעוֹשִׂים עַל פִּיו שְׂבָכָה כְּמִין מִכְבָּר מַעֲשֵׂה רֶשֶׁת וְהַמְעָרֶה מִמֶּנּוּ מֵטִיל הַמַּיִם מִמְּקוֹמוֹת הַרְבֵּה, וְרֹב הַכֵּלִים שֶׁשּׁוֹתִין בָּהֶם מַיִם בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׁמָעֵאל עֲשׂוּיִים כָּךְ, וּסְבִיב אוֹתָהּ שְׂבָכָה בּוֹלְטִים שִׁנַּיִם כְּשִׁנֵּי הַמַּסְרֵק, שֶׁעוֹשִׂים אוֹתָן לְנוֹי. וְאִם נִתְלָה שֶׁרֶץ בַּאֲוִיר אוֹתָן שִׁנַּיִם, פְּלִיגֵי בָהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבָּנָן אִי חֲשִׁיב תּוֹךְ כְּלִי חֶרֶס אִי לֹא. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים דְּחָשְׁבֵי לַהּ תוֹךְ וּמְטַמְּאִין:


מסרק של צרצור (comb of the water cooler – if an unclean object touches the comb of a cooler) – an earthenware vessel that they make at its mouth a net-work/mat like a kind of netting/lattice-work and one who empties from it pours the water from many places. But most of the vessels that they drink water from in the Islamic countries are made like this, and surrounding that net-work/mat protrudes teeth like the teeth of a comb, that they make them for beauty. And if an unclean creature/reptile was suspended in the airspace of those teeth, Rabbi Yossi and the Sages dispute if it is considered the inside of an earthenware vessel or not. But the Halakha is according to the Sages that they consider it as an inside [of the vessel] and that it defiles.



## Chapter 3


### Mishnah 1

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:1:1)


**שִׁעוּר כְּלִי חֶרֶס לִטַּהֵר.** דְּתוּ לֹא מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, וְאִם הָיָה טָמֵא טָהוֹר כְּאִלּוּ נִשְׁבַּר כֻּלּוֹ, דְּתוּ לֹא חֲזִי לְמִלְּתֵיהּ וְלֹא חֲשׁוּב תּוֹךְ דִּידֵיהּ. אֲפִלּוּ הָיְתָה חָבִית זוֹ מְיֻחֶדֶת לִגְרוֹגָרוֹת וְלֶאֱגוֹזִים, וְנִקְּבָה בְּמוֹצִיא זַיִת, טְהוֹרָה, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא חָזַר וְיִחֲדָהּ אַחַר כָּךְ לְקַבֵּל בָּהּ רִמּוֹנִים וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן, אֲבָל חָזַר וְיִחֲדָהּ לְקַבֵּל בָּהּ רִמּוֹנִים, טְמֵאָה עַד שֶׁתִּנָּקֵב בְּמוֹצִיא רִמּוֹן, וּמִשֶּׁנִּקְּבָה בְּמוֹצִיא רִמּוֹן שׁוּב אֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה:


שיעור כלי חרס ליטהר (the measure – of the perforation/hole in an earthenware vessel to render it clean) – that it further not be susceptible to receive defilement. And if it was impure, it was purified as if it was broken entirely, that further it is not appropriate/fit for its matter and its inside is not considered. Even if it was an arched, pouched vessel/jug for dried figs and/or nuts and it was perforated when removing olives, it is pure, all the while that he did not go back and designate it afterwards to receive in it pomegranates and things like them. But if he went back and designated it to receive in it pomegranates, it is impure until a perforation is made when removing a pomegranate, and from when it was perforated while removing a pomegranate, it no longer becomes susceptible to receiving [ritual] impurity.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:1:2)


**שִׁעוּרוֹ בְמַשְׁקִין.** בְּנֶקֶב שֶׁכְּשֶׁמְּשִׂימִין הַכְּלִי עַל גַּבֵּי מַשְׁקִין נִכְנָסִין הַמַּשְׁקִין דֶּרֶךְ אוֹתוֹ נֶקֶב לְתוֹךְ הַכְּלִי, וְהוּא נֶקֶב גָּדוֹל מִמּוֹצִיא מַשְׁקֶה:


שיעורו במשקין – the hole/perforation that when they place the vessel over the liquids, the liquids enter through that hole into the vessel, and it is a larger hole from that which releases liquids.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:1:3)


**לְכָךְ וּלְכָךְ.** כְּגוֹן קְדֵרָה שֶׁמְּבַשְּׁלִים בָּהּ בָּשָׂר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מַנִּיחִין בָּהּ אֹכֶל בְּלֹא מַשְׁקֶה, וּלְמַשְׁקֶה לֹא חַזְיָא שֶׁהֲרֵי נִקְּבָה בְּכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה, אֲפִלּוּ הָכִי אָזְלִינַן בָּהּ לְחֻמְרָא, וְאֵינָהּ טְהוֹרָה עַד שֶׁתִּנָּקֵב בְּמוֹצִיא זֵיתִים:


לכך ולכך – such as a pot that they cook meat in, even though they don’t place in it food without liquid, for the liquid is not recognized for it was perforated for the entrance of liquid, even so, we follow the stringent position, that it is not [ritually] pure until it will be perforated for the removal of olives.



### Mishnah 2

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:1)


**חָבִית שִׁעוּרָהּ בִּגְרוֹגָרוֹת.** רְגִילִים הָיוּ לְהָנִיחַ גְּרוֹגָרוֹת בֶּחָבִית:


חבית שיעורה בגרוגרות – it was the regular practice that they would place dried figs in a jar.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:2)


**רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר בְּזֵיתִים.** כִּסְתָם מַתְנִיתִין דִּלְעֵיל. וְהָוֵי סְתָם וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַחֲלֹקֶת וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כִּסְתָם. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:


רבי מאיר אומר בזיתים – like the anonymous Mishnah of above (i.e., Tractate Kelim, Chapter 3, Mishnah 1). And this is anonymous Mishnah followed by a dispute (i.e., between Rabbis Shimon, Yehuda and Meir) but the Halakha is not according to the anonymous [Mishnah]. But the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yehuda (i.e., the measurement is with nuts).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:3)


**הַלְּפָס וְהַקְּדֵרָה שִׁעוּרָן בְּזֵיתִים.** לְהַחְמִיר. כִּדְפָרֵישְׁנָא לְעֵיל:


הלפס והקדרה (the stew-pot/tightly covered pot and cooking pot) – to be stringent, as is explained above (see Mishnah 1 of this chapter).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:4)


**הַפַּךְ וְהַטְּפִי.** כְּלֵי שֶׁמֶן הֵן. אֶלָּא שֶׁהַטְּפִי פִּיו צַר מְאֹד, לְכָךְ נִקְרָא טְפִי שֶׁאֵין יוֹרֵד מִמֶּנּוּ אֶלָּא טִפִּין טִפִּין. וּטְפִי דִּתְנַן בְּפִרְקִין דִּלְעֵיל שֶׁהוּא טָהוֹר, הַיְנוּ כְּשֶׁהִתְקִינוֹ לְכַסּוֹת בּוֹ סַל שֶׁל עֲנָבִים כִּדְפָרֵישְׁנָא לְעֵיל:


הפך והטפי (oil cruise and the vessel with a narrow neck/dripper) – they are utensils for oil, but the mouth of the ewer/dripper is very narrow, for this [reason], it is called a טפי/dripper for it (i.e., the oil) only descends from it drop by drop and the טפי/dripper as it is taught in the Mishnah in the chapter above (see Tractate Kelim, Chapter 2, Mishnah 3) is [ritually] pure, that is, that they (i.e., the Sages), ordained to cover with it a basket of grapes as we explained above (see Tractate Kelim, Chapter 2, Mishnah 3).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:5)


**בְּשָׁמֶן.** הַיְנוּ כּוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן. וְאֵין שִׁעוּרוֹ שָׁוֶה לְמַיִם, דְּשֶׁל שֶׁמֶן דַּק, שֶׁהֲרֵי כְלִי שֶׁמַּחֲזִיק מַיִם אוֹ יַיִן אֵינוֹ מַחֲזִיק שֶׁמֶן:


בשמן – that is the would bring in the liquid of oil [of olives]. But its measurement is not equivalent to that of water, for that which is of oil is thin, for the vessel that holds water or wine does not hold oil.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:6)


**הַצַּרְצוּר.** כְּלִי עָשׂוּי לִשְׁתּוֹת בּוֹ מַיִם וְעַל פִּיו שְׂבָכָה כְּמַעֲשֵׂה רֶשֶׁת שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנֵס לְתוֹכוֹ דָבָר רַע וְיִטָּנְפוּ הַמַּשְׁקִין:


הצרצור (stone vessel containing a strainer and having an indented – comb-like- rim/a sort of cooler) – a vessel made to drink water from it and through its mouth, is a matting/net-work so that nothing bad can enter into it and soil the liquids.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:7)


**שְׁלָשְׁתָּן.** הַפַּךְ וְהַטְּפִי וְהַצַּרְצוּר, שִׁעוּרָן בְּנֶקֶב מוֹצִיא זֵרְעוֹנִים, כְּגוֹן הָאֲפוּנִים. דְּסָבַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דִּלְזֵרְעוֹנִים נַמִּי עֲבִידֵי, וַהֲווּ כְמוֹ הֶעָשׂוּי לְכָךְ וּלְכָךְ דִּלְעֵיל דִּמְטִילִין אוֹתוֹ לְחֻמְרוֹ. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:


שלשתן – the oil cruise and the dripper and the comb-like cooler, their measure is with a hole that lets out seeds, like beans. For Rabbi Shimon holds that they are also made for seeds, and they are like that which is made for this and that, like above (see Chapter 3, Mishnah 1), they subject it for the more stringent rule. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Shimon.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:2:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:8)


**נֵר שִׁעוּרוֹ בְשָׁמֶן.** בְּכוֹנֵס מַשְׁקֶה שֶׁל שֶׁמֶן. דִּסְתָם נֵר לְשֶׁמֶן עֲבִיד:


נר שיעורו בשמן – when one brings in liquid of [olive] oil. For a mere lamp is designed for oil.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:2:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:9)


**רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר בִּפְרוּטָה קְטַנָּה.** דְּסָבַר עֲבִיד נַמִּי לְאַנּוֹחֵי בֵיהּ פְּרוּטוֹת, וּמְטִילִין אוֹתוֹ לְחֻמְרוֹ. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:


רבי שמעון אומר בפרוטה קטנה – that he held that it was made to place in it פרוטות/drops (see Mishnah 6 of this chapter) and they pour it for its stringency. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Shimon.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:2:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:10)


**נֵר שֶׁנִּטַּל פִּיו.** בָּטַל שֵׁם נֵר מִמֶּנּוּ:


נר שנטל פיו – the designation of lamp is nullified.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:2:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:2:11)


**וְשֶׁל אֲדָמָה.** אֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִצְרַף בְּכִבְשָׁן. וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֻסַּק פִּי הַנֵּר בִּפְתִילָה הַדּוֹלֶקֶת, לָא חֲשִׁיב בְּכָךְ כְּאִלּוּ נִצְרַף בְּכִבְשָׁן, וְטָהוֹר:


ושל אדמה – it is not susceptible to receive defilement all the while that it is not smelt in a kiln. But even though that the nozzle of the lamp is burned by the wick, this is not considered as if it was smelt in a kiln, and it is pure.



### Mishnah 3

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:3:1)


**חָבִית שֶׁנִּקְּבָה.** בְּמוֹצִיא זַיִת, וְטָהֲרָה, כְּשֶׁחָזַר וַעֲשָׂאָהּ בְּזֶפֶת, מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא:


חבת שניקבה – when it releases olive [oil]. And it is pure, and when it was repaired with pitch, it becomes susceptible to receive defilement from here onwards.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:3:2)


**חָזְרָה וְנִשְׁבְּרָה.** לִשְׁבָרִים הַרְבֵּה. וְאוֹתוֹ הַשֶּׁבֶר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הַזֶּפֶת מַחֲזִיק רְבִיעִית וְיוֹשֵׁב שֶׁלֹּא מְסֻמָּךְ, טָמֵא. וּבְחָבִית הַמַּחְזֶקֶת מִלֹּג וְעַד סְאָה עָסְקִינַן, כְּדִתְנַן בְּפִרְקִין דִּלְעֵיל מִלֹּג וְעַד סְאָה בִּרְבִיעִית. וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין סְתִימָה מוֹעֶלֶת לְנֶקֶב הַבָּא לְאַחַר שְׁבִירָה, שָׁאנֵי הָךְ סְתִימָה, שֶׁנַּעֲשֵׂית קֹדֶם שֶׁבָּטַל שֵׁם כְּלִי מִמֶּנָּה. דְּחָבִית שֶׁנִּקְּבָה שֵׁם חָבִית עָלֶיהָ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁטָּהֲרָה, אֲבָל חֶרֶס הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִן הֶחָבִית בָּטַל שֵׁם כְּלִי מֵעָלָיו אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִקַּב, לְפִיכָךְ אֵין מוֹעֶלֶת סְתִימָה בַנֶּקֶב שֶׁלּוֹ:


חזרה ונשברה – into many pieces. That shard which has in it pitch holding one-quarter [of a LOG] and it sits without being supported/propped up is impure. But are dealing with a jar that holds from a LOG to a SEAH [the uncleanness will persist if the remnant will hold] a quarter of a LOG as is taught in the Mishnah in the previous Chapter (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 2, Mishnah 2). But even though the closing up (through repair with pitch) has no effect on the hole that comes after breakage, this closing up is different because it was done prior to having nullifying the designation of a vessel from it, for a jug that was perforated, its designation as a jug is upon it even though it is pure, but earthenware that departs from the jug, nullifies the designation of the name of a vessel from it even though it is not perforated. Therefore, closing up its hole has no benefit.



### Mishnah 4

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:1)


**חָבִית שֶׁנִּתְרוֹעֲעָה.** כְּמוֹ כֹתֶל רָעוּעַ. שֶׁלֹּא נָפְלוּ חֲרָסֶיהָ אֲבָל הִיא רְעוּעָה כָל כָּךְ שֶׁאִם יְטַלְטְלוּהָ וַחֲצִי קַב גְּרוֹגָרוֹת בְּתוֹכָהּ תִּשָּׁבֵר לְגַמְרֵי. וּטְהוֹרָה הִיא כִּדְאָמְרִינַן לְקַמָּן בְּאִידָךְ פִּרְקִין [מִשְׁנָה ב]:


חבית שנתרועעה – like a broken/shattered wall. That is earthenware did not fall out, but it is so cracked that if he carried it and one-half of a KAB of dried figs that are in it would break completely. And it is [ritually] pure as we state in the other (i.e., next) chapter (i.e., Tractate Kelim, Chapter 4) [Mishnah 2].


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:2)


**וּטְפָלָהּ.** שֶׁטַּח פָּנֶיהָ:


וטפלה (to paste/plaster) – that he plastered its facing.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:3)


**בִּגְלָלִים.** כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִפְּלוּ הַחֲרָסִים:


בגללים – in order that the potter’s clay would not fall off.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:4)


**נִשְׁבְּרָה.** שֶׁנָּפְלוּ הַחֲרָסִים וְדִבֵּק הַשְּׁבָרִים בְּקוֹלָן שֶׁל סוֹפְרִים, אוֹ שֶׁהֵבִיא חֲרָסִים מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר וְדִבְּקָן וְאַחַר כָּךְ טְפָלָן בִּגְלָלִים, טְהוֹרָה. וְהוּא הַדִּין טְפָלָן בְּטִיט, כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא חָזַר וּצְרָפָהּ בַּכִּבְשָׁן:


נשברה – that the earthenware fell off and he glued the shards with the glue that scribes use (to paste together strips of papyrus – see Tractate Pesahim, Chapter 3, Mishnah 1). Or that he brought potter’s clay from another place and glued them and afterwards plastered them over with dung, it is pure, and the same law applies when he plastered them with clay/mud, all the while that he did not go back and smelt it in a kiln.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:5)


**חֶרֶס מַחֲזִיק רְבִיעִית.** וּכְגוֹן שֶׁהַחֶרֶס בָּאָה מֵחָבִית הַמַּחְזֶקֶת מִלֹּג וְעַד סְאָה, דְּשִׁעוּרָהּ בִּרְבִיעִית כִּדְפָרֵישְׁנָא לְעֵיל:


חרס מחזיק רביעית – and such as that the earthenware comes from a jar [that is susceptible to become impure] that holds from a LOG until a SEAH, that its measurement is with a quarter-of-a-LOG as was explained above (see Tractate Kelim, Chapter 2, Mishnah 2).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:4:6)


**כֻּלָּן מִטַּמְּאִין בְּמַגָּע.** דְּכֻלָּן נַעֲשִׂים יָד לְאוֹתוֹ חֶרֶס, וּמִטַּמְּאִין מִשּׁוּם יָד. וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ בִּלְבַד מִטַּמֵּא בַּאֲוִיר, דְּאֵין אֲוִיר לְיַד כְּלֵי חֶרֶס:


כולן מטמאין במגע – and all of them are made into a handle for that potsherd and defile because of that handle. And [the part] opposite it only defiles through its airspace, for there is no airspace to the handle of an earthenware vessel.



### Mishnah 5

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:5:1)


**כְּלִי חֶרֶס הַבָּרִיא.** שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא רָעוּעַ וְלֹא שָׁבוּר:


כלי חרס הבריא – that is not shattered or broken.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:5:2)


**מְטַמְּאִין.** אִם נִטְמָא הַכְּלִי מֵאֲוִירוֹ, טְמֵאִים אֳכָלִים וּמַשְׁקִים שֶׁנָּגְעוּ בַטְּפֵלָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא חֲשׁוּבָה כַכְּלִי עַצְמוֹ:


מטמאין – if the vessel is defiled from its airspace, food and liquids that came in contact with its plaster are impure, because it is considered like the vessel itself (according to Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Meir).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:5:3)


**הַטּוֹפֵל אֶת הַבָּרִיא טָהוֹר.** דְּדַוְקָא הַכְּלִי רָעוּעַ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְאוֹתָהּ טְפֵלָה הוּא דַּחֲשִׁיבָה הַטְּפֵלָה כִכְלִי וְנִטְמְאוּ הָאֳכָלִים הַנּוֹגְעִים בָּהּ כְּשֶׁהַכְּלִי טָמֵא, אֲבָל טְפֵלַת הַבָּרִיא אֵינָהּ חֲשׁוּבָה כַכְּלִי. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


הטופל את הבריא טהור – that specifically the vessel that is shattered that needs that plastering, that one (i.e., the vessel) is where the plastering is like the vessel and the foods that came in contact with it are defiled when the vessel is impure. But the plastering of a healthy/whole vessel is not considered like a vessel. And the Halakha is according to the Rabbis.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:5:4)


**וְכֵן בְּחִדּוּק קֵרוּיָה.** כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן עִם חֲכָמִים בִּטְפֵלַת הַבָּרִיא כָּךְ נֶחְלְקוּ בְחִדּוּק קֵרוּיָה, וְהִיא דְּלַעַת יְבֵשָׁה וַחֲלוּלָה שֶׁשּׁוֹאֲבִין בָּהּ מַיִם, וּרְגִילִים לְהַדֵּק סְבִיבוֹתֶיהָ בְּעִגּוּל שֶׁל עֵץ אוֹ שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תִּשָּׁבֵר אִם תִּגֹּף בָּאֶבֶן. דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דִּמְטַמְּאִין בִּטְפֵלַת הַבָּרִיא מְטַמְּאִין אַף בְּזוֹ, וַאֲפִלּוּ הָיְתָה הַקֵּרוּיָה בְרִיאָה. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, אִם הָיְתָה הַקֵּרוּיָה בְרִיאָה וְאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה לְעֹגֶל זֶה לָא חֲשִׁיב הָעֹגֶל כְּגוּפָהּ שֶׁל קֵרוּיָה, וְאִם נִטְמֵאת הַקֵּרוּיָה לֹא נִטְמָא הָעֹגֶל:


וכן בחידוק קרויה (the lining of a pumpkin that has been hollowed out – to be used as a drawing vessel – i.e., the earthen vessel or clay that has been fitted as a protection) – just as Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon disputed with the Sages with the plastering of a whole vessel, so they disputed with regard to the lining of a pumpkin that has been hollowed out, and this is a dry and hollow gourd that they draw water with, and they regularly fasten around it in a circle of wood or of iron in order that it would not break if it is corked with a stone. For Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon who make unclean the plastering of a whole [earthenware vessel] (i.e., unbroken or unshattered) also make unclean even this, and even if it was a pure pumpkin-shell used as a drawing vessel. But the Sages state that if it was a pure pumpkin-shell used as a drawing vessel and it doesn’t have a need for this hoop, this hoop is not like the body of the pure pumpkin-shell used as a drawing vessel, and if the pure pumpkin-shell became defiled, the hoop did not become defiled.



### Mishnah 6

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:6:1)


**יַבְּלִית.** מִין עֵשֶׂב שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ יַבְּלָא. וּרְגִילִין לָטוּחַ בּוֹ הַכַּדּוֹת הַגְּדוֹלוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יִפְלְטוּ הַיַּיִן שֶׁמְּזִיעִין:


יבלית (a pulp made of Cynodon leaves and used for lining large water vessels) – a kind/species of grass that its name is יבלא/a species of grass (Cynodon. And they regularly plaster with it the large jugs so that the wine will not escape when it drips.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:6:2)


**פִּטָּסִין.** כַּדּוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת. כְּמוֹ הַלָּלוּ בַּעֲלֵי פִטָּסִין דִּבְמַסֶּכֶת בֵּיצָה [דַּף טו:]:


פטסין (large cylindrical vessel, cash or tub of earthen material) – large jugs, like those (the first to leave the lecture room) who are owners of tubs of wine that is in Tractate Betzah 15b.



### Mishnah 7

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:1)


**מֵחַם.** כְּלִי שֶׁמְּחַמְּמִים בּוֹ הַמַּיִם:


מיחם – a vessel that they heat water in (i.e., a boiler).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:2)


**בְּחֹמֶר.** טִיט עָב:


בחומר- thick plaster.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:3)


**חַרְסִית.** דַּק כְּחֶרֶס. וְיֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים, כְּתִישַׁת חֲרָסִים:


חרסית (potter’s clay) – thin like earthenware. But there are those who explain/interpret it as crushing/pounding of earthenware.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:4)


**הַנּוֹגֵעַ בַּחֹמֶר טָמֵא.** לְפִי שֶׁהוּא נִדְבָּק וּמִתְחַבֵּר בַּמֵּחַם וַחֲשׁוּב כְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁל כְּלִי, הִלְכָּךְ אִם נִטְמָא הַמֵּחַם נִטְמָא הַחֹמֶר שֶׁסְּבִיבוֹ כְּמוֹתוֹ, וְהָאֳכָלִים הַנּוֹגְעִים בַּחֹמֶר טְמֵאִים:


הנוגע בחומר טמא – because it Is joined and attached to the kettle and is considered like the essence of the vessel. Therefore, if the boiler is defiled, the thick plaster surrounding it is defiled like it, and those eating who touch the thick plaster are impure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:7:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:5)


**וּבַחַרְסִית טָהוֹר.** דְּחַרְסִית אֵינוֹ נִדְבָּק וּמִפְרִיךְ וְנָפִיל, וְלָא חֲשִׁיב כְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁל כְּלִי:


ובחרסית טהור – for the potter’s clay is not joined but is scraped/peeled and falls off, and is not considered like the essence of the vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:7:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:6)


**קוּמְקוּם.** יוֹתֵר גָּדוֹל מִמֵּחַם. וּבְלַעַ"ז קוֹרְאִין לוֹ קומקומ"ו:


קומקום (kettle) – it is larger than a boiler, and in the foreign language, they call it a KUMKUMO.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:7:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:7)


**שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל אֶת הַחַמִּין.** שֶׁהַזֶּפֶת נִתָּךְ וְנָמֵס בְּמַיִם חַמִּין. וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְקַבֵּל אֶת הַצּוֹנֵן אֵינוֹ חֲשׁוּב כְּלִי וְטָהוֹר:


שאינו יכול לקבל את החמין – for the pitch is smelted and melts/dissolves in hot water, and even though it is able to hold the cold water, it is not considered as a vessel and is pure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:7:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:8)


**וְכֵן הָיָה אוֹמֵר בִּכְלֵי זֶפֶת.** כֵּלִים הָעֲשׂוּיִין מִן הַזֶּפֶת עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁהֵן טְהוֹרִין, הוֹאִיל וְאֵין יְכוֹלִין לְקַבֵּל אֶת הַחַמִּין כַּצּוֹנֵן. וְרַבּוֹתַי פֵּרְשׁוּ בִּכְלֵי זֶפֶת, בְּכֵלִים הַזְּפוּתִים, וּמְפָרֵשׁ וְאָזֵיל כֵּיצַד, כְּלֵי נְחֹשֶׁת שֶׁזְּפָתָן טְהוֹרִים. אִם הָיוּ הַכֵּלִים טְמֵאִים וְנָגַע אָדָם אוֹ אֳכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין בַּזֶּפֶת, טְהוֹרִים, דְּאֵין הַזֶּפֶת חִבּוּר וְאֵינוֹ נֶחְשָׁב כְּעַצְמוֹ שֶׁל כְּלִי:


וכן היה אומר בכלי זפת – vessels that are made from pitch itself, which are pure, since they are not able to hold the hot like they can the cold. But my Rabbis explained, regarding vessels lined with pitch, in pitch vessels of pitch, and it explains further on [in this Mishnah], how so? Vessels of copper that were lined with pitch are pure. If the vessels were impure and a person or foods or liquids touched/came in contact with pitch, they are pure, for the pitch does not combine and is not considered like the essence of the vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:7:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:9)


**וְאִם לְיַיִן.** וְאִם זְפָתָן מִתְּחִלָּה לָשׂוּם בְּתוֹכָן יַיִן וְאֵין דַּעְתּוֹ לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן בְּחַמִּין כְּלָל:


ואם ליין – if he lined them with pitch from the outset to place in them wine and it was not his intention to use them for hot liquids at all.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:7:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:7:10)


**טְמֵאִין.** דְּאָז הָוֵי הַכְּלִי צָרִיךְ לַזֶּפֶת וְהָוֵי זֶפֶת חִבּוּר:


טמאין – for the vessel requires pitch and the pitch is attached/joined.



### Mishnah 8

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:1)


**יוֹתֵר מִצָּרְכָּהּ.** כְּנֶגֶד הַנֶּקֶב הוּא צָרְכָּהּ, וּמַה שֶּׁהוּא שֶׁלֹּא כְּנֶגֶד הַנֶּקֶב הָוֵי יוֹתֵר מִצָּרְכָּהּ, וְלָא חֲשִׁיב חִבּוּר, כֵּיוָן דְּלֹא צָרִיךְ לֶחָבִית. וְרַמְבַּ"ם פֵּרֵשׁ, יוֹתֵר מִצָּרְכָּהּ כְּגוֹן שֶׁעָשָׂה הַסְּתִימָה עָבָה בְיוֹתֵר עַד שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִנָּטֵל מִמֶּנָּה וְתִשָּׁאֵר סְתוּמָה, וַאֲפִלּוּ הַכֹּל כְּנֶגֶד הַנֶּקֶב:


יותר מצרכה – corresponding to the hole/perforation it needs it, and what is not corresponding to the hole/perforation is more than its needs, and it is not considered an attachment/joining, since it is not needed for the jar. But Maimonides explained that more that is its need as for example that he made the closure most thick until one would be able to remove from it and it would remain closed, and even if everything is corresponding to the hole/perforation.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:2)


**זֶפֶת שֶׁנָּטְפָה עַל הֶחָבִית.** שֶׁאֵינָהּ נְקוּבָה:


זפת שנטפה על החבית (pitch which dripped on the jar) – that is not perforated.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:3)


**הַנּוֹגֵעַ בָּהּ.** בְּטִפַּת הַזֶּפֶת:


הנוגע בה – with the drop of pitch.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:4)


**טָהוֹר.** אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֶחָבִית טְמֵאָה. שֶׁאֵין הַזֶּפֶת חִבּוּר לֶחָבִית כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין הֶחָבִית צְרִיכָה לָהּ:


טהור – even though the jar is impure. For the pitch is not in a connection/attachment to the jar, since the jar does not require it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:8:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:5)


**שֶׁפְּקָקוֹ בְזֶפֶת.** שֶׁסָּתַם פִּי הַנֶּקֶב שֶׁל הַמַּשְׁפֵּךְ הֶעָשׂוּי לְהַכְנִיס מִמֶּנּוּ יַיִן לֶחָבִית:


שפקקן בזפת – he closed up the mouth of the hole/perforation of the funnel that is made to bring wine from it into the jar.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:8:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:6)


**רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה מְטַמֵּא.** דַּחֲשִׁיב לֵיהּ סְתִימָה, בֵּין בְּשֶׁל עֵץ בֵּין בְּשֶׁל חֶרֶס:


רבי אלעזר בן עזריה מטמא – because it (i.e., the pitch) is considered for it as a closure, whether of wood or whether of earthenware.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:8:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:7)


**וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא בְשֶׁל עֵץ.** מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַזֶּפֶת הוּא מִינוֹ, שֶׁהַזֶּפֶת יוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵץ:


ר"ע מטמא בשל עץ – because the pitch is of its [same] species/kind, for the pitch comes out from the tree.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:8:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:8)


**וּמְטַהֵר בְּשֶׁל חָרֶס.** שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ וְלָא חֲשִׁיב חִבּוּר. וְלֹא דָּמֵי סְתִימַת פִּי הַמַּשְׁפֵּךְ לִסְתִימַת נֶקֶב הֶחָבִית דַּחֲשִׁיב חִבּוּר, לְפִי שֶׁהַנֶּקֶב שֶׁבְּפִי הַמַּשְׁפֵּךְ שֶׁעֲשָׂאוֹ הַיּוֹצֵר מִתְּחִלָּה חָלָק הוּא וְנִקְלָף הַזֶּפֶת מִמֶּנּוּ וְאֵינוֹ מִתְקַיֵּם, אֲבָל חָבִית שֶׁנִּקְּבָה לְאַחַר שֶׁהֻסְּקָה בַכִּבְשָׁן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַנֶּקֶב לִהְיוֹת חָלָק וְשָׁוֶה וְאֵין הַזֶּפֶת נִקְלָף מִמֶּנּוּ, אִי נַמִּי, נֶקֶב שֶׁבְּפִי הַמַּשְׁפֵּךְ סוֹפוֹ לְהָסִיר סְתִימָתוֹ כְשֶׁיִּרְצֶה לִשְׁפֹּךְ יַיִן בֶּחָבִית, הִלְכָּךְ לָא חֲשִׁיבָא סְתִימָה אֶלָּא בְמַשְׁפֵּךְ שֶׁל עֵץ לְפִי שֶׁהוּא מִינוֹ, אֲבָל חָבִית שֶׁנִּקְּבָהּ אֵין סוֹפוֹ לְהָסִיר הַסְּתִימָה:


ומטהר בשל חרס – which is not its kind/species and is not considered an attachment. And the closing of the mouth of a funnel is not similar to the closing of the perforation of a jug which is considered an attachment, because the perforation in the mouth of the funnel that was made by the artisan from the outset was smooth and the pitch was peeled from it and does not endure, but the jug that was perforated after it was heated in a kiln, it is impossible to perforate to be smooth and even, and the pitch is not peeled from it, or alternatively, the perforation that is at the mouth of the funnel, its function is to remove its covering/closure when he wants to pour wine from the jug. Therefore, it is not considered a closing other than with a wooden funnel because it is its kind/species, but a jug that is perforated, its function is not to remove the closure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 3:8:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/3:8:9)


**רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַהֵר בִּשְׁנֵיהֶם.** דִּסְתִימַת פִּי הַמַּשְׁפֵּךְ לָא חֲשִׁיבָא סְתִימָה, וַהֲרֵי הוּא כְאִלּוּ לֹא נִסְתַּם וְאֵין לוֹ בֵּית קִבּוּל. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:


רבי יוסי מטהר בשניהם – for the closing of the mouth of the funnel is not considered a closure, and it is as if it was not closed and lacks a receptacle. But the Halakha is according to Rabbi Akiva.



## Chapter 4


### Mishnah 1

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 4:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/4:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/4:1:1)
