And they are pure when they are on their own, for they are the decorations of the animal, and the decorations of the animal are not susceptible to receive defilement.



### Mishnah 6

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:1)


**פִּיקָה.** כְּמִין כַּדּוּר קָטָן נָקוּב בָּאֶמְצַע שֶׁמְּשִׂימוֹת הַנָּשִׁים בְּרֹאשׁ הַפֶּלֶךְ שֶׁטֹּווֹת בּוֹ כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּכְבַּד:


פיקה (whorl/spindle knob) – like a small ball that is perforated in the middle that women place at the top of the spindle when they spin with it in order that it becomes heavy.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:2)


**רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא.** דִּכְלִי מַתָּכוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שֵׁם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ הוּא, וְטָמֵא, כְּדִתְנַן בְּרֵישׁ פִּרְקִין:


רבי עקיבא מטמא – for it is a metal vessel that has a designation/name of its own, and it is ritually impure, as it is taught in the Mishnah at the beginning of the chapter (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 11, Mishnah 2).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:3)


**וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.** דְּאֵין לוֹ שֵׁם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ אֶלָּא שֵׁם לְוַי, פִּיקָא שֶׁל כּוּשׁ, אוֹ פִּיקָה שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ דָבָר שֶׁהִיא מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת לוֹ. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


וחכמים מטהרין – that it doesn’t have a designation/name of its own but rather an epithet, a spindle knob of reed used as a spindle, or a spindle knob of a that same thing that it uses. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:4)


**וּמְצֻפָּה.** אִם הִיא שֶׁל עֵץ וּמְצֻפָּה בְמַתֶּכֶת טָמֵא:


ומצפה (and if it is overlaid) – if it was of wood and it is overlaid with metal, it is ritually impure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:5)


**טְהוֹרָה.** דְּבָתַר עִקָּרָא אָזְלִינַן, וְלֹא בָתַר הַצִּפּוּי שֶׁהוּא שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת טָמֵא:


טהורה – that after the essence we follow, but not after the covering/overlaying which is of metal which is ritually impure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:6)


**כּוּשׁ.** פֶּלֶךְ שֶׁהַנָּשִׁים טֹווֹת בּוֹ:


כוש – a spindle that the women spin on.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:7)


**וְהַמַּקֵּל.** שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת טָמֵא. הוֹאִיל וְאָדָם רוֹדֶה בוֹ אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה, כִּכְלִי עָשׂוּי לְתַשְׁמִישׁ אָדָם הוּא חָשׁוּב:


והמקל (and the staff) – of metal which is rituall impure, for since a person chastises the animal with it, it is considered like a vessel that is made for the use by a person.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:8)


**סִמְפּוֹנְיָא.** מִין כְּלִי זֶמֶר הוּא, כְּדִכְתִיב בְּדָנִיֵּאל (פרק ג) פְּסַנְתְּרִין וְסִמְפּוֹנְיָא:


סמפוניא (a wind instrument) – a kind of musical instrument, as it is written in Daniel (3:5): "פסנתרין סומפניה [וכל הני זמרא]"/”psaltery, bagpipe, [and all other types of instruments].”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:9)


**וְחָלִיל.** אַף הוּא מִין שֶׁל כְּלִי זֶמֶר, וְחָלוּל הוּא וְקוֹלוֹ נִשְׁמָע עַד לְמֵרָחוֹק:


וחליל – even it is a kind of musical instrument, and it is hollowed out and its sound is heard from a [great] distance.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:10)


**וּמְצֻפִּין טְהוֹרִים.** אִם [הוּא] שֶׁל עֵץ וּמְצֻפֶּה נְחֹשֶׁת טָמֵא, טָהוֹר הוּא. דְּבָתַר עִקַּר הַכְּלִי אָזְלִינַן שֶׁהוּא שֶׁל עֵץ, וְלָא חֲשִׁיב יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא חָלוּל, כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי לְבֵית קִבּוּל:


ומצופין אהורים – if it is of wood and is overlaid with ritually impure copper, it is [considered] ritually pure. For we follow after the essence of the vessel which is of wood. And if it has a receptacle, it is not considered, even though it is hollow, since it is not made for the receptacle. ‘


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:11)


**אִם יֶשׁ לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל כְּנָפַיִם.** כֵּלִים דַּקִּים קְטַנִּים כִּדְמוּת כְּנָפַיִם נוֹתְנִים בְּתוֹךְ הַסִּמְפּוֹנְיָא. שֶׁמְּסַיְּעִים לְהַשְׁמָעַת קוֹל הַנִּגּוּן. וְאִם עָשׂוּ בְתוֹכָהּ מָקוֹם לְבֵית קִבּוּל שֶׁל כְּנָפַיִם הַלָּלוּ, חֲשִׁיב בֵּית קִבּוּל:


אם יש לה בית קיבול כפנים (if it has a receptacle for the wings [= bags of the bagpipe]) – small thin vessels in the image of wings, which we put into the wind instrument (i.e., bagpipe), that assist in projecting the sound of the music, if they made it within the place of the receptacle of these wings (i.e., the bags of the bagpipe), it is considered a receptacle.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:6:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:6:12)


**בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ.** בֵּין שֶׁהִיא מְצֻפָּה וּבֵין שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְצֻפָּה, טְמֵאָה:


ובין כך ובין כך – whether it is overlaid or whether it is not overlaid, it is ritually impure.



### Mishnah 7

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:1)


**קֶרֶן עֲגֻלָּה וְקֶרֶן פְּשׁוּטָה.** חֲצוֹצְרוֹת מִקַּרְנֵי הַבְּהֵמוֹת עֲשׂוּיוֹת פְּרָקִים פְּרָקִים מְחֻבָּרִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁאַחַת מֵהֶן צוּרָתָהּ עֲגֻלָּה וְאַחֶרֶת פְּשׁוּטָה. וְחִבּוּר הַפְּרָקִים שֶׁל עֲגֻלָּה קָשִׁים וּצְרִיכִים אֻמָּן יוֹתֵר מֵחִבּוּר הַפְּרָקִים שֶׁל פְּשׁוּטָה, וּמִפְּנֵי זֶה אָמְרוּ הַמַּחֲזִיר קֶרֶן עֲגֻלָּה בְשַׁבָּת חַיָּב חַטָּאת, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּפְשׁוּטָה:


קרן עגולה וקרן פשוטה (a round metal horn and a plain, straight horn) – a trumpet from the horns of cattle that are made attached section by section, but rather that one of them is made round and the other is [made] straight. But the connection of the sections of the round metal horns is hard and requires an artisan more than the connection of the sections of the plain, straight horn, and because of this, they (i.e., the Sages) said that a person who returns a round metal horn on the Sabbath is liable for sin-offering, which is not the case with a plain, straight horn.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:2)


**קֶרֶן עֲגֻלָּה טְמֵאָה.** שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל. וְקֶרֶן פְּשׁוּטָה טְהוֹרָה, שֶׁאֵין לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל. וְקַרְנַיִם דִּין כְּלֵי עֶצֶם יֵשׁ לָהֶן, שֶׁפְּשׁוּטֵיהֶן טְהוֹרִים כִּפְשׁוּטֵי כְלֵי עֵץ:


קרן עגולה טמאה – that it has a receptacle. But the plain, straight horn is ritually pure, for it lacks a receptacle. And the horns have the law of the boney utensils, for their flat, level surfaces are ritually pure like flat wooden implements.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:3)


**מְצֻפִּית.** מְקוֹם הַנָּחַת הַפֶּה, וְהוּא הַקָּצָר שֶׁבָּהּ. מִלְּשׁוֹן עוֹמְדִים צְפוּפִים:


מצופות (overlaid mouthpiece of a musical instrument) – the place where the mouth is placed, and it is the narrow part of it. It is from the language of "עומדים צפופים" /standing crowded together (see Tractate Avot, Chapter 5, Mishnah 5).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:4)


**טְמֵאָה.** דְּחָשְׁבִינַן לָהּ כִּכְלֵי מַתָּכוֹת, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא פְּשׁוּטָה מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה:


טמאה – for we consider it as a metal vessel, and even though it is plain/straight, it is susceptible to receiving ritual impurity.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:7:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:5)


**הַקַּו שֶׁלָּהּ.** הַצַּד הָרָחָב שֶׁבָּהּ, אִם הָיָה שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת:


הקב שלה (the cavity, the lower part of the trumpet/horn) – the wide side that is on it, if it is made of metal.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:7:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:6)


**רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן מְטַמֵּא וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִים.** וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


ר' טרפון מטמא וחכים מטהרים – But the Halakha is according to the Sages.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:7:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:7)


**קְנֵי מְנוֹרָה טְהוֹרִים.** שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שֵׁם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן, וּתְנַן לְעֵיל בְּרֵישׁ פִּרְקִין כָּל כְּלִי מַתָּכוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שֵׁם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, טָמֵא:


קני מנורה טהורים – that they lack a name a name of their own, and it is taught in the Mishnah at the beginning of this chapter (see Tractate Kelim, Chapter 11, Mishnah 2), that metal vessels that have a name of its own is ritually impure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:7:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:8)


**הַפֶּרַח.** מְקוֹם מוֹשַׁב הַנֵּר שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הַמְּנוֹרָה פֶּרַח שְׁמוֹ:


הפרח – the place where the candle sits that is at the top of the candelabrum, is called by the name of פרח/calyx (an ornament in the shape of a flower).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:7:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:7:9)


**בָּסִיס.** רַגְלֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא יוֹשֶׁבֶת עֲלֵיהֶן:


בסיס – the feet of the candelabrum/Menorah that it sits on them (i.e., the base).



### Mishnah 8

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:1)


**קַסְדָּא.** כּוֹבַע נְחֹשֶׁת שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים אַנְשֵׁי הַמִּלְחָמָה עַל רֹאשָׁן:


קסדא – the bronze hat that the men of war place on their heads.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:2)


**וּלְחָיַיִם.** טַסִּין שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים עַל לְחָיֵיהֶן:


ולחיים – tin foil or other plating material of bronze that they place on their cheeks.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:3)


**אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶן בֵּית קִבּוּל מַיִם.** שֶׁשּׁוֹתִין בָּהֶם מַיִם בַּמִּלְחָמָה:


ואם יש בהן בית קיבול מים – that they drink water in them during war.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:4)


**כִּידוֹן.** רֹמַח קָטָן שֶׁבְּיַד הַשָּׂרִים וְהַמְּלָכִים:


כידון (light spear/javelin) – a small spear that is in the hands of the officers and the kings.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:5)


**נִיקוֹן.** כְּמוֹ קִינוֹן. לְשׁוֹן וּמִשְׁקַל קֵינוֹ (שמואל ב כא). וְהוּא הַבַּרְזֶל שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הָרֹמַח:


ניקון (iron point of a javelin) – like a canon. It is the language of (II Samuel 21:16): “[And Ishbi-benob tried to kill David – He was a descendant of the Rapha (a race of ghosts)]; his bronze spear [weighed three hundred shekels and he wore new armor].” And it is the bronze that is within the spear.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:6)


**מַגָּפַיִם.** בָּתֵּי שׁוֹקַיִם שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל שֶׁנּוֹשְׂאִין אַנְשֵׁי הַמִּלְחָמָה:


מגפיים (metal leggings, greaves) – bronze upper part of the leg that men of war carry [into battle].


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:7)


**תַּכְשִׁיטֵי נָשִׁים.** אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עֲשׂוּיִין לִמְלָאכָה אֶלָּא לְנוֹי, מְרַבִּינַן לְהוּ מִקְּרָא דִכְתִיב (במדבר לא) וְכָל אֲשֶׁר לֹא יָבֹא בָּאֵשׁ תַּעֲבִירוּ בַמָּיִם:


תכשיטי נשים – even though they are not made for work but rather for beauty/ornamentation, we derive from Scripture as it is written (Numbers 31:23): “and anything that cannot withstand fire you must pass through water.”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:8)


**עִיר שֶׁל זָהָב.** כְּמִין עֲטָרָה נוֹתְנוֹת הַנָּשִׁים בְּרֹאשָׁן עֲשׂוּיָה כְצוּרַת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם:


עיר של זהב – like a diadem/tiara that women place on their heads in the shape of Jerusalem.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:9)


**קַטְלָיוֹת.** חוּטִים שֶׁל זָהָב שֶׁנּוֹתְנוֹת סְבִיב הַצַּוָּאר. וּמִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה חוֹנֶקֶת עַצְמָהּ בָּהֶן כְּדֵי שֶׁתֵּרָאֶה בַּעֲלַת בָּשָׂר, לְכָךְ נִקְרָאִים קַטְלָיוֹת:


קטליות (necklace – a chain the links of which are of metal and strung on a linen or woolen thread) – golden threads that they (i.e., the women) place around the neck. But because the woman chokes herself with them in order that she should appear with much flesh, therefore, we call them קטליות (that act as something that kills).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:10)


**וּנְזָמִים.** יֵשׁ מֵהֶן נִזְמֵי הָאַף וְיֵשׁ מֵהֶן נִזְמֵי הָאֹזֶן:


ונזמים – there are those of them that are nose rings and there are those of them that are earrings.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:11)


**בְּחוּט שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן.** שֶׁהָיוּ הַחֻלְיוֹת נְקוּבוֹת וּמִלְּאוּ מֵהֶן הַחוּט:


בחוט של פשתן – that the links of which are perforated and they filled from them the thread.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:12)


**הַחֻלְיוֹת טְמֵאוֹת.** דְּכָל חֲדָא בְאַנְפֵּי נַפְשָׁא חֲשִׁיבָא כְלִי מַעֲשֶׂה:


החוליות טמאות – each one of them is considered on its own as a working vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:13)


**שֶׁל אֲבָנִים.** שֶׁהָיוּ מַרְגָּלִיּוֹת וַאֲבָנִים נְקוּבוֹת וּמִלְּאוּ מֵהֶן הַחוּט:


של אבנים – that there were jewels/pearls and stones perforated and they filed from them the thread.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:14)


**טָמֵא.** הַחוּט, הוֹאִיל וְשֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת הוּא:


טמא – the thread, since it is of metal.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:8:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:8:15)


**כִּמְלֹא צַוַּאר קְטַנָּה.** כִּמְלֹא צַוָּאר שֶׁל בַּת קְטַנָּה:


כמלוא צואר קטנה – encompass the neck of a small girl.



### Mishnah 9

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:1)


**כִּקְדֵרָה מִלְּמַטָּה.** רָחָב מִלְּמַטָּה וְיֵשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל:


כקדרה מלמטה (like a pot-shape from the bottom) – wide from below and it has a receptacle.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:2)


**וְכָעֲדָשָׁה מִלְמַעְלָה.** עַל רֹאשׁ הַנֶּזֶם מִלְּמַעְלָה יֵשׁ לוֹ גַרְעִין שֶׁל זָהָב אוֹ שֶׁל כֶּסֶף עָשׂוּי כָּעֲדָשָׁה:


וכעדשה מלמעלה – on the top of the earring from the above, it has a globule/kernel of gold or of silver made like a lentil.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:3)


**וְנִפְרַק.** הָעֲדָשָׁה מִן הַקְּדֵרָה:


ונפרק (dislocated) – the lentil from the pot.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:4)


**הַקְּדֵרָה טְמֵאָה.** שֶׁהֲרֵי יֵשׁ לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל. וְלֹא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא מִתַּכְשִׁיטֵי נָשִׁים, שֶׁהֲרֵי אֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לְתַכְשִׁיט כְּמוֹת שֶׁהִיא:


הקדירה טמאה – for it has a receptacle. But not because it is women’s ornaments, for it is not worthy of being an ornament as it is.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:9:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:5)


**וְהָעֲדָשָׁה טְמֵאָה.** שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ שֵׁם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ:


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:9:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:6)


**צִנּוֹרָא.** רֹאשׁ הַנֶּזֶם הַנִּכְנָס בְּנֶקֶב הָאֹזֶן אוֹ בְנֶקֶב הָאַף. וּלְפִי שֶׁהוּא עָשׂוּי כְּמַזְלֵג קָרוּי צִנּוֹרָא. תַּרְגּוּם מִזְלְגוֹתָיו צִנּוֹרְיָתֵהּ:


צינורא (hook of a detached earring) – the top of the earring that enters into the incision in the ear or the incision of the nose. And because it is made like a fork, it is called a צנורא. The Aramaic translation of מזלגותיו (see Exodus 27:3)/flesh hooks is צנורייתיה/its hooks.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:9:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:7)


**טְהוֹרָה.** שֶׁאֵין לָהּ שֵׁם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ:


טהורה – because it does not have a name of its own.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:9:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:8)


**הֶעָשׂוּי כְּמִין אֶשְׁכּוֹל.** נֶזֶם הֶעָשׂוּי אַרְבָּעָה אוֹ חֲמִשָּׁה גַרְגְּרִין זֶה עַל גַּבֵּי זֶה כְּמִין אֶשְׁכּוֹל:


העשוי כמין אשכול – an earring made like four or five globules/kernels one on top of another like a kind of cluster.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 11:9:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/11:9:9)


**וְנִפְרַק טָהוֹר.** שֶׁאֵין לְכָל גַּרְגִּיר וְגַרְגִּיר שֵׁם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, וְהוּא אֵינוֹ רָאוּי לְתַשְׁמִישׁ מִשֶּׁנִּפְרַק:


ונפרק טהור – because each globule/kernel does not have a name of its own and it is not worthy of use from when it became detached.



## Chapter 12


### Mishnah 1

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:1)


**טַבַּעַת אָדָם.** כְּגוֹן טַבַּעַת שֶׁל אֶצְבַּע. אֲבָל טַבַּעַת שֶׁהִתְקִינָהּ לַחְגֹּר בּוֹ מָתְנָיו וְלִקְשֹׁר בָּהּ בֵּין כְּתֵפָיו, טְהוֹרָה, וְהַיְנוּ טַבַּעַת כֵּלִים. וְטַעֲמָא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלֹא רַבֵּי קְרָא לְטֻמְאָה אֶלָּא תַכְשִׁיטֵי אָדָם וְלֹא תַכְשִׁיטֵי בְהֵמָה וְכֵלִים:


טבעת אדם – as for example the ring of a finger. But the ring that they established to gird his loins and to and to tie it between his shoulders is ritually pure, and that is a ring of vessels. And the reason is because Scripture did not include anything other than ornaments of a man, but not the ornaments of an animal and vessels.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:2)


**קוֹרַת הַחִצִּים.** אִית דִּמְפָרְשֵׁי אַשְׁפָּה שֶׁהַחִצִּים מֻנָּחִים בָּהּ, וְאִית דִּמְפָרְשֵׁי הַמַּטָּרָה לַחֵץ:


קורת החצים (beam of arrows) – there are those who interpret the dung heap that the arrows are placed upon. And there are those who interpret the target of the arrow.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:3)


**וְשֶׁל אֲסִירִין.** עוֹשִׂין כְּמִין פְּגִימָה בַקּוֹרָה לְהַכְנִיס בָּהּ רֶגֶל אָדָם [וּמַנִּיחִין עֵץ אָרֹךְ עַל גַּבָּהּ] וְאֵין יָכוֹל לָצֵאת. וּבִלְשׁוֹן מִקְרָא קוֹרֵהוּ סַד, וְתָשֵׂם בַּסַּד רַגְלַי (איוב יג). וְקוֹרוֹת שֶׁל חִצִּים וְשֶׁל אֲסִירִין הָאֲמוּרִין כָּאן, דְּמַתֶּכֶת נִינְהוּ וְלֹא שֶׁל עֵץ:


ושל אסירין (and that of prisoners) – that they make like a kind of notch in the beam to bring into it the foot of a man [and they place a long piece of wood on top of it] and one is not able to go out/escape. And in the language of Scripture, they call it a סד/stocks (Job 13:27 – though the verse is slightly misquoted by Bartenura who writes: וישם בסד רגלי – while the Biblical text writes): "ותשם בסד רגלי"/”that You put my feet in the stocks [and watch all my ways].” But the beams of arrows and of prisoners that are mentioned here are of metal and not of wood.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:4)


**קוֹלָר.** שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים בְּצַוַּאר הָאֲסִירִים. [וְהוּא סוֹגֵר]. תַּרְגּוּם וַיִּתְּנֻהוּ בַסּוּגַר (יחזקאל יט), בְּקוֹלָרִין. וּמִשּׁוּם דְּקוֹלָר עָשׂוּי שֶׁיִּשָּׂאֶנּוּ עִמּוֹ בְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוֹלֵךְ, חֲשׁוּב כְּלִי מַעֲשֶׂה טְפֵי מִקּוֹרַת הָאֲסִירִים שֶׁאֵינוֹ זָז בָּהּ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ, הִלְכָּךְ קוֹלָר טָמֵא:


קולר (prisoner’s chain/collar around the neck) – that they place on the neck of prisons. [And it closes]. The Aramaic translation of "ויתנהו בסוגר" (Ezekiel 19:9)/”With hooks he was put in a cage, [They carried him off to the king of Babylon and confined him in a fortress],” with the prisoner’s chain/collar around the neck, and because the prisoner’s collar was made that he would carry with him in every place that he goes, it is considered a usable vessel more than the beam of prisoners which does not move with it from its place. Therefore, the prisoner’s collar/chain is ritually impure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:5)


**שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית נְעִילָה.** עוֹשִׂים לַשַּׁלְשֶׁלֶת בֵּית נְעִילָה [וְנוֹתְנִים אוֹתָהּ בְּרֶגֶל הַסּוּסִים] וְסוֹגְרִים בְּמַפְתֵּחַ, וַחֲשִׁיבָא כְּלִי:


שיש בה בית נעילה – they make for the chain a lock-piece [and place them on the foot of the horses, and close them with a key, and it is considered a vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:6)


**לִכְפִיתָה.** שַׁלְשְׁלָאוֹת שֶׁכּוֹפְתִים בָּהֶן הַקּוֹף וְגוּרֵי הַכְּלָבִים הַקְּטַנִּים. וּלְנוֹי הֵן עֲשׂוּיִין וַהֲווּ תַכְשִׁיט דִּבְהֵמָה וְלֹא מִטַּמֵּא:


לכפיתה (for binding, color-band for animals) – chains that they bind with them the money and the cubs/young animals of small dogs. And they are made for the adornment/beauty and they are an ornament of animals and do not ritually defile.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:7)


**סִיטוֹנוֹת.** סוֹחֲרִים גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁמּוֹכְרִים בְּמִדָּה גַסָּה. וְיֵשׁ לָהֵן שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת שֶׁקּוֹבְעִים בְּרֹאשָׁהּ אֶחָד הַמִּדָּה, סְאָה אוֹ תַרְקַב, וְרֹאשָׁהּ הַשֵּׁנִי נוֹתְנִים בְּטַבַּעַת שֶׁבַּדֶּלֶת אוֹ בַקּוֹרָה, וְסוֹגְרִים עָלֶיהָ בְּמַפְתֵּחַ כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תִגָּנֵב הַמִּדָּה:


סיטונות (wholesale provision dealers – of wheat) – large merchants who sell in big measure. And they have a chain that they affix at one end of the measure, a Seah or a dry measure of three Kabs/Tarkab, and its second end they place in a ring that is I the door or in the beam and close it with a key in order that the measure not be stolen.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:8)


**וְשֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים טְהוֹרָה.** דִּסְתָמָא עֲשׂוּיָה לְנוֹי וְתַכְשִׁיט לַכְּלִי:


ושל בעלי בתים טהורים – for it is merely made for adornment/beauty and it is an ornament for the vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:9)


**מַפְתֵּחַ אֶחָד.** מֵחֻלְיָא אַחַת. דְּשַׁלְשֶׁלֶת בְּחֻלְיָא אַחַת לֹא עָבְדֵי אֱינָשֵׁי, וְלָא חֲשִׁיבָא כְלִי:


מפתח אחד – from one link. People don’t make use of a chain in one link, and it is not a vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:1:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:1:10)


**אוֹ שֶׁקָּשַׁר חִלָּזוֹן בְּרֹאשָׁהּ.** כִּדְמוּת חִלָּזוֹן שֶׁהוּא דָג שֶׁבַּיָּם שֶׁמִּדָּמוֹ צוֹבְעִים הַתְּכֵלֶת קָשַׁר לָהּ בְּרֹאשָׁהּ עָשׂוּי מִבַּרְזֶל, וְהוּא מְשַׁוֵּי לַהּ מָנָא:


או שקשר חלזון בראשה – like the image of snail which is a fish in the see that from its blood they dye the Tekhelet [for the ritual fringes of the Tallit]– he ties it by its head which is made of iron, and it is like a vessel.



### Mishnah 2

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:1)


**קְנֵה מֹאזְנַיִם שֶׁל סָרוֹקוֹת.** סוֹרְקֵי צֶמֶר וּפִשְׁתִּים, וּמוֹכְרִים אוֹתוֹ בְּמִנְיַן לִיטְרָאוֹת, כְּשֶׁרוֹצִין לִשְׁקֹל יֵשׁ לָהֶם מַקֵּל אָרֹךְ שֶׁל עֵץ וְתָלוּי בְּרֹאשׁוֹ כְמִין טַבַּעַת מִלְּמַעְלָה, וְאֻנְקְלָיוֹת שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל תְּלוּיִין מִלְּמַטָּה בְשַׁלְשֶׁלֶת, עֲשׂוּיִין כְּמִין וָוִין וְרָאשֵׁיהֶם כְּפוּפִים מִלְּמַעְלָה, וְיֵשׁ לְאוֹתוֹ מַקֵּל טַבַּעַת אַחֶרֶת שֶׁמְּהַלֶּכֶת עַל פְּנֵי כָל הַמַּקֵּל וְאֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לָצֵאת מִמֶּנּוּ, וּכְמִין עֶשֶׁת שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל אוֹ שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת עָב וְכָבֵד תָּלוּי בְּאוֹתָהּ טַבַּעַת, וּכְשֶׁבָּא לִשְׁקֹל שַׂק שֶׁל צֶמֶר אוֹ שֶׁל מַטְוֶה, תּוֹחֵב אֶת הָאֻנְקְלִי בַּשַּׂק וְאוֹחֵז בַּטַּבַּעַת שֶׁכְּנֶגְדּוֹ לְמַעְלָה וּמַעֲלֵהוּ בָּאֲוִיר, וְהַטַּבַּעַת שֶׁבּוֹ הָעֶשֶׁת שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל תָּלוּי מַרְחִיקָהּ מִטַּבַּעַת שֶׁאוֹחֵז בָּהּ, וּמַכְבֶּדֶת עַל הַקָּנֶה עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא בְיֹשֶׁר שֶׁלֹּא יַכְרִיעַ לְשׁוּם צַד יוֹתֵר, וּלְפִי הַרְחָקַת הַטַּבַּעַת שֶׁבּוֹ הָעֶשֶׁת שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל יוֹדֵעַ חֶשְׁבּוֹן הַמִּשְׁקָל, שֶׁיֵּשׁ סִימָנִים בַּמַּקֵּל, עַד כָּאן לִיטְרָא אַחַת, עַד כָּאן עֲשָׂרָה, עַד כָּאן מֵאָה. וְזֶה נִקְרָא פֶּלֶס בִּלְשׁוֹן מִקְרָא, כְּדִכְתִיב (ישעיה מ) וְשָׁקַל בַּפֶּלֶס הָרִים. פֶּלֶס וּמֹאזְנֵי מִשְׁפָּט לַה'‏ (משלי טז):


קנה מאזנים של סרוקות (the beam of the balance of wool combers/dealers in hatchelled wool) – those who hatchel wool or flax, and sell it a number of liters/measures of capacity, when they want to weigh, they have a long wooden rod and it is suspended at its head like a ring from above., and hooks of iron are suspended from below in a chain, made like hooks and their heads are bent from above. And there is for that rod another ring that goes over the face of the rod and one is not able to go out from it, and it is like a polished block/bar of iron or of thick and heavy copper suspended in that ring, and when he comes to weigh a bag of wool or of yarn, e inserts the hook in the sack and holds the ring that corresponds to it above and raises it in the air, and the ring that has the bar/polished block of iron is suspended removed from the ring that holds it, and it weighs down on the beam until it comes straight and does not bend to any side more, and because the distance of the ring that contains bar/polished block of iron, he knows the number/accounting of the weight, which has symbols on a rod, until here is one Liter, until there, ten, until there – one hundred, and this is called in the language of Scripture פלס , as it is written (Isaiah 40:12): “And weighed the mountains with a scale [and the hills with a balance],” [and] (Proverbs 16:11): “Honest scales and weights are the LORD’s; [All the weights in the bag are His work].”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:2)


**וְשֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים.** אֵין רְגִילִים לָתֵת בּוֹ אֻנְקְלָיוֹת שֶׁהֵן אוֹתָן הַוָּוִין שֶׁתּוֹחֲבִים בַּשַּׂק לְהַעֲלוֹתוֹ, אֶלָּא בְלֹא אֻנְקְלָיוֹת קוֹשְׁרִים בַּחֶבֶל וְתוֹלִין בַּקָּנֶה. אֻנְקְלָיוֹת גָּרְסִינַן, וְלֹא גָרְסִינַן אֻנְקְיוֹת:


ושל בעלי בתים – they don’t regularly place in it hooks which are the hooks that they insert in a sake to raise it, but without hooks, they tie it with a rope and suspend it on a pole. We have the reading אונקליות but we don’t have the reading אונקיות.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:3)


**אֻנְקְלִי שֶׁל כַּתָּפִין.** עֵץ אָרֹךְ כְּעֵין מוֹט שֶׁהַכַּתָּף מַנִּיחַ עַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְתוֹלֶה בוֹ שְׁנֵי שַׂקִּים אֶחָד לְפָנָיו וְאֶחָד מֵאַחֲרָיו בִּשְׁנֵי אֻנְקְלָיוֹת שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל הַתְּחוּבוֹת בַּמּוֹט עַל שְׁנֵי קְצוֹתָיו:


אונקלי של כתפין (hooks of porters/carriers) – a long piece of wood like a kind of balancing pole/staff that the porter places on his shoulder and suspends on it two bags – one in front of him and another behind him with two iron hooks that are inserted in the balancing pole/staff on its two sides.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:4)


**שֶׁל רוֹכְלִים.** מוֹכְרֵי בְשָׂמִים וְתַמְרוּקֵי נָשִׁים:


של רוכלין – those who sell spices and women’s perfumes.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:5)


**טְמֵאָה.** מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל:


טמאה – because it has a receptacle.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:6)


**שֶׁלְּפָנָיו טְמֵאָה.** לְפִי שֶׁהוּא מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהּ:


שלפניו טמאה – because he uses it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:7)


**וְשֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו טְהוֹרָה.** שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהּ אֶלָּא לִשְׁמִירָה, שֶׁלֹּא יִפֹּל הַמַּשְּׂאוֹי מֵאַחֲרָיו. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:


ושלאחריו טהורה – that he doesn’t use it other than for protection, so that the burden will not fall from behind him, but the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yehuda.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:8)


**דַּרְגָּשׁ.** מִטָּה קְטַנָּה שֶׁל עוֹר וְתוֹלִין רְצוּעוֹת בִּשְׂפַת הָעוֹר סָבִיב וְיֵשׁ אֻנְקְלָיוֹת שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל בַּאֲרֻכּוֹת הַמִּטָּה וּכְשֶׁרוֹצִים לִנְטוֹתָהּ עוֹנְבִין הָרְצוּעוֹת בְּאוֹתָן אֻנְקְלָיוֹת:


דרגש (footstool in front of a high bed/state bed with its footstool) – a small bed of leather and they suspend straps at the rim of the leather around and there are iron hooks along the length of the bed and when they wish to stretch it they intertwine/fasten by means of a loop with those hooks.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:9)


**נַקְלִיטִין.** שְׁנֵי עַמּוּדִים שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין בְּאֶמְצַע דָּפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה, אֶחָד מַרְאֲשׁוֹתֶיהָ וְאֶחָד בְּמַרְגְּלוֹתֶיהָ, וּמְפֻצָּלִין בְּרָאשֵׁיהֶן, וּמַנִּיחִין קָנֶה מִזֶּה לָזֶה וּפוֹרְסִים עָלָיו סָדִין. וּפְעָמִים שֶׁאֵין הָעַמּוּדִים מְפֻצָּלִים, אֶלָּא כְעֵין שְׁנֵי וָוִין מַנִּיחִין בְּרָאשֵׁי הַנַּקְלִיטִין, וְהוּא אֻנְקְלִי:


נקליטין (poles of the bedstead, connected by a cross-pole over which a net is spread to form a slanting cover/curtain frame) – two pillars/posts that they place in the middle of the walls of the bed, one from its head and the other from its feet, and it is forked/split at their head, and they place a beam from this side to that and spread over it a sheet. But sometimes the pillars are not forked/split, but it is like two hooks that they place at the top of the poles of the bedstead/curtain frame, and these are hooks.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:10)


**שִׁדָּה.** תֵּבָה קְטַנָּה:


שידה – a small chest.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:11)


**אָקוֹן.** תֵּבָה שֶׁעוֹשִׂין הַצַּיָּדִים לָצוּד בָּהּ דָּגִים:


אקון (reed basket) – a chest that hunters make to hunt fish with.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:12)


**כָּל הַמְחֻבָּר לַטָּמֵא.** אֻנְקְלִי הַמְחֻבֶּרֶת לִכְלִי הַמְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, טָמֵא:


כל המחובר לטמא – a hook that is attached to a vessel that is susceptible to receive ritual impurity is impure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:13)


**לַטָּהוֹר.** כְּגוֹן מְנוֹרַת הָעֵץ שֶׁהִיא טְהוֹרָה, טְהוֹרָה:


לטהור – as for example, a wooden candelabrum which is ritually pure is pure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:14)


**אַחַת אַחַת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן.** כָּל אֻנְקְלִי שֶׁפָּרְשָׁה מִכְּלִי:


אחת אחת בפני עצמה – every hook that is separated from tis vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:2:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:2:15)


**טְהוֹרָה.** לְפִי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ שֵׁם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ:


טהורה – because it doesn’t have a name of its own.



### Mishnah 3

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:1)


**טֶנִי.** הוּא כְלִי שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת מַחֲזִיק שְׁלֹשָׁה קַבִּים. וְהוּא מִלְּשׁוֹן וְשַׂמְתָּ בַטֶּנֶא. וּבַעֲלֵי בָתִּים מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁין בּוֹ שֶׁמַּנִּיחִין שָׁם גְּרוּטָאוֹת מִשִּׁבְרֵי כְלֵי מַתָּכוֹת:


טני (metal cover of a box) – it is a metal vessel that holds three Kab. And it is from the language of "ושמת בטנא" (Deuteronomy 26:2): “put it in a basket.” And owners of homes use it when they place there the rubbish of fragments/shards from metal vessels.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:2)


**רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מְטַמֵּא.** דְּסָבַר כִּסּוּי חֲשׁוּב כְּלִי הוֹאִיל וְיֵשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל:


רבן גמליאל מטמא – for he holds that thee cover is considered a vessel since it has a receptacle.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:3)


**וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.** דְּסָבְרֵי אֵין כִּסּוּי חֲשִׁיב כְּלִי. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


וחכמים מטהרין – for they hold that a cover is not considered a vessel. But the Halakha is according to the Sages.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:4)


**וְשֶׁל רוֹפְאִים טָמֵא.** לְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל. מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָרוֹפְאִים מַנִּיחִין בּוֹ סַמְמָנִים:


ושל רופאים טמא – according to everyone. This is because doctors place drugs in them.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:5)


**מִגְדָּל.** בֵּית הָאוֹצָר שֶׁל עֵץ. ארמריא"ו בְּלַעַ"ז. וּבַעֲרָבִי אלמנס"ר:


מגדל – a storehouse of wood. In the foreign language ARMARIO. And in Arabic ALMENSAR.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:6)


**וְשֶׁל רוֹפְאִים טְמֵאָה.** מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנּוֹתֵן עָלֶיהָ אֶת הָאִסְפְּלָנִית וְתוֹלֶה בָהּ הַמִּסְפָּרַיִם:


ושל רופאים טמאה – because they place upon it a compress/rag and suspends on it the scissors.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:3:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:7)


**הַיַּתּוּכִין.** מֶלְקָחַיִם שֶׁנּוֹטֵל בָּהֶם הַכְּלִי שֶׁהִתִּיךְ בּוֹ אֶת הַכֶּסֶף, לְהָרִיקוֹ לְתוֹךְ כְּלִי אַחֵר:


יתוכין – tongs that they take the vessel with them when he cast/poured on it the silver to empty it into another vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:3:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:8)


**וְהַפְּרָכִין.** בַּתּוֹסֶפְתָּא מְפָרֵשׁ אֵלּוּ הֵן פְּרָכִין, הַקְּבוּעִים בַּכִּירַיִם. וְרַבּוֹתַי לֹא פֵרְשׁוּהָ לִי:


הפריכין (the bars of a grate through which poking is done) – in the Tosefta (see Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia 2:10) it explains what are the bars of a grate through which the poking is done? That are established as iron tools for crowding olives into the vat. But my teachers did not explain it to me.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:3:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:9)


**עַקְרַב בֵּית הַבַּד.** בַּרְזֶל עָקוּם דּוֹמֶה לְעַקְרָב, הַקָּבוּעַ בְּקוֹרַת בֵּית הַבַּד שֶׁדּוֹרְכִים בָּהּ הַזֵּיתִים:


עקרב בית הבד(the iron-shod part of the pressbeam) – curved iron that is similar to a scorpion, that is affixed in the beam of the olive press when they press the olives.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:3:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:10)


**אֻנְקְלִי שֶׁבַּכְּתָלִים.** וָוִין שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל הַקְּבוּעִים בַּכְּתָלִים לִתְלוֹת בָּהֶם כֵּלִים:


אונקלי שבכתלים – iron hooks that are affixed in the walls to suspend vessels on them.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:3:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:3:11)


**טְהוֹרָה.** דְּאֵין תַּשְׁמִישָׁן אֶלָּא עִם הַקַּרְקַע:


טהורים – for their use is only with the ground.



### Mishnah 4

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:1)


**מַסְמֵר הַגָּרָע.** אִזְמֵל שֶׁל אֻמָּן הַמַּקִּיז דָּם. וְנִקְרָא גָרָע עַל שֵׁם שֶׁמְּגָרֵעַ אֶת הַדָּם. וְיֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים, מַסְמֵר שֶׁל נַפָּחִים שֶׁקָּבוּעַ לָהֶן מַסְמֵר בַּסַּדָּן, כְּשֶׁמְּסַלְּקִים חֲתִיכָה שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל מִן הָאֵשׁ וְרוֹצֶה לַחְתֹּךְ מִמֶּנָּה מַנִּיחָהּ עַל הַמַּסְמֵר וּמַכֶּה בַקֻּרְנָס וְנִגְרַעַת:


מסמר הגרע (the nail of the bloodletter) – the cutting tool/surgeon’s knife of an artisan who lets blood flow (i.e., old-time, low-class doctors), and he is called a blood letter because he diminishes the blood. But there are those who interpret the nail of blacksmiths for they had a nail affixed on the block, when they remove a piece of iron from the fire and they want to cut from it, they place it on a nail and beat it with a mallet and it is reduced.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:2)


**אֶבֶן הַשָּׁעוֹת.** אֶבֶן שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ קַוִּים וּרְשׁוּמִים עֲלֵיהֶם שְׁמוֹת הַשָּׁעוֹת, וּמַסְמְרִים תְּחוּבִים בָּהּ שֶׁבָּהֶם מְכַוְּנִים אֶת הַשָּׁעוֹת:


אבן השעות (sundial) – a rock/stone that has upon it lines and inscriptions upon them of the names of the hours, and nails are inserted I it and through them, they determine the hours.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:3)


**מַסְמֵר הַגַּרְדִּים.** מַסְמֵר אָרֹךְ שֶׁהָאוֹרֵג מַכְנִיס בְּקָנֶה דַק וּמְחַבֵּר עַל הַקָּנֶה אֶת הַמַּטְוֶה:


מסמר הגרדים (weaver’s nail/pin) – a long nail that the weaver brings into a thin reed and attaches yarn on the reed.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:4)


**אָרוֹן שֶׁל גָּרוֹסוֹת.** הָעוֹשִׂין גְּרִיסִין שֶׁל פּוֹל בָּרֵחַיִם שֶׁלָּהֶן יֵשׁ לָהֶן כְּמִין אָרוֹן שֶׁל עֵץ:


ארון של גרוסות (ark of the grist dealer) – those who make pounded beans in their millstones, they have a kind of wooden ark/chest.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:5)


**רַבִּי צָדוֹק מְטַמֵּא.** אוֹתוֹ אֲרוֹן, דְּתוֹרַת כְּלִי עָלָיו:


רבי צדוק מטמא – that ark/chest, for it has the law of a vessel upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:6)


**וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.** דִּכְלִי עֵץ הֶעָשׂוּי לְנַחַת הוּא וְאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי לִטַּלְטֵל. וְרַבִּי צָדוֹק סָבַר, פְּעָמִים מְטַלְטְלִין אוֹתוֹ לְתַקְּנוֹ. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק:


וחכמים מטהרין – for a wooden vessel is made for pleasure and is not made to be carried. But Rabbi Tzadok holds, sometimes, hey carry it to repair it. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Tzadok.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:4:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:7)


**הָיְתָה עֲגָלָה.** שֶׁהָאָרוֹן מֻנָּח עָלֶיהָ, שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת:


היתה עגלה – that the ark was placed upon it, of metal.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:4:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:4:8)


**טְמֵאָה.** שֶׁהֲרֵי הִיא עֲשׂוּיָה לְתַשְׁמִישׁ:


טמאה – for it is made for usage.



### Mishnah 5

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:5:1)


**שֶׁהִתְקִינוֹ.** שֶׁעִקֵּם רֹאשׁוֹ אוֹ חִדְּדוֹ כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה פּוֹתֵחַ וְנוֹעֵל בּוֹ:


שהתקינו – that its head is curved or that he sharpened it in order that he would open and close it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:5:2)


**הֶעָשׂוּי לִשְׁמִירָה.** לְסִימָן לִרְאוֹת אִם נִכְנַס שָׁם אָדָם אִם לָאו, שֶׁאִם לֹא יִמְצָאֶנּוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִנִּיחוֹ בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁאָדָם בָּא לְשָׁם:


העשוי לשמירה – as a sign to see if a person enters there or not, for if they don’t find it like he placed it, it is known that a person came there.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:5:3)


**עַד שֶׁיִּצְרְפֶנּוּ.** בָּאֵשׁ לְצֹרֶךְ זֶה. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


עד שיצרפנו (until he smelted/forged it anew) – in fire for this purpose/need. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:5:4)


**מַסְמֵר הַשֻּׁלְחָנִי.** מַסְמֵר קָבוּעַ בָּעַמּוּד שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַשֻּׁלְחָנִי לְהַעֲמִיד בּוֹ תְרִיסֵי הַחֲנוּת, וּכְשֶׁמְּסַלֵּק הַתְּרִיסִים נִשְׁאָר שָׁם הַמַּסְמֵר. וּמְטַהֲרִין רַבָּנָן מִשּׁוּם דְּתַשְׁמִישׁוֹ עִם הַקַּרְקַע. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


מסמר השלחני – a nail that is establish on a pillar that is in front of the moneychanger to set up the shutters of the store, and when they remove the shutters, the nail remains there. But the Rabbis declare it ritually pure because its use is with the ground. And the Halakha is according to the Sages (note: this is already taught in Tractate Eduyot, Chapter 3, Mishnah 8).



### Mishnah 6

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:6:1)


**וּתְלוֹי הַמַּגְרֵדוֹת.** בְּבָתֵּי מֶרְחֲצָאוֹת תּוֹלִין מַגְרֵדוֹת שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת, וְהַנִּכְנָסִים שָׁם כָּל אֶחָד לוֹקֵחַ מִגְרֶדֶת וּמִתְגָּרֵד בָּהּ רַגְלָיו:


ותלוי המגרדות (hanger of a strigil) – in bathhouses, they hang metal strigils and those who enter there each take a strigil and rubs with it his feet.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:6:2)


**וְגֹלְמֵי כְלֵי מַתָּכוֹת.** כֵּלִים שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לָשׁוּף לְגָרֵד וּלְהָקִישׁ בְּקֻרְנָס, אוֹ שֶׁמְּחֻסָּר אֹגֶן, אוֹ אֹזֶן, אֵינָם טְמֵאִים לְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים עַד שֶׁתִּגָּמֵר מְלַאכְתָּן:


וגולמי כלי מתכות (unfinished metal vessels) – vessels that one needs to rub, to comb and to beat with a mallet, or if he is missing a rim of a vessel or a handle, they are not ritually impure according to the words of the Sages until their work is completed.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:6:3)


**וְטַבְלָא שֶׁנֶּחְלְקָה לִשְׁנָיִם.** טַבְלָא שֶׁל חֶרֶס שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ לְבִזְבֵּזִים וְנַעֲשֵׂית שְׁתֵּי חֲתִיכוֹת שָׁווֹת, שֶׁאֵין אַחַת מֵהֶן גְּדוֹלָה מֵחֲבֶרְתָּהּ, בְּהָא פְלִיגֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וַחֲכָמִים. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


וטבלא שנחלקה לשנים – an earthenware tray that has a vertical rims/edges (by which a flat utensil is made into a vessel-like receptacle) and is made into two equal pieces. For not one of them is bigger than its neighbor. In this, Rabban Gamaliel and the Sages dispute. But the Halakha is according to the Sages.



### Mishnah 7

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:1)


**דִּינָר שֶׁנִּפְסַל.** שֶׁפְּסָלַתּוּ מַלְכוּת אוֹ מְדִינָה, אוֹ שֶׁנֶּחְסַר:


דינר שנפסל – that the kingdom defiled it or the country, or that it was lacking [its appropriate weight].


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:2)


**וְהִתְקִינוֹ.** שֶׁנִּקְּבוֹ כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְלֶנּוּ בְּצַוַּאר בְּנוֹ אוֹ בְצַוַּאר בִּתּוֹ:


והתקינו – that he pierced it in order that he could suspend it on the neck or his son or his daughter.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:3)


**סֶלַע.** אַרְבָּעָה דִינָרִים:


סלע – four Denarim.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:4)


**וְהִתְקִינָהּ לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹקֵל בָּהּ.** כֶּסֶף אוֹ זָהָב. דְּאִלּוּ דָבָר הַנִּדְבָּק כְּגוֹן בָּשָׂר וָיַיִן, הָא תַנְיָא בְּפֶרֶק הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הַסְּפִינָה [בָּבָא בַּתְרָא דַּף פט] שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין מִשְׁקָלוֹת שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת לִשְׁקֹל בָּהֶן דָּבָר הַנִּדְבָּק:


והתקינה להיות שוקל בה – silver or gold. For these are a thing that is joined/affixed as for example meat and/or wine, for behold it is taught in a Baraita in the Chapter “He who sells a boat” (Tractate Bava Batra, Chapter 5) [folio 89b]: “They don’t make weights of metal to weigh on them a thing that is attached/affixed.”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:7:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:5)


**עַד שְׁנֵי דִינָרִים.** שֶׁהוּא שֶׁקֶל אֶחָד. וְהוּא חֲצִי סֶלַע:


עד שני דינרים – which is one Shekel. And it is one-half of a Selah.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:7:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:7:6)


**פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן יָקוֹץ.** שֶׁלֹּא יְרַמּוּ בָהּ בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁיַּחְשְׁבוּ שֶׁהוּא שֶׁקֶל. וְכֵן אִם הוּא יוֹתֵר מִשֶּׁקֶל נַמִּי יָקֹץ שֶׁלֹּא יִטְעוּ בוֹ וְיִקְּחוּהוּ בְסֶלַע:


פחות מכאן יקוץ – so that people will not be deceived with it that they will think that it is a Shekel. And similarly, if it is more than a Shekel, it should also be cut up so that they don’t error with it and purchase it for a Selah.



### Mishnah 8

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:1)


**הָאוֹלָר.** כְּעֵין מִסְפָּרַיִם שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת שֶׁמְּתַקְּנִים בּוֹ הַקֻּלְמוֹסִין:


האולר (a penknife) – like a kind of metal scissors that they prepare with it the writing pen/reed.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:2)


**וְהַקֻּלְמוֹס.** שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת וּבַרְזֶל אוֹ שֶׁל כֶּסֶף:


והקולמוס – of bronze and iron or of silver.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:3)


**מְטוּטֶלֶת.** [חֲתִיכַת] בַּרְזֶל וְעוֹפֶרֶת שֶׁתָּלוּי בְּחֶבֶל שֶׁתּוֹפֵס הַבַּנַּאי בְּיָדוֹ לִרְאוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא הַכֹּתֶל עָקוּם:


מטוטלת (plumb-line) – iron and lead that is hanging from a rope that the builder holds in his hand to see that the wall will not come to be curved.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:4)


**וְהַמִּשְׁקָלוֹת.** לִיטְרָא וַחֲצִי לִיטְרָא:


והמשקלות – a liter or a half-liter.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:8:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:5)


**הַכִּירוֹן.** כְּלִי בַרְזֶל שֶׁבּוֹ תּוֹחֲבִים הַזֵּיתִים בַּמַּעֲצָר שֶׁעוֹצְרִים אוֹתָן בּוֹ:


והכירון (iron tool for crowding olives into the vat) – an iron vessel in which they insert the olives in an adze that they stop them in it. –


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:8:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:6)


**וְהַכַּן וְהַכַּנָּא.** הָאַמָּה שֶׁמְּסַרְגְּלִים בָּהּ הַסְּפָרִים, וְהַלּוּחַ שֶׁתַּחְתֶּיהָ. כֵּן פֵּרֵשׁ הֶעָרוּךְ:


והכן והכנא (measuring rod/ruler and measuring table) – the cubit that they draw lines/rule on books/scrolls, and the table that is underneath it. So the Arukh explained.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:8:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:7)


**גֹּלְמֵי כְלֵי עֵץ.** שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁלְמָה מְלַאכְתָּן, כְּגוֹן שֶׁחֲסֵרִים אֹגֶן, אוֹ אֹזֶן, אוֹ הַבָּסִיס שֶׁלָּהֶן שֶׁהֵן יוֹשְׁבִים עָלָיו, אוֹ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לְהַחְלִיקָן וּלְהַשְׁווֹתָן, נִקְרָאִים גֳּלָמִים:


גולמי כלי עץ (unfinished wooden utensils) – that their work [in forming them] was not completed. As for example that they are missing a rim or a handle, or their base when they sit upon it, or that tone needs to divide them and to compare them, they are called גולמים/unfinished.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:8:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:8)


**חוּץ מִשֶּׁל אֶשְׁכְּרוֹעַ.** גָּרְסִינַן. וְהוּא מִין אֶרֶז. תְּאַשּׁוּר, מְתַרְגְּמִינַן אֶשְׁכְּרוֹעַ. וְגָלְמֵי כֵלִים שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ מֵעֵץ זֶה, טְהוֹרִין, לְפִי שֶׁקְּלִפָּתוֹ עָבָה וְקָשָׁה, וְאֵין חֲשׁוּבִין כֵּלִים עַד שֶׁתּוּסַר קְלִפָּתָם וְתִגָּמֵר מְלַאכְתָּם. וְגִרְסַת הַתּוֹסֶפְתָּא, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל פִּירָשָׁע, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מְחֻסָּרִים שְׁלִיקָה. וּפִירָשָׁע הוּא עֲצֵי גֹּפֶר. וְכֵלִים הַנַּעֲשִׂים מִמֶּנּוּ אֵין מְלַאכְתָּן נִגְמֶרֶת אֶלָּא בִשְׁלִיקָה, שֶׁמַּכְנִיסִים אוֹתָן בָּאֵשׁ וּמוֹצִיאִין שֶׁלֶק, וְשׁוּב אֵין יְרֵאִים שֶׁמָּא יִסָּדְקוּ:


חוץ משל אשכרוע (except for the ones made from boxwood/ebony) – We have this reading. And it is a kind of cedar, תאשור which we translate into Aramaic as boxwood/ebony. And unfinished vessels that were made from this wood, are pure, because its husk/skin is thick and hard, but they are not considered vessels until their husks are removed and the work [in creating/forming them] is completed. But the reading of the Tosefta is: חוץ משל פירשע/except for ebony or box wood (see Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia 2:19), because they are lacking boiling [before they can be used]. And פירשע/ebony or boxwood is a resinous wood. But vessels made from it – their work is not [considered to be] completed other than through boiling, that we bring them into the fire and we remove seething, overboiled matter and furthermore, they are not fearful that perhaps they will split.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:8:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:9)


**גְּרוֹפִית שֶׁל זַיִת.** עָנָף שֶׁל זַיִת קָרוּי גְּרוֹפִית. כְּמוֹ שֶׁל תְּאֵנָה דְנִקְרָא יִחוּר. וְאִם עָשׂוּ כְלִי מִן הַגְּרוֹפִית, גֹּלֶם הוּא וְאֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה:


גרופית של זית (a vessel made out of a piece of an olive tree) – a branch of an olive is called a גרופית/a vessel made out of a piece of it, like that of a fig which is called a young shoot [of a fig tree]. But if they made a vessel from a piece of an olive tree, it is an unfinished product and it does not become accessible to receive ritual impurity.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 12:8:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/12:8:10)


**עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁלֹק.** שֶׁיַּכְנִיסוּ אוֹתָן בָּאֵשׁ עַד שֶׁיּוֹצִיאוּ הַשֶּׁלֶק שֶׁלָּהֶן. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:


עד שישלק – until we bring them into the fire that will remove their seething/overboiled matter. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yehuda.



## Chapter 13


### Mishnah 1

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:1)


**הַסַּיִף וְהַסַּכִּין וְהַפִּגְיוֹן.** סַכִּין שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי פִיּוֹת קָרוּי פִּגְיוֹן:


הסיף והסכין והפגיון – a knife that has two mouths is called a dagger.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:2)


**מַגַּל יָד.** מַגָּל חָלָק עָשׂוּי לְשַׁבֵּר עֲצָמוֹת וְלַחְתֹּךְ עֵצִים:


מגל יד (an implement combining a knife and saw) – a smooth implement made to break bones and to cut wood.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:3)


**מַגַּל קָצִיר.** מָלֵא פְגִימוֹת וּתְלָמִים:


מגל קציר (sickle/scythe – a implement with indentations) – filled with notches and ridges.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:4)


**הַשְּׁחוֹר.** הֵם מִסְפָּרַיִם קְטַנִּים שֶׁמְּגַלְּחִין בָּהֶם. וְנִקְרָאִים שְׁחוֹר לְפִי שֶׁהֵם מַשִּׁירִין אֶת הַשֵּׂעָר, דְּמַשִּׁירִין וּמַשְׁחִירִין חַד הוּא, וְהָכִי אָמְרִינַן בְּפֶרֶק מַשִּׁילִין פֵּרוֹת [בֵּיצָה דַּף לה] מַאן דְּתָנֵי מַשְׁחִילִין לֹא מִשְׁתַּבֵּשׁ. וְיֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים, הַשְּׁחוֹר, תַּעַר:


השחור (hair-pinchers or razor) – they are small scissors that one shaves with them. And they are called שחור because they remove the hair, that removing and blackening is one thing, and so we state in the chapter "משילין פירות"/ They let down pieces of produce (Tractate Betzah 35b) that the one who taught “you may let fruit slide down [through an aperture in the roof}/משחילין is not erroneous (see also Tractate Bekhorot, Chapter 6, Mishnah 7). But there are those who interpret השחור is a razor.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:5)


**וְהַזּוּג שֶׁל סַפָּרִים.** מִסְפָּרַיִם גְּדוֹלִים מִן הַשְּׁחוֹר:


והזוג של ספרים – larger scissors than the hair-pincher [or] razor.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:6)


**שֶׁנֶּחֱלְקוּ.** שֶׁהֵן שֶׁל חֻלְיוֹת וּמְפָרְקִים אוֹתָן זֶה מִזֶּה. וְכֵן הַתַּעַר יֵשׁ שֶׁאֵין בֵּית יָד שֶׁלּוֹ מְחֻבָּר, וּמְפָרְקִין אוֹתוֹ:


שנחלקו – that they are of links and they take them apart from each other. And similarly, the razor has those whose handle is not attached and they remove it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:7)


**הַסָּמוּךְ לַיָּד.** חֲזִי לִמְלָאכָה טְפֵי. אֲבָל הַסָּמוּךְ לָרֹאשׁ, יָרֵא שֶׁמָּא יַחְתֹּךְ יָדוֹ. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:


הסמוך ליד – that it is appropriate for work more, but near the head, he fears lest it wound his hand. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yossi.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:8)


**מִסְפֶּרֶת שֶׁנֶּחְלְקָה.** הֵם מִסְפָּרַיִם שֶׁל נָשִׁים, וּכְשֶׁנֶּחְלְקָה אַכַּתִּי כָּל חַד חֲזִי לַחְתֹּךְ:


מספורת שנחלקה (shears which are divided [into two]) – they are women’s scissors, and when they are divided, each one is fit for cutting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:1:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:1:9)


**וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.** כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


וחכמים מטהרין – since it was broken. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.



### Mishnah 2

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:1)


**קֹלִגְרִיפוֹן.** כְּלִי שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁוֹ הָאֶחָד כְּמִין שִׁנַּיִם שֶׁתּוֹחֲבִין בַּפַּת אוֹ בַבָּשָׂר וּמוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ מִן הַתַּנּוּר, וּבְרֹאשׁוֹ הָאַחֵר גּוֹרְפִין בּוֹ גֶחָלִים וָאֵפֶר מִן הַתַּנּוּר:


קוליגריפון (name of a batter’s tool resembling the stylus with one pointed end to pick up the bread called, “the tooth” and one flat and broad end to scrape the ashes out) – a utensil that at its one head is like teeth that we insert in bread or in meat when we remove it from the oven, And with the other head, we scrape out the coals and ashes from the oven.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:2)


**נִטְּלָה כַפָּהּ.** הַצַּד הָרָחָב הֶעָשׂוּי כְּכַף שֶׁגּוֹרְפִין בּוֹ הָאֵפֶר:


ניטלה כפה (that has lost is palm – the flat and broad end – is susceptible to uncleanness on account of its tooth) – the wide side that is made like a spoon that that we scrape the ashes out with it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:3)


**טְמֵאָה.** מִפְּנֵי הָרֹאשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ הַשִּׁנַּיִם שֶׁרְאוּיִין לְתַשְׁמִישָׁן:


טמאה – because the second head that has in it teeth that are appropriate for their use.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:4)


**מִכְחוֹל.** רֹאשׁוֹ אֶחָד חַד כְּעֵין זַכְרוּת לִכְחֹל בּוֹ אֶת הָעַיִן, וְרֹאשׁוֹ הָאַחֵר רָחָב לְנַקּוֹת בּוֹ אֶת הָאֹזֶן:


מכחול (a painting staff the spoon-shaped side of which is broken off) – its one head is pointed/sharp like a kind of thin and pointed side of a double tool to paint the eye with, and the other head is wide to clean the ear with it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:5)


**מַכְתֵּב.** רֹאשׁוֹ אֶחָד חַד כְּמַחַט לִכְתֹּב עַל פִּנְקָס שֶׁל שַׁעֲוָה, וְרֹאשׁוֹ הָאַחֵר עָב וְחָלָק לִמְחֹק בּוֹ הַכְּתָב הֶחָקוּק בַּשַּׁעֲוָה וּלְהַחְלִיקָהּ, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא רָאוּי לַחֲזֹר וְלִכְתֹּב בּוֹ:


מכתב (stylus/writing tool) – one head is pointed/sharp to write on a notebook of wax and the other head is thick and smooth to erase/rub out the writing that is engraved in the way and to smoothen it, in order that it would appropriate to return and to write once again on it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:6)


**זוֹמָלִסְטְרָא.** רֹאשׁוֹ אֶחָד כַּף עָשׂוּי לְקַבֵּל אֶת הַזֻּהֲמָא מִן הַקְּדֵרָה וּלְהַעֲבִירָהּ, וְרֹאשׁוֹ הָאַחֵר כְּעֵין מַזְלֵג לְהַעֲלוֹת הַבָּשָׂר:


זומלסטרא (soup-ladle – with a spoon on one side and a fork on the other) – one head is a spoon, made to receive the filth/smell from the pot and to remove it and the other head is a kind of fork to bring out the meat.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:7)


**וְכֵן הַשֵּׁן שֶׁל מַעְדֵּר.** בְּרֹאשׁוֹ אֶחָד הוֹפְכִים אֶת הַקַּרְקַע, וּבְרֹאשׁוֹ אַחֵר מְחַבְּרִים כְּלֵי הַמַּחְרֵשָׁה זֶה עִם זֶה:


וכן השן של מעדר (the tooth of the mattock/share of the plough) – at its one head they turn over the soil and at the other head the attach the vessel of the plough one with the other.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:2:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:2:8)


**שִׁעוּר כֻּלָּן.** אִם נִטַּל הָרֹאשׁ הָאֶחָד שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שֶׁיִּשָּׁאֵר בָּרֹאשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי כְדֵי שִׁעוּר בֵּית אֲחִיזָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה רָאוּי לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ:


שיעור כולן – if the one head was removed that it is necessary that there would remain of the second head in order to be the measurement of the handle that it would be appropriate to do the work.



### Mishnah 3

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:3:1)


**חַרְחוּר.** כְּלִי עָשׂוּי כְּמִין מָרָה שֶׁחוֹפְרִים בּוֹ אֶת הַקַּרְקַע, וּבַרְזֶל שֶׁלּוֹ מְחֻדָּד טְפֵי לַחְתֹּךְ בּוֹ הַשָּׁרָשִׁים שֶׁלֹּא יְעַכְּבוּ אֶת הַמַּחְרֵשָׁה:


חרחור (coulter, inserted into the horizontal pole/מרדע in front of the ploughshare/דרבן ) – a vessel made like a hoe that we dig up the ground, and its iron is more pointed/sharp to sever the roots so that it will not detain the plough.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:3:2)


**שֶׁיִּנָּטֵל רֻבּוֹ.** רֹב הַבַּרְזֶל אוֹ רֹב חִסּוּמוֹ:


שינטל רובו – most of the iron or most of the steel-coating of the cutting tools/steel-edge.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:3:3)


**מְקוֹפוֹ.** חֹר שֶׁמַּכְנִיס בּוֹ הַקָּתָא. כְּמוֹ [בְּרָכוֹת דַּף נה] קוֹפָא דְּמַחֲטָא:


מקופו (the eye of the coulter for the insertion of the horizontal pole) – a hole in which they insert the handle/helve like [Talmud Berakhot 55b]: “the hole of the needle.”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:3:4)


**טָהוֹר.** דְּתוּ לֹא חֲזִי לִמְלָאכָה כֵּיוָן שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לְהַכְנִיס בּוֹ בֵית יָד:


טהור – for further it is not appropriate for work since one is not able to bring in a handle.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:3:5)


**קֻרְדֹּם.** מְחֻדָּד וְחוֹתֵךְ מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדָיו. הַצַּד הָאֶחָד רָחָב וּמִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁין בּוֹ הַנַּגָּרִים וְקָרוּי עֻשְׁפּוֹ, תַּרְגּוּם מַחְרַשְׁתּוֹ עוּשְׁפֵיהּ. וְהַצַּד הַשֵּׁנִי קָצָר וְקָרוּי בֵּית בִּקּוּעוֹ לְפִי שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ צַד בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים מְבַקְּעִים עֵצִים. וּבַגְּמָרָא בְמַסֶּכֶת בֵּיצָה [דַּף לא] קוֹרֵא לַצַּד הָרָחָב נַקְבוּת שֶׁלּוֹ, וְלַצַּד הַקָּצָר זַכְרוּת שֶׁלּוֹ:


קרדום (hatchet) – that is pointed/sharp and cuts from its two sides. The one side is wide and carpenters use it and it is called its cutting edge. The Aramaic translation of the strigil is called its cutting edge. But the second side is short and it is called that part of the spade (or shovel) that is used for chopping, because it is on that side that homeowners cut/split wood. And in the Gemara in Tractate Betza [folio 31b] it calls the wide side its broadside of a double tool. But the short side is called the thin and pointed side of the double tool [of the hatchet used for splitting].



### Mishnah 4

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:1)


**מַגְרֵפָה.** עֲשׂוּיָה לִגְרֹף אֶת הָאֵפֶר מִן הַכִּירָה וּמִן הַתַּנּוּר, וּכְשֶׁהוּסְרָה כַפָּהּ נִשְׁאַר הַבֵּית יָד שֶׁלָּהּ עָשׂוּי כְּעֵין קֻרְנָס שֶׁל נַפָּחִים, וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר:


מגריפה (ladle/shovel) – made to remove the ashes from the double-stove and from the oven, but when its blade was removed, its handle remained which is made in the form of a mallet of blacksmiths. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Meir.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:2)


**מְגֵרָה.** הִיא מַשּׂוֹר בִּלְשׁוֹן מִקְרָא. סיג"א בְּלַעַ"ז:


מגירה (saw) – it is a fattened ox (see Psalms 69:32 and many other examples throughout Scripture) in the language of Scripture, SIGA in the foreign tongue.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:3)


**אַחַת מִבֵּינְתַיִם טְהוֹרָה.** אִם נִטַּל מִכָּל בֵּין שְׁתֵּי שִׁנַּיִם שֵׁן אַחַת, אִי אֶפְשָׁר יוֹתֵר לִגְרֹר בָּהּ, הִלְכָּךְ טְהוֹרָה, דְּלֹא חַזְיָא לְתַשְׁמִישָׁהּ:


אחת מבינתיים טהורה – if he removed from one tooth from all that have two teeth, it is impossible to anymore to drag any further, therefore it is is ritually pure and is not appropriate for use.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:4)


**נִשְׁתַּיֵּר בָּהּ.** מִן הַשִּׁנַּיִם הַשְּׁלֵמִים שִׁעוּר הַסִּיט בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד:


נשתייר בה – from the complete teeth the measurement of a סיט/the distance between the tip of the thumb and the index finger when held apart in one place.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:5)


**טְמֵאָה.** הַמְּגֵרָה, דִּבְאוֹתוֹ מְלֹא הַסִּיט שֶׁהוּא שָׁלֵם חַזְיָא לִגְרֹר. וְשִׁעוּר מְלֹא הַסִּיט, כָּל מַה שֶּׁאֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם לְהַרְחִיב בֵּין אֶצְבַּע לָאַמָּה:


טמאה – the saw [is ritually impure]. For with that full extent of the distance between the tip of the thumb and the index finger when held apart which is complete is appropriate for dragging. And the measurement of the full extent of the distance between the tip of the thumb and the index finger when held apart, all what is possible for a person to distance between the finger and the forearm.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:6)


**מַעֲצָד.** כְּלִי בַּרְזֶל שֶׁהֶחָרָשׁ מְנַסֵּר בּוֹ הַנְּסָרִים. דולדור"א בְּלַעַ"ז:


מעצד (adze)– an iron vessel that the carpenter planes the boards.. DOLDORA in the foreign language.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:7)


**אִזְמֵל.** תַּעַר קָטָן שֶׁמָּלִין בּוֹ אֶת הַתִּינוֹק. תַּרְגּוּם חַרְבוֹת צוּרִים, אִיזְמְלִין חֲרִיפִין:


איזמל – a small razor that one circumcises a baby with. The Aramaic translation of חרבות צורים/flint knives (see Joshua 5:2-3) which is “sharp knives.”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:8)


**וְהַמַּפְסֶלֶת.** בַּרְזֶל מְחֻדָּד קָבוּעַ בְּתוֹךְ עֵץ, וּמוֹלִיכִין וּמְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ עַל הַלּוּחַ וּמַחֲלִיקִין אוֹתוֹ. לְשׁוֹן פְּסָל לְךָ:


והמפסלת (plane/sculptor’s chisel) – sharp/pointed iron that is fixed within wood and they take it and bring it over the board and smooth it out. It is the [Scriptural] language of (Exodus 34:1): “"פסל לך/”Carve for yourself.”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:9)


**מַקְדֵּחַ.** כְּלִי שֶׁבּוֹ מְנַקְּבִים הַלּוּחוֹת:


מקדח (borer – used by carpenters) – a vessel/utensil that they make holes/perforate boards.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:10)


**שֶׁנִּפְגְּמוּ.** נִתְבַּקְּעוּ:


שנפגמו (which have been damaged) – that were split/broken apart.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:11)


**נִטַּל חִסּוּמָן.** בְּפִי הַחֶרֶב וּבְפִי הַסַּכִּין וּבְפִי הַקֻּרְדֹּם וּבְחֻדּוֹ שֶׁל מַקְדֵּחַ נוֹתְנִים בַּרְזֶל טוֹב וְנֶחְשָׁב, אצאל"ו בְּלַעַ"ז, וְחוֹסְמִין פִּיהֶן בּוֹ כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא חַד לַחְתֹּךְ יָפֶה, וְזֶה קָרוּי חִסּוּמָן:


ניטל חיסומן (if their steel-edge is worn off) – in the mouth of the sword and in the mouth of the knife and in the mouth of a hatchet/mattock and in the thin part of the borer they place good and considered iron, ATZALAV in the foreign tongue, and they muzzle their mouths with it in order that it will be sharp/pointed to cut/sever well, and this is called, חיסומן/their steel-edge.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:4:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:4:12)


**וְהָרוּקְנִי.** הָעֵץ שֶׁהַמַּפְסֶלֶת קְבוּעָה בוֹ קָרוּי רוּקְנִי. וְאִם נִטַּל הַבַּרְזֶל שֶׁפּוֹסֵל וּמַחְלִיק וְנִשְׁאַר הָעֵץ לְבַדּוֹ בְּלֹא הַבַּרְזֶל, טָהוֹר:


והרוקני (the plane [the wooden body] by itself) – the wood that the sculptor’s chisel/plane is fixed in it is called רוקני. But if the iron was worn off that makes ritually impure and smoothens, and the wood remains alone without iron, it is ritually pure.



### Mishnah 5

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:1)


**חֲרִירָהּ.** כְּמוֹ חוֹרָהּ. הַחוֹר שֶׁמַּכְנִיסִין בּוֹ הַחוּט:


חרירה (the eye-needle) – like its hole. The hole that one threads/brings the thread through (see also Tractate Shabbat 52b for a similar expression).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:2)


**עֻקְצָהּ.** הָרֹאשׁ הַחַד שֶׁמַּכְנִיסִים בַּבֶּגֶד כְּשֶׁתּוֹפְרִין. כְּמוֹ עֻקְצֵי תְאֵנִים, שֶׁהוּא הַחֹד שֶׁבַּתְּאֵנִים:


עוקצה (whose point is broken off) – the sharp head that they bring into the clothing when they sew. Like the peduncle of a fig (that is attached to the tree when it is cut off).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:3)


**אִם הִתְקִינָהּ לְמִתּוּחַ.** דֶּרֶךְ הָאוֹרְגִים שֶׁלּוֹקְחִים מַחַט שְׁבוּרָה וְנוֹתְנִים אוֹתָהּ בִּשְׂפַת הַבֶּגֶד כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּמָּתְחוּ שִׂפְתוֹתֶיהָ:


אם המתינה למתוח (if he made it into a stretching pin) – it is the manner of weavers that take a broken needle and place it into the rim of the cloth in order to stretch its rims.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:4)


**מַחַט שֶׁל סַקָּאִים.** מַחַט גָּדוֹל שֶׁתּוֹפְרִים בּוֹ הַשַּׂקִּים הָעֲשׂוּיִים מִשְּׂעַר עִזִּים, וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן מִן הַבְּגָדִים הַגַּסִּין:


מחט של סקאים (sack-maker’s needle) – a large needle that they sew with it the sacks that are made from the hair of goats and similar animals from the thick clothing.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:5)


**שֶׁהוּא כוֹתֵב בָּהּ.** בְּפִנְקָס שֶׁל שַׁעֲוָה:


שהוא כותב בה – on a tablet of wax.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 13:5:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/13:5:6)
