[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:4:4)


**אַף מַלְבֵּן הַכִּסֵּא טָמֵא.** כְּלוֹמַר, אַף מַלְבֵּן הַכִּסֵּא בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ בְלֹא הַכִּסֵּא וּבְלֹא חִפּוּיָו טָמֵא, כָּל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁהַכִּסֵּא בְלֹא חִפּוּיָו טָמֵא. מַלְבֵּן, צוּרַת לְבֵנָה מְרֻבַּעַת עוֹשִׂים עַל הַכִּסֵּא וְיוֹשְׁבִים עָלָיו:


אף מלבן הכסא טמא – meaning to say, that even the frame of the chair on its own, without the seat and without its cover is impure, all the more so that he chair without its covering is impure. The frame, is the form of square brick they make on the chair and they sit upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:4:5)


**כִּסֵּא שֶׁקְּבָעוֹ בַעֲרֵבָה.** הֵבִיא כִסֵּא מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר וּקְבָעוֹ בַעֲרֵבָה דֶרֶךְ יְשִׁיבָתוֹ. וַעֲרֵבָה אֵינָהּ טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, דְּחַזְיָא לְלִישָׁה:


כסא שקבעו בעריבה (a chair that one affixed to a trough) – they brought a chair from another place and affixed it in a trough in the manner of his sitting. But the trough is not impure through treading. For it is appropriate for kneading.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:4:6)


**בֵּית שַׁמַּאי מְטַמְּאִין.** דְּלֹא בָטֵל כִּסֵּא לְגַבֵּי עֲרֵבָה:


בית שמאי מטמאין – for it did not annul the seat concerning the trough.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:4:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:4:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:4:7)


**וּבֵית הִלֵּל מְטַהֲרִין.** מִמִּדְרָס. דְּבָטֵל כִּסֵּא לְגַבֵּי עֲרֵבָה. אֲבָל כִּסֵּא הֶעָשׂוּי בָּעֲרֵבָה עַצְמָהּ מוֹדוּ בֵית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל דְּטָהוֹר:


ובית הלל מטהרין – [makes it pure] from [impurity through] treading, for the seat is nullified concerning the trough. But concerning a seat made in the trough itself, the School of Shammai agrees with the School of Hillel that it is pure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:4:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:4:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:4:8)


**וְשַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר.** אַף כִּסֵּא הֶעָשׂוּי בָּעֲרֵבָה עַצְמָהּ טָמֵא מִדְרָס:


ושמאי אומר – even the sea that is made inside the trough itself is impure through treading.



### Mishnah 5

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:5:1)


**כִּסֵּא שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ חִפּוּיָו יוֹצְאִים.** שֶׁאֵין הַנְּסָרִים בּוֹלְטִים חוּץ מִן הַכִּסֵּא. שֶׁהַכִּסֵּא עָשׂוּי מֵאַרְבָּעָה עֵצִים וּנְסָרִים קְבוּעִין מִשְּׁלֹשׁ רוּחוֹת הַכִּסֵּא עוֹמְדִין גְּבוֹהִים תַּחַת הָעֵצִים מְהֻדָּקִים זֶה אֵצֶל זֶה, וּמִמַּעַל לָעֵצִים לוּחוֹת עֲשׂוּיִין לֵישֵׁב עֲלֵיהֶן. וְאִם נִשְׁבְּרוּ הַלּוּחוֹת הָעֲשׂוּיוֹת לְמוֹשָׁב, יָכוֹל לְהַטּוֹת הַכִּסֵּא לְכָל צַד שֶׁיִּרְצֶה וְלֵישֵׁב עַל אוֹתָן הַנְּסָרִים הַקְּבוּעִים בְּשָׁלֹשׁ רוּחוֹת שֶׁל כִּסֵּא, אֲבָל כְּשֶׁהֵן בּוֹלְטִים לַחוּץ אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַטּוֹתוֹ עַל צִדּוֹ. וְחִפּוּיָו דְּהָכָא לָאו כְּחִפּוּיָו דְּרֵישָׁא שֶׁהֵן כְּמוֹ שִׁנַּיִם בּוֹלְטִים, אֶלָּא לַנְּסָרִים שֶׁמְּחַפִּין הָעֵצִים קָרֵי חִפּוּיָו:


כסא שלא היו חפויו יוצאין – that the boards/planks do not protrude outside of the chair. That the chair is made from four [pieces of] wood and planks fixed from three directions of the chair stands high under the wood that is fastened with each other, and from above the wood, tablets are made to sit upon them. But if the tablets are broken that are made for sitting, one can tip the chair to each side that one wishes and to sit upon those boards that are affixed from the three sides of the chair, but when they protrude outward, he is not able to tip it on its side. And the covers/seat boards mentioned here are not like the covers/seat boards mentioned in the first part of the Mishnah, for they are like protruding teeth, but rather for the boards that cover the wood are called חפויו/upholstered seat.



### Mishnah 6

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:6:1)


**שֶׁנִּטַּל חִפּוּיוֹ הָאֶמְצָעִי.** שֶׁנִּטַּל לוּחַ הָאֶמְצָעִי וְנִשְׁאַר לוּחַ מִכָּאן וְלוּחַ מִכָּאן:


שניטל חפויו האמצעי – that the middle board/tablet was removed and there remains a board from here and a board from there.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:6:2)


**טָמֵא.** דַּחֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה:


טמא – for it is appropriate for sitting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:6:3)


**אִם הָיָה רָחָב טֶפַח.** חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה. וְאִם לֹא, לֹא:


אם היה רחב טפח – it would be appropriate for sitting, but if is not, it is not [appropriate for sitting].



### Mishnah 7

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:7:1)


**שְׁנַיִם מֵחִפּוּיָו.** מִלּוּחוֹת הָעֲשׂוּיוֹת לְמוֹשָׁב:


שנים מחפויו – from the tablets that are made for sitting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:7:2)


**רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא.** וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:


רבי עקיבא מטמא – But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Akiba.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:7:3)


**וְנִשְׁתַּיֵּר בּוֹ בֵית קַבָּלָה.** שֶׁהוּא חָלוּל קְצָת וְרָאוּי לְקַבֵּל רִמּוֹנִים, טָהוֹר. וְלֹא מְטַמְּאִינַן לֵיהּ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל:


ונשתייר בו בית קבלה – that is slightly hollow and appropriate to receive pomegranates is pure, and we don’t defile it because it has a receptacle.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:7:4)


**מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבָּטַל הָעִקָּר.** דְּעִקָּרוֹ לִישִׁיבָה עֲבִיד וְלֹא לְבֵית קִבּוּל, וְהוֹאִיל וְנִתְבַּטֵּל הָעִקָּר שֶׁבַּעֲבוּרוֹ הָיָה חֲשׁוּב כְּלִי, בָּטְלָה הַטְּפֵלָה, וְלֹא מִטַּמֵּא מִטַּעַם שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל. וְכֵן הֲלָכָה. דְּהָכִי תְנַן לְעֵיל פֶּרֶק הַמְפָרֵק גַּבֵּי מִשְׁפֶּלֶת. וּבְפֶרֶק כָּרִים וּכְסָתוֹת גַּבֵּי חֵמֶת:


מפני שבטל העקיר – for is made for the primary purpose of sitting and not as a receptacle , for since the primary purpose was nullified, and on whose account it was considered a vessel, the secondary purpose was annulled, but it was not nullified for the reason that it has a receptacle. And this is the Halakha. And this is taught above in the chapter “Who takes apart/loosens” (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 19, Mishnah 10) and in the chapter “Mattresses and Pillows” (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 20, Mishnah 2).



### Mishnah 8

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:1)


**שִׁדָּה.** עֲשׂוּיָה כְמִין אָרוֹן. וּבְשִׁדָּה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מַחְזֶקֶת אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מַיְרֵי, שֶׁהִיא מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה:


שידה (chest, strong box) – made like a kind of ark. And we are speaking of a chest that does not hold forty Se’ah, which is susceptible to receive ritual impurity.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:2)


**שֶׁנִּטַּל הָעֶלְיוֹן.** הַכִּסּוּי שֶׁעָלֶיהָ:


שניטל העליון – the covering that is over it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:3)


**הַתַּחְתּוֹן.** שׁוּלֶיהָ:


התחתון – its rim.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:4)


**נִטַּל הָעֶלְיוֹן וְהַתַּחְתּוֹן.** וְהַדַּפִּין שֶׁבַּצְּדָדִין נִשְׁאֲרוּ:


ניטל העליון והתחתון – but the planks that are on the sides remained.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:8:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:5)


**וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.** וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


וחכמים מטהרין – And the Halakha is according to the Sages.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:8:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:8:6)


**הַסַּתָּת.** מְסַתֵּת אֲבָנִים. וְהוּא מְתַקֵּן לוֹ מָקוֹם לָשֶׁבֶת בְּקָצֶה הָאֶחָד מֵהָאֶבֶן כְּשֶׁמְּסַתֵּת בַּקָּצֶה הַשֵּׁנִי:


הסתת (stone-cutter, chiseler) – who cuts/chisels stones. And he prepares for him a place to sit on one end of the stone when he is cutting/chiseling the other end.



### Mishnah 9

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:1)


**כֹּפֶת.** חֲתִיכַת עֵץ עָבָה וּרְחָבָה. וְהָכִי מַשְׁמַע פֵּרוּשׁוֹ בַתּוֹסֶפְתָּא:


כופת (a block with a concave top to sit upon/bolster, stool) – a thick and wide piece of wood, and this is implied in his explanation in the Tosefta (see Tosefta Demai, Chapter 1, Halakha 11 and see also Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra, Chapter 2, Halakha 1).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:2)


**סֵרְקוֹ.** צִיְּרוֹ:


סרקו – which was painted.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:3)


**וְכִרְכְּמוֹ.** צְבָעוֹ בְכַרְכֹּם:


וכרכמו (which was varnished) – which was colored with crocus/saffron.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:4)


**וְעֲשָׂאוֹ פָנִים.** פִּסְּלוֹ בְמַעֲצָד וְהִשְׁוָהוּ בִרְהִיטְנִי, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִרְאִים לוֹ פָנִים יָפִים:


ועשאו פנים (or was polished) – he invalidated it with an adze and made it smooth with a tool for planning wood, that it should have a nice appearance.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:9:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:5)


**רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַמֵּא.** דְּמוֹשָׁב הוּא:


רבי עקיבא מטמא – for it is for sitting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:9:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:6)


**וַחֲכָמִים מְטַהֲרִין.** דְּכַחֲתִיכַת עֵץ בְּעָלְמָא חֲשִׁיב:


וחכמים מטהרין – for it is considered like a plain piece of wood.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:9:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:7)


**עַד שֶׁיָּחֹק.** שֶׁיַּחְקֹק בּוֹ מְקוֹם יְשִׁיבָה:


עד שיחק בו (until he will make a hollow on it) – until he hollows out a place of sitting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:9:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:8)


**הִתְקִינָן לִישִׁיבָה טְהוֹרִים.** מִמִּדְרָס. לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עֲשׂוּיִין לִישִׁיבָה וּבָטְלָה דַעְתּוֹ אֵצֶל כָּל אָדָם:


התקינו לישיבה – from impurity through treading/Midras, because they are not made for sitting and knowledge of it was abolished among all people.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:9:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:9)


**סֵרְגָן בְּגֶמִי.** עַל פִּיהֶן, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁמְּסָרְגִין אֶת הַמִּטּוֹת:


סרגן בגמי (if he plaited them over with reed-grass) – on their openings, in the manner that they plait the beds.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:9:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:9:10)


**טְמֵאִין.** דְּאֵין הַתֶּבֶן וְהַמּוֹכִין יְכוֹלִין לִפֹּל, וַחֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה:


טמאין – that the straw and the hackled wool/a soft spongy substance won’t be able to fall, and they are appropriate for sitting.



### Mishnah 10

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:1)


**הָאַסְלָה.** בֵּית מוֹשָׁב שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל מְכֻסֶּה עוֹר, וְיוֹשְׁבִים עָלָיו בְּבֵית הַכִּסֵּא:


האסלא (privy/toilet; iron frame of a privy-stool covered with leather) – place of sitting of iron which is covered with leather, and they sit upon it in the toilet.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:2)


**פֵּרְשָׁה.** הָעוֹר מִן הַבַּרְזֶל:


פירשה (if it was separated) – the leather from the iron.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:3)


**הָעוֹר טָמֵא מִדְרָס.** דְּעוֹר בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה, וְהַבַּרְזֶל בְּלֹא עוֹר לֹא חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה, וַחֲזִי לִשְׁאָר תַּשְׁמִישִׁים:


העור טמא מדרס – that the leather by itself is appropriate for sitting, but the iron without the leather is not appropriate for sitting, but it is appropriate for other usages.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:4)


**טְרַסְקָל.** סַל קָטָן עָשׂוּי מֵעֲרָבָה קְלוּפָה, וְאוֹכְלִים עָלָיו לֶחֶם:


טרסקל (basket) – a small basket made from peeled willows, and they eat bread upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:5)


**וְהַטְּרַסְקָל טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם.** דְּמִפְּנֵי קָטְנוֹ לֹא חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה. וְלֹא לִשְׁאָר תַּשְׁמִישִׁין, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ דְפָנוֹת:


והטרסקל טהור מכלום (a chair on three legs, a camp-chair is clean of all) – that because of its being small, it is not appropriate for sitting , and neither for the rest of the usages, for it has no walls.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:6)


**סַפְסָלִים שֶׁבַּמֶּרְחָץ.** שֶׁל שַׁיִשׁ הֵן:


ספסלים שבמרחץ – they are of marble.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:7)


**שֶׁשְּׁתֵּי רַגְלָיו שֶׁל עֵץ טָמֵא.** אִם יָשַׁב הַזָּב עָלָיו טְמֵאִין הָרַגְלַיִם: **שֶׁל עֵץ.** מִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב. אֲבָל הַסַּפְסָל עַצְמוֹ טָהוֹר, דִּכְלֵי אֲבָנִים אֵין לָהֶם טֻמְאָה כְלָל לֹא מִדִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה וְלֹא מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים:


ששתי רגליו של עץ טמא – if the person with gonorrhea sat upon it, the legs of wood are unclean because of uncleanness through sitting. But the bench itself is ritually pure, for the stone vessels have no defilement at all, neither from the words of the Torah nor from the words of the Scribes.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:8)


**וְאַחַת שֶׁל אֶבֶן טָהוֹר.** דַּהֲוֵי כְאִלּוּ הַסַּפְסָל כֻּלּוֹ מֵאֶבֶן:


ואחת של אבן טהור – for it is as if the bench is completely made from stone.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:9)


**שֶׁשִּׁגְּמָן.** שֶׁפִּסְּלָן וְתִקְנָן בִּרְהִיטְנִי:


ששיגמן (which one planed; or that one joined with bamboo) – that had become unfit and were repaired with a tool to plane wood/a chisel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:10)


**שֶׁיְּהוּ הַמַּיִם הוֹלְכִים תַּחְתֵּיהֶן.** וְלָאו לִישִׁיבָה עֲבִידֵי, אֲבָל בְּנֵי אָדָם יוֹשְׁבִים שָׁם כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִטַּנְּפוּ מִמֵּי הַמֶּרְחֲצָאוֹת הַיּוֹצְאִים. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


שיהו המים הולכים תחתיהן – but they are not made for sitting, but people sit there in order that they not be soiled from the water of bath-houses that come out. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:11)


**קַנְקֵילִין.** כְּלִי שֶׁמְּשִׂימִין תַּחְתָּיו אֵשׁ וְגָפְרִית כְּדֵי לְעַשֵּׁן הַבְּגָדִים שֶׁעָלָיו:


קנקילין (perforated vessel for fumigation) – a vessel that they place fire and sulfur underneath them in order to fumigate the clothing that is upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:12)


**שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ בֵּית קַבָּלַת כְּסוּת.** שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל לְקַבֵּל הַבְּגָדִים שֶׁעָלֶיהָ:


שיש לה בית קבלה כסות – that it has a receptacle to receive the clothing that is upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 22:10:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/22:10:13)


**כְּכַוֶּרֶת.** מְפֻלֶּשֶׁת מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִים:


ככוורת – that it is perforated from its two sides.



## Chapter 23


### Mishnah 1

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:1)


**הַכַּדּוּר.** פלוט"א בְּלַעַ"ז:


הכדור – PLOTA in the foreign language.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:2)


**וְהָאִמּוּם.** דְּפוּס שֶׁל מִנְעָל. וְכָל אֵלּוּ חִיצוֹנֵיהֶם עוֹר וּמְלֵאִין מִבִּפְנִים שֵׂעָר אוֹ מוֹכִין:


והאימום (model, shoe-maker’s last) – frame of a shoe. And all of these their outer sections are leather and they filled from the inside with hair or hackled wool/a spongy substance.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:3)


**וְהַקָּמֵעַ וְהַתְּפִלִּין.** יֵשׁ בְּתוֹךְ הַבָּתִּים שֶׁל עוֹר פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת כְּתוּבוֹת בִּקְלָף:


והקמיע והתפילין (the [parchment] amulet and the phylactery) – there is within the housing of leather [Biblical] portions written on parchment.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:4)


**וּבְמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָן טָהוֹר.** אִם נִטְמָא אַחַת מֵאֵלּוּ בְמֵת וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִקְרַע, וְנָגַע אֶחָד בְּמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָן, טָהוֹר, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָן חִבּוּר לָהֶן וְאֵין מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָן טָמֵא כְמוֹתָן:


ובמה שבתוכן טהור – if one of these was defiled through [contact with] a corpse and afterwards was torn, and a person came in contact with what is within them, he is ritually pure, because there isn’t any attachment with what is within them, and there isn’t anything that is within them that is ritually impure like them.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:5)


**הַכָּאוּף.** כְּמוֹ אֻכָּף:


הכאוף – like אוכף/saddle.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:6)


**הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ טָמֵא.** אִם נִטְמָא הָאֻכָּף בְּמֵת, כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַנּוֹגֵעַ בּוֹ טָמֵא, כָּךְ הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּמַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכוֹ טָמֵא:


הנוגע במה שבתוכו טמא – if the saddle was defiled through [contact with] a corpse, just as what touches it is ritually impure, so the person who coms in contact with what is within it is also ritually impure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:1:7)


**מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַתֶּפֶר מְחַבְּרוֹ.** וְעוֹשֵׂהוּ אֶחָד, זֶה שֶׁבִּפְנִים עִם הַחִיצוֹן:


מפני שהתפר מחברו (because the stitching connects it – the covering to the stuffing) – and makes it one, that which is within with the outer part.



### Mishnah 2

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:1)


**זָרֵיז הָאַשְׁקְלוֹנִי.** חֲגוֹרָה רְחָבָה שֶׁבָּהּ חוֹבְשִׁים אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה. תַּרְגּוּם וַיַּחֲבֹשׁ אֶת חֲמוֹרוֹ, וְזָרֵז (בראשית כב) וּבְאַשְׁקְלוֹן עוֹשִׂים אוֹתָן שֶׁל עֵץ, וּקְרוּיִין זָרֵיז אַשְׁקְלוֹנִי עַל שֵׁם מְקוֹמָן:


זריז האשקלוני (the Ashkelonian saddle) – a wide belt in which harness/saddle the cattle. It is the Aramaic translation of (Genesis 22:3): “And he (i.e., Abraham) saddled his ass,” and he saddled it. And in Ashkelon they make it of wood, and it is called the Ashkelonian saddle on account of their place.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:2)


**מְדוֹכָה הַמָּדִית.** מַכְתֶּשֶׁת הָעֲשׂוּיָה בְמָדַי. לוֹקְחִים חֲתִיכַת עֵץ גְּדוֹלָה עָבָה וַאֲרֻכָּה, וְחוֹקְקִים כְּמִין מַכְתֶּשֶׁת בְּאֶמְצָעָהּ, וְרוֹכְבִים עָלֶיהָ מִכָּאן וּמִכָּאן וְכוֹתְשִׁים. וּלְפִיכָךְ יֵשׁ עָלָיו תּוֹרַת מֶרְכָּב:


מדוכה המדית (a Median mortar – on the protruding handles of which the pounders ride when at work) – a mortar that is made in Median. They take a large, thick, and long piece of wood, and they hollow it out/shape a receptacle in its middle, and ride upon it from here and from there and pound it/crush it. Therefore, it has upon it the law of מרכב/riding upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:3)


**עָבִיט שֶׁל גָּמָל.** תַּרְגּוּם בְּכַר הַגָּמָל, בַּעֲבִיטָא דְגַמְלָא (שם לא):


עביט של גמל (the cushion on the camel’s back) – It is the Aramaic translation of the camel bearing for the first time, the cushion on the camel’s back (Genesis 31:34): “[Rachel, meanwhile, יhad taken the idols and placed them] In the camel cushion [and sat on them].”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:4)


**טַפֵּיטָן שֶׁל סוּס.** אֻכָּף שֶׁעַל הַסּוּס בִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה טַפֵּיטָן שְׁמוֹ, וְשֶׁל גָּמָל עָבִיט שְׁמוֹ, וְשֶׁל נָאקָה אֻכַּף שְׁמוֹ, כָּל אֶחָד שְׁמוֹ עָלָיו. וְכֻלָּן מֶרְכָּב הֵן, אֶלָּא שֶׁיֶּשׁ מֵהֶן שֶׁפְּעָמִים עֲשׂוּיִין לֵישֵׁב עֲלֵיהֶן:


טפיטן של סוס (horse-cloth, housing) – the saddle that is upon the horse in the language of eh Mishnah it is called טפיטן/horse-cloth, housing, and for a camel, its name is a cushion/עביט, and of a נאקה/camel it is called a saddle, each one has its name upon it. And all of them are for riding, but there are from them that sometimes they are made to sit upon them.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:5)


**טַפֵּיטָן שֶׁל סוּס טָמֵא מוֹשָׁב.** דְּאֵין טָמֵא מֶרְכָּב אֶלָּא הַמְיֻחָד לִרְכִיבָה בְּפִסּוּק רַגְלַיִם, וְאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי לִישִׁיבָה כְלָל:


טפיטן של סוס טמא משום מושב – but it is not ritually impure through riding other than which is designated for riding through spreading of the feet, but it is not made for sitting at all.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:6)


**בַּקֻּנְפּוֹן.** שָׂדֶה שֶׁשּׂוֹחֲקִים שָׁם הַמְּלָכִים, וּרְגִילִים לָשֶׁבֶת עַל הַטַּפֵּיטָן שֶׁל סוּס לִרְאוֹת בִּשְׂחוֹק הַמֶּלֶךְ, הִלְכָּךְ טָמֵא מוֹשָׁב. קוּנְפּוֹן, שָׂדֶה, בִּלְשׁוֹן לע"ז קנפ"ו. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:


בקונפון (plain for exercise and amusement – because soldiers and sports stand upon it) – a field that the kings play there, and they regularly sit on the horse-cloth/housing of the horse to see the playing of the king, therefore it is impure through sitting. קונפון is a field, KANPO in the foreign tongue. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Yossi.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:2:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:2:7)


**אֲבָל אֻכָּף שֶׁל נָאקָה טָמֵא.** רַמְבַּ"ם פֵּרֵשׁ, טָמֵא מוֹשָׁב. וְתַנָּא קַמָּא קָאָמַר לַהּ, דְּפָלֵיג אַטַּפֵּיטָן שֶׁל סוּס וּמוֹדֶה בְאֻכָּף שֶׁל נָאקָה שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא מוֹשָׁב. וְרַבּוֹתַי פֵּרְשׁוּ, אֲבָל אֻכָּף שֶׁל נָאקָה טָמֵא מֶרְכָּב. וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי קָאָמַר לַהּ, דְּמוֹדֶה לְתַנָּא קַמָּא בְּאֻכָּף שֶׁל נָאקָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְיֻחָד אֶלָּא לִרְכִיבָה:


אבל אוכף של נאקה טמא – Maimonides explained, that it is impure through sitting. And the first Tanna/teacher said it, for he argues concerning the horse-cloth of a horse, but agrees regarding the saddle of a camel that it is ritually impure through sitting. But my teachers/Rabbis explained, but a saddle of a camel is impure through riding. But Rabbi Yossi stated that, for he agrees with the first Tanna/teacher regarding the saddle of a camel that it is not designated other than for riding.



### Mishnah 3

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:3:1)


**חָלַק מַגָּעוֹ מִמַּשָּׂאוֹ.** דְּנוֹשֵׂא מְטַמֵּא בְגָדִים וְאֵין נוֹגֵעַ מְטַמֵּא בְגָדִים:


חלק מגעו ממשאו (distinguished touching it from carrying it) – for a person who carries [something] defiles clothing but the one who touches it does not defile clothing.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:3:2)


**תָּפִית שֶׁל חֲמוֹר.** עֵצִים שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים עַל גַּב הַחֲמוֹר לְחַבֵּר וְלִקְשֹׁר עֲלֵיהֶם הַמַּשָּׂא. וְאֵינָן רְאוּיִין לֹא לִרְכִיבָה וְלֹא לִישִׁיבָה:


תפית של חמור (saddle of a sumpter-ass – consisting of wooden frames) wood that we place on top of the donkey to attach and to tie upon them the load, but they are not appropriate either for riding nor for sitting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:3:3)


**שִׁנָּה אֶת הַנְּקָבִים.** דִּבְשִׁנּוּי נִקְבֵיהֶן נוֹתֵן מָקוֹם לְאָדָם לֵישֵׁב שָׁם:


שינה אתת הנקבים (if one changed the width between the spaces) – that through the change of their incisions/spaces, one gives place for a person to sit there.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:3:4)


**אוֹ שֶׁפֵּרְצָן.** שֶׁהֱסִירָם מִמְּקוֹמָם וּנְתָנָן זֶה לְצַד זֶה. וְיֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים, תָּפִית שֶׁל חֲמוֹר טְהוֹרָה לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּרָחְבָּהּ טֶפַח, וְכָל שֶׁאֵין בְּרָחְבָּהּ טֶפַח לֹא חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה, וּכְשֶׁשִּׁנָּה אֶת הַנְּקָבִים דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁהִרְחִיב מְקוֹם הַמּוֹשָׁב אוֹ שֶׁפֵּרְצָן וְנַעֲשָׂה מְקוֹם הַמּוֹשָׁב רָחָב טֶפַח, טְמֵאָה:


או פרצן (or broke them into one another) – that he removed them from their places and put them one at the side of the other. And there are those who interpret: the saddle of a sumpter-ass is pure because there isn’t a handbreadth of width, and all where there isn’t a handbreadth of width is not appropriate for sitting, and when he changed the width between the spaces, that is, that he widened the place for sitting or that he broken them into one another, and it became a place of sitting that was a handbreadth wide, it is ritually impure.



### Mishnah 4

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:4:1)


**הַמִּטָּה וְהַכַּר וְהַכֶּסֶת שֶׁל מֵת.** אַף עַל גַּב דְּמֵת אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא מִדְרָס וְהָנָךְ לַמֵּת עֲשׂוּיִין וְלֹא לֵישֵׁב עֲלֵיהֶן, אֲפִלּוּ הָכִי טְמֵאִים מִדְרָס, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַנָּשִׁים יוֹשְׁבוֹת עֲלֵיהֶן [וּמְבַכּוֹת אֶת מֵתֵיהֶן]:


המטה והכר והכסת (the bed and the mattress and the cushion) – even though that the corpse does not defile through treading, and these are made for a corpse but not to sit upon, even so, they defile through treading, because the women sit upon them [and bewail their dead] (see Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra, Chapter 2, Halakha 8).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:4:2)


**וּמַשְׁבֵּר שֶׁל חַיָּה.** מוֹשַׁב הָאִשָּׁה הַיּוֹלֶדֶת. עַל הָאָבְנַיִם (שמות א) מְתַרְגְּמִינַן עַל מַתְבְּרָא:


ומשבר של חיה (the travailing chair of the midwife) – the sitting place of the woman who is giving birth. We translate into Aramaic that of (Exodus 1:16): “[When you deliver the Hebrew women, look] at the birthstool: on the travailing chair/על מתברא.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:4:3)


**שֶׁהוּא כוֹרֵם עָלָיו.** גָּרְסִינַן. כְּלוֹמַר מְקַפֵּל וּמְתַקֵּן שָׁם אֶת הַבְּגָדִים:


שהוא כורם עליו (upon which he piles the clothes – to press them) – we have this reading. Meaning to say, that he folds and repairs there the clothing.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:4:4)


**אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֵין בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב.** וּמַתְנִיתִין דְּפִרְקִין דִּלְעֵיל דִּתְנַן כִּסֵּא שֶׁל כַּלָּה שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ חִפּוּיָו דְּמַשְׁמַע הָא לֹא נִטְּלוּ חִפּוּיָו טָמֵא, פְּלִיגָא אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:


אמר ר' יוסי אין בהן משום מושב – and our Mishnah of the chapter that is above (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 22, Mishnah 7) where it is taught: "כסא של כלה שנטלו חפויו"/”Also a chair of the bride whose seat boards have been removed” which implies that if the seat boards had not been removed it is ritually impure. This is in conflict with Rabbi Yossi. But the Halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Yossi.



### Mishnah 5

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:1)


**הַחֵרֶם.** לְשׁוֹן מְצוֹדִים וַחֲרָמִים (קהלת ז). רֶשֶׁת עֲשׂוּיָה מִחוּטִים נִקְשָׁרִים זֶה בָזֶה וּבוֹ נְקָבִים נְקָבִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁיֶּשׁ מְעַט בְּתַחְתִּית הָרֶשֶׁת שֶׁהוּא אָרוּג כְּבֶגֶד, וְקָרוּי זוּטוֹ. וְהָרֶשֶׁת כֻּלָּהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה מִפְּנֵי הָאָרוּג כְּבֶגֶד שֶׁבְּתַחְתִּיתָהּ:


החרם (the fish net) – it is the language of (Ecclesiastes 7:26): “[Now, I find woman more bitter than death;] she is all traps, [her hands are fetters and her heart is snares].” A net is made from threads that are tied one to the other, and in it are many incisions, but that there is a bit at the bottom of the net that is woven like clothing which is called זוטו/a catch, a bag-like receptacle for catch in the fisher’s net;/the solid web of the net-work (being a receptacle of solid web). And the entire net is susceptible to receiving defilement because of the webbing like clothing that is at its bottom.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:2)


**הָרְשָׁתוֹת וְהַמִּכְמָרוֹת.** מִינֵי מְצוֹדוֹת שֶׁצָּדִין בָּהֶן חַיּוֹת וְעוֹפוֹת וְדָגִים:


הרשתות והמכמרות (the nets and the traps) – kinds of traps that they hunt wild beasts, and birds and fish.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:3)


**מַדָּף.** הַצַּיָּדִין שֶׁצָּדִין עוֹפוֹת מְבִיאִין לוּחַ שֶׁל עֵץ וּמַנִּיחִים תַּחַת הַלּוּחַ חִטִּין אוֹ פְתִיתִים, וְהָעוֹף בָּא לֶאֱכֹל אוֹתָם וְנוֹפֵל הַדַּף עָלָיו וְנִתְפָּס:


מדף (clap-board, trap for birds) – the hunters that hunt birds bring a board of wood and place underneath the board [pieces of] wheat or broken pieces [of barley] , and the bird comes to eat them and the board falls upon it and it is captured.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:4)


**פְּלָצוּר.** מִין מְצוֹדָה שֶׁל עֵץ:


פלצור (a kind of snare, press) – a kind of wooden trap.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:5)


**הַסְּכָרִין.** הַסּוֹתְמִים וְסוֹכְרִים אֶת הַמַּיִם. לְשׁוֹן וַיִּסָּכְרוּ מַעְיְנוֹת תְּהוֹם (בראשית ח):


הסכרין (the skeins of the fisherman/water-locks for fishing purposes) – that close up and dam in/bar the water, it is the language of (Genesis 8:2): “The fountains of the deep [and the floodgates of the sky] were stopped up.”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:5:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:6)


**טְמֵאִים.** מְקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה אִם נָגְעוּ בְמֵת אוֹ שֶׁרֶץ:


טמאים – they are susceptible to receive defilement if the came in contact with a corpse or a reptile.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:5:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:7)


**אָקוֹן.** סַל שֶׁצָּדִים בּוֹ דָגִים:


אקון (reed basket used as a fisher’s cauf) – a basket that they hunt in it fish.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:5:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:8)


**רְטוֹב.** סַל שֶׁצָּדִים בּוֹ עוֹפוֹת:


רטוב (basket made of green twigs, used as a bird’s trap) – a basket that they hunt birds with.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 23:5:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/23:5:9)


**כְּלוּב.** עָשׂוּי מִנְּצָרִים שֶׁל עֲרָבָה קְלוּפָה אוֹ מִגֶּמִי, וְיֵשׁ חָלָל כְּאֶצְבַּע אוֹ פָחוֹת בֵּין נֵצֶר לְנֵצֶר, וּמַנִּיחִים שָׁם עוֹפוֹת. וְקוֹרִים לוֹ בְּלַעַ"ז גביא"ה. וּבַמִּקְרָא, כִּכְלוּב מָלֵא עוֹף (ירמיה ה):


כלוב (shed, coop, twisted together) – it is made from wicker of a folded willow or from reed-grass, and there is a cavity in the center, or less between each wicker, and they place birds there. And we call it GEVIAH in the foreign tongue. And in Scripture (Jeremiah 5:27): “As a cage is full of birds, [so their houses are full of guile;].”



## Chapter 24


### Mishnah 1

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:1)


**שְׁלֹשָׁה תְרִיסִין הֵן.** שְׁלֹשָׁה דִינִים חֲלוּקִין זֶה מִזֶּה יֵשׁ בִּתְרִיסִין, דְּהַיְנוּ מָגִנִּים:


שלשה תריסין הן – there are three laws divided/disputed from each other regarding shields, which are protecting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:2)


**תְּרִיס הַכָּפוּף.** הַמְּצוּיִין אֶצְלֵנוּ, שֶׁמַּקִּיפִים אֶת הָאָדָם מִשָּׁלֹשׁ רוּחוֹת:


תריס הכפוף (bent shield) – which is found with us, that surround a person from three directions.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:3)


**טָמֵא מִדְרָס.** דְּעָשׂוּי לִשְׁכִיבָה, שֶׁשּׁוֹכְבִים עָלָיו בַּמִּלְחָמָה. וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁטָּמֵא טְמֵא מֵת, דְּקַיְמָא לָן כָּל הַטָּמֵא מִדְרָס טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת:


טמא מדרס – that is made for lying, that we lie upon it during war, and all the more so, that it defiles through that which is impure through contact with a corpse, that we hold that all who are impure through treading are defiled through contact with a corpse.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:4)


**שֶׁמְּשַׂחֲקִים בּוֹ בַּקֻּמְפּוֹן.** בַּשָּׂדֶה שֶׁל עֵמֶק הַמֶּלֶךְ, בָּאִים שְׁנַיִם כָּל אֶחָד חַרְבּוֹ בְיָדוֹ וּתְרִיס קָטָן עָגֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ כָפוּף בְּיָדוֹ הַשְּׂמָאלִית, וּלְמֵדִין לְהָגֵן כָּל אֶחָד בְּמָגִנּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יַכֵּהוּ חֲבֵרוֹ. וְקוֹרִין לוֹ אשגרימ"ר בְּלַעַ"ז:


שמשחקין בו בקומפון (with which they play in the field/plain for exercise and amusement) – in the field of the king’s valley, two come, each one with his sword in his hand sand a small round shield that is not bent in his left hand, and each of them learn to defend with his shield so that his fellow doesn’t strike him. And we call it ASHGARIMER in the foreign language.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:5)


**טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת.** וְהוּא הַדִּין שֶׁטָּמֵא טֻמְאַת שֶׁרֶץ וּנְבֵלָה וּשְׁאָר טֻמְאוֹת כֻּלָּן, חוּץ מִמִּדְרָס, שֶׁאֵינוֹ נַעֲשֶׂה אַב הַטֻּמְאָה אִם שָׁכַב עָלָיו הַזָּב אוֹ יָשַׁב, אֶלָּא רִאשׁוֹן כְּמַגָּעוֹ שֶׁל זָב:


טמא טמא מת –and the same law applies when he is defiled from the defilement of a reptile or from a carrion and the rest of the defilements together, except for treading, which is not made one of the original causes of Levitical uncleanness if a person with gonorrhea lay on it or sat upon it, but rather first degree [of Levitical uncleanness] like when having contact with someone with gonorrhea.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:1:6)


**וְדִיצַת הָעַרְבִיִּין.** תְּרִיס קָטָן בְּיוֹתֵר שֶׁהָעַרְבִיִּים עוֹשִׂים לְדִיצָה וּלְשִׂמְחָה וְלִשְׂחוֹק, וְאֵינוֹ כְלִי שֶׁל תַּשְׁמִישׁ:


ודיצת הערביין (a shield used at Arabian sports) – the smallest shield that the Arabs use for dancing/rejoicing and for joy and sport, but it is not a vessel of use [and is clean of all uncleanness].



### Mishnah 2

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:2:1)


**כְּקַתֶּדְרָא.** שֶׁהִיא קְצָרָה וּמֻקֶּפֶת מִשָּׁלֹשׁ רוּחוֹת:


בקתדרא (of a throne) – which is short and surrounded from three sides.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:2:2)


**טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.** דִּמְיֻחֶדֶת לִישִׁיבָה:


טמאה מדרס – that it is designated for sitting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:2:3)


**כְּמִטָּה.** שֶׁהִיא אֲרֻכָּה וּמְיֻחֶדֶת לְהַנִּיחַ בָּהּ פְּרַקְמַטְיָא, וְהַשּׁוֹכֵב בָּהּ אוֹמְרִים לוֹ עֲמֹד וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְלַאכְתֵּנוּ:


כמטה – which is long and designated for placing on it wares/goods. And a person who lies on it, we say to him, “Stand up and let us do our work.”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:2:4)


**וְשֶׁל אֲבָנִים.** הָעֲשׂוּיָה לְהוֹלִיךְ בָּהּ אֲבָנִים:


ושל אבנים – that is made to carry stones on it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:2:5)


**טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם.** לְפִי שֶׁפְּרוּצָה מִתַּחְתִּיתָהּ נְקָבִים גְּדוֹלִים כְּמוֹצִיא רִמּוֹן:


טהורה מכלום – because it is breached from its bottom with large incisions like one that produces a pomegranate.



### Mishnah 3

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:3:1)


**שֶׁנִּסְדְּקָה טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.** דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁנִּסְדְּקָה וְאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לְלִישָׁה, מְיַחֲדִין אוֹתָהּ לִישִׁיבָה:


שנסדקה טמאה מדרס – for since it became chipped off/cut into and is not appropriate for kneading, we designate it for sitting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:3:2)


**טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת.** דִּכְלִי תַשְׁמִישׁ הִיא:


טמאה טמא מת – for it is a vessel of usage.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:3:3)


**הַבָּאָה בַמִּדָּה.** שֶׁמַּחְזֶקֶת אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה בְּלַח שֶׁהֵן כּוֹרַיִם בְּיָבֵשׁ:


הבאה במדה (holds prescribed measure) – that it holds forty Se’ah in moist which are two Kor dry.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:3:4)


**טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם.** שֶׁמִּפְּנֵי כָבְדָהּ וְגָדְלָהּ אֵינָהּ מִטַּלְטֶלֶת מְלֵאָה, וַאֲנַן דּוּמְיָא דְשַׂק בָּעִינַן דְּמִטַּלְטֵל מָלֵא וְרֵיקָן:


טהורה מכלום – that because of its heaviness and size it doesn’t carry full, but we require something similar to a sack that carries full and empty.



### Mishnah 4

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:4:1)


**תֵּבָה שֶׁפִּתְחָהּ מִצִּדָּהּ.** מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת יְשִׁיבָה עִם מְלַאכְתָּהּ, שֶׁיְּכוֹלִים לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהּ כְּשֶׁהוּא יוֹשֵׁב, בִּזְמַן שֶׁפִּתְחָהּ מִצִּדָּהּ. מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כְּשֶׁפִּתְחָהּ מִלְּמַעְלָן. וְהַבָּאָה בְמִדָּה דִתְנִינַן בְּמַתְנִיתִין שֶׁהִיא טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם, אַאֵינָהּ מְיֻחֶדֶת לְמִדְרָס קָאֵי, דְּהַטְּמֵאָה מִדְרָס אֲפִלּוּ בָאָה בְמִדָּה לְעוֹלָם הִיא טְמֵאָה:


תיבה שפתחה מצדה – it is used for sitting with its work/task, that we are able to use I when he is sitting, at the time when its opening is on its side. Which is not the case when its opening is from above. And [the words]: "הבאה במדה"/ that which holds the prescribed measure that are taught in our Mishnah that it is clean of all, refers to that it is not designated for Midras/treading uncleanness, for that which is unclean through treading – is even when it holds the prescribed measure, it is always impure.



### Mishnah 5

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:5:1)


**תַּרְבּוּסִים.** כֵּלִים שֶׁל עוֹר כְּעֵין אַרְגָּזִים:


תרבוסים (dressers/counters) – leather vessels similar to chests.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:5:2)


**שֶׁל סַפָּרִים.** מַקִּיזִים דָּם:


ספרים – who engage in blood letting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:5:3)


**טָמֵא מִדְרָס.** גָּדוֹל הוּא וַחֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה אוֹ לְמִזְגָּא עֲלֵיהּ:


טמא מדרס – it is large and appropriate for sitting or to mix wine upon it.וש


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:5:4)


**שֶׁאוֹכְלִים עָלָיו.** כְּלִי תַשְׁמִישׁ הוּא:


שאוכלים עליו – it is a vessel of usage.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:5:5)


**וְשֶׁל זֵיתִים.** שֶׁסּוֹחֲטִין בּוֹ הַזֵּיתִים, לָא חֲשִׁיב כְּלִי שֶׁל מְשַׁמְּשֵׁי אָדָם:


ושל זיתים – to press on it the olives. It is not considered a vessel for human usage.



### Mishnah 6

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:6:1)


**בְּסִיסָאוֹת.** וְאֶת כַּנּוֹ מְתַרְגְּמִינַן וְיַת בְּסִיסֵיהּ:


בסיסאות (stands) – (Exodus 30:28) “and its stand” which we translate into Aramaic as "וית בסיסיה"/and its stand.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:6:2)


**וְשֶׁל דְּלֻפְקִי.** כְּלִי עֵץ שֶׁמְּשִׂימִים בּוֹ צְלוֹחִיּוֹת וַאֲשִׁישׁוֹת וָאֳכָלִים וּמַשְׁקִים, וּמִמֶּנּוּ נוֹטְלִים וְנוֹתְנִים עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן. וְהַבָּסִיס שֶׁלְּפָנָיו אֵינוֹ לִישִׁיבָה, אֲבָל תּוֹרַת כְּלִי עָלָיו:


ושל דלפקי (delphica – a three-legged table used as a waiter or toilet table) – a wooden vessel that one places upon it flasks/bottles with a wide belly and a narrow neck and jugs and food and drinks, and from it, we take and place on the table. But the base that is in front of it is not for sitting, but it has the status of a vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:6:3)


**וְשֶׁל מִגְדָּל.** אוֹצָר שֶׁל עֵץ. ארמריא"ו בְּלַעַ"ז:


ושל מגדל (turret, cupboard) – a wooden storehouse. ARMRIAV in the foreign language.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:6:4)


**טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם.** דְּלָאו כְּלִי הוּא וְצוּרָתוֹ מוֹכַחַת עָלָיו:


טהור מכלום – it is not a vessel and its shape proves it.



### Mishnah 7

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:7:1)


**שָׁלֹשׁ פִּנְקָסִיּוֹת הֵן.** הָעֲשׂוּיִין לִכְתֹּב בָּהֶן. כְּמוֹ חֶנְוָנִי עַל פִּנְקָסוֹ:


שלש פנקסיות הן (three kinds of writing tablets) – that are made to write uppn them, like the shopkeeper on his writing tablet.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:7:2)


**אֱפִיפוֹרִין.** לוּחַ שֶׁמַּנִּיחִים עָלָיו אָבָק שֶׁל עָפָר וְכוֹתְבִים בּוֹ חֶשְׁבּוֹנוֹת. וְגָדוֹל הוּא וַחֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה:


אפיפורין (papyrus) (see Tractate Kelim, Chapter 16, Mishnah 1) – a board that they place upon it the powder of the dust and they write upon it purchases. And it is large and appropriate for sitting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:7:3)


**שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל שַׁעֲוָה.** לוּחַ שֶׁטָּחִין פָּנָיו בְּדוֹנַג וְרוֹשְׁמִין עַל הַדּוֹנַג בְּחֶרֶט:


שיש לה בית קבלו שעוה – a board that the grind its face in wax and mark on the wax with a chisel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:7:4)


**וַחֲלָקָה.** שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ שַׁעֲוָה, וְכוֹתְבִים עָלֶיהָ בִּדְיוֹ, וְאֵין לָהּ בֵּית קִבּוּל:


וחלקה (smooth one) – that has no wax on it, and they write upon it with ink, and it has no receptacle.



### Mishnah 8

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:8:1)


**שֶׁל זַגָּגִים.** שֶׁמַּנִּיחִים עָלֶיהָ כְּלֵי זְכוּכִית:


של זגגים (frame of the glass-makers used to put their wares on) – they place upon it glass vessels.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:8:2)


**סָרָגִין.** עוֹשֵׂי הַמֶּרְכָּבוֹת. בָּעֲרָבִי קוֹרִין לְמֶרְכָּב סיר"ג. וְיֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים, שֶׁמְּסָרְגִים אֶת הַשְּׂבָכוֹת. וּטְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָהּ מִמְּשַׁמְּשֵׁי אָדָם:


סרגין (frame of the netmakers) – those who make harnesses/riding seats. In Arabic they call מרכב/riding seat a SIREG. And there are those who interpret/explain that they strap (in zig-zag)/girth the lattice-work/mesh, and it is pure from everything, because it is not from what a person uses.



### Mishnah 9

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:9:1)


**מַשְׁפֵּלוֹת.** קֻפּוֹת עֲשׂוּיוֹת לְהוֹצִיא בָהֶם זְבָלִים לַשָּׂדוֹת:


משפלות (wicker baskets carried on a pole over the shoulder – see also Tractate Kelim, chapter 19, Mishnah 10) – baskets made to bring out manure to the fields.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:9:2)


**שֶׁל זֶבֶל טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.** לְפִי שֶׁרְאוּיָה לִישִׁיבָה:


של זבל טמאה מדרס – for It is appropriate for sitting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:9:3)


**וְהַפֻּחְלָץ.** עָשׂוּי כְּעֵין מִכְבָּר מַעֲשֵׂה רֶשֶׁת, וְהַנְּקָבִים שֶׁלּוֹ רְחָבִים יוֹתֵר מִמַּשְׁפֶּלֶת שֶׁל תֶּבֶן. וְאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה אֲפִלּוּ לְקַבֵּל תֶּבֶן, שֶׁנְּקָבֶיהָ רְחָבִים בְּיוֹתֵר, וְגַם אֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִישִׁיבָה, שֶׁחֲבָלִים שֶׁלָּהּ קָשִׁים וְאֵין רְאוּיִין לֵישֵׁב עֲלֵיהֶן, הִלְכָּךְ טְהוֹרָה מִכְּלוּם:


והפוחלץ (a bale made of a net of ropes with wide meshes , containing the freight of camels) – it is made similar to sieve made of netting and its incisions are wider than that of wicker baskets of straw , and it is not fit for even to receive straw, since its incisions are so wide, and it is also not fit for sitting , for its ropes are hard and they are not fit for sitting upon the, therefore they are pure from everything.



### Mishnah 10

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:10:1)


**מַפָּצִים.** כְּמִין מַחְצְלָאוֹת עֲשׂוּיוֹת מֵחִילָף וּמִסִּיב וְקָנֶה וְגֹמֶא וְגֶמִי וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן:


מפצים (mat of reeds/poor man’s mattress) – like a kind of matting made from a species of rush (so named from its sharp edges) and from fibrous substance and reed and bulrush/papyrus and similar kinds of things.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:10:2)


**וְשֶׁל צַבָּעִים.** שֶׁהַצַּבָּעִים נוֹתְנִים עֲלֵיהֶם הַבְּגָדִים:


ושל צבעים (and of dyers) – that the dyers put them upon them clothing.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:10:3)


**טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת.** שֶׁאֵינָם מְיֻחָדִים לִישִׁיבָה, אֲבָל תּוֹרַת כֵּלִים יֵשׁ לָהֶן:


טמא טמא מת – that they are not designated for sitting , but they have the status of a vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:10:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:10:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:10:4)


**וְשֶׁל גִּתּוֹת.** הָעֲשׂוּיוֹת לְכַסּוֹת בָּהֶן עֲנָבִים וְזֵיתִים:


ושל גתות (and of winepresses) – that are made to cover grapes and olives with them.



### Mishnah 11

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:11:1)


**חֲמָתוֹת.** נֹאדוֹת שֶׁל עוֹר:


חמתות (goatskins drawn off the body without opening the belly and sewed up and pitched at the ends where the legs and the tail were cut off) – leather skins.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:11:2)


**תּוּרְמְלִין.** כִּיסִין גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁל עוֹר, שֶׁהָרוֹעֶה מַנִּיחַ חֲפָצָיו לְתוֹכָן:


תורמלין (three kinds of bags – with regard to Levitical uncleanness) – large leather pouches that the shepherd places his belongings into (see also Tractate Kelim, Chapter 20, Mishnah 1).


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:11:3)


**הַמְקַבְּלִים כַּשִּׁעוּר.** הַמְפֹרָשׁ לְמַעְלָה בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כָּרִים, הַחֵמֶת שֶׁל שִׁבְעַת קַבִּים, וְהַתּוּרְמֵל שֶׁל חֲמֵשֶׁת קַבִּין. וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן אִם מַחֲזִיקִים יוֹתֵר, דְּאָז מְשַׁמְּשִׁים יְשִׁיבָה עִם מְלַאכְתָּן. אֲבָל פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן לֹא:


המקבלים כשעור (those that hold the prescribed quantity) – That is explained above at the beginning of the Chapter כרים/Mattresses (Chapter 20 of Tractate Kelim, Mishnah 1). The goatskin of seven Kab, and the shepherd’s bag of five Kab. And all the more so, if it holds more, it can be used for sitting with its work, but not with less than this.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:11:4)


**וְשֶׁל עוֹר הַדָּג טְהוֹרִים מִכְּלוּם.** דְּכָל הַבָּא מִבְּרִיּוֹת שֶׁבַּיָּם, טָהוֹר:


ושל עור הדג טהורים מכלום – for all that comes from live creatures that are in the ocean is pure.



### Mishnah 12

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:12:1)


**לְשָׁטִיחַ.** לִשְׁטֹחַ בָּאָרֶץ לֵישֵׁב עָלָיו:


לשטיח (rug) – to stretch/spread on the ground to sit upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:12:2)


**לְתַכְרִיךְ הַכֵּלִים.** לִכְרֹךְ בּוֹ אֶת הַכֵּלִים, כְּגוֹן סַכִּינִים וּמִסְפָּרַיִם וּמְחָטִים כְּדֵי לְשָׁמְרָן:


לתכריך הכלים (as a wrapper for vessels/utensils) – to wrap up the utensils,, as for example, knives and scissors and needles in order to preserve them.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:12:3)


**וְשֶׁל רְצוּעוֹת וְשֶׁל סַנְדָּלִים.** עוֹר הָעוֹמֵד לַחְתֹּךְ מִמֶּנּוּ רְצוּעוֹת וְסַנְדָּלִים, טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם, דִּמְחֻסַּר מְלָאכָה הוּא. אֲבָל רְצוּעוֹת הַמְתֻקָּנוֹת כְּבָר, טְמֵאוֹת, כִּדְמוּכָח בְּמַסֶּכֶת נְגָעִים פֶּרֶק י"א:


ושל רצועות ושל סנדלים – leather that stands to cut from it straps and sandals, is ritually pure from everything, for it is not used for work. But straps that are already prepared, are ritually impure, as is explained in Tractate Negaim, Chapter 11.



### Mishnah 13

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:13:1)


**לְוִילוֹן טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת.** הֶעָשׂוּי לְמָסָךְ לִפְנֵי הַפֶּתַח, טָמֵא, לְפִי שֶׁהַשַּׁמָּשׁ מִתְעַטֵּף בְּשׁוּלָיו לִפְעָמִים וּמִתְחַמֵּם בּוֹ:


לוילון טמא טמא מת (that is used for a curtain – is susceptible to corpse uncleanness) – that is made for a curtain/screen in front of the opening is ritually impure, because the attendant wraps himself up in its rims on occasion and warms himself in it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:13:2)


**שֶׁל צוּרוֹת.** בֶּגֶד שֶׁהוּא בְיַד רוֹקֵם וּבוֹ מִינֵי צוּרוֹת כְּדֵי לִרְאוֹת בּוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּמוֹתוֹ בְּבֶגֶד אַחֵר:


של צורות (for shapes, images) – clothing that is in the hand of the embroiderer, and there are many images in it in order to see it to make something like it in another cloth.



### Mishnah 14

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:14:1)


**שֶׁל יָדַיִם טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס.** לְפִי שֶׁפְּעָמִים נוֹתְנָהּ עַל הַכֶּסֶת וְיָשֵׁן עָלֶיהָ:


של ידים טמאה נדרס – because that sometimes they place it (i.e., the napkin) on the cushion and he sits upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:14:2)


**וְשֶׁל תַּכְרִיךְ נִבְלֵי בְנֵי לֵוִי.** שֶׁהָיוּ הַלְוִיִּים כּוֹרְכִים כְּלֵי הַשִּׁיר שֶׁלָּהֶן בְּמִטְפַּחַת. וְדֶרֶךְ שְׁאָר בְּנֵי אָדָם לַעֲשׂוֹת לָהֶן תִּיק שֶׁל עוֹר, וְאַף הֵן טְהוֹרִים:


ושל תכריך נבלי בני לוי – that the Levites would wrap their musical instruments in bands/wrappers. And it was the manner of the rest of the people to do so with a leather casing, and even they are ritually pure.



### Mishnah 15

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:15:1)


**פְּרָקְלִינִין.** צוּרַת יָד שֶׁל עוֹר שֶׁנּוֹשְׂאִים צַיָּדֵי עוֹפוֹת כְּשֶׁתּוֹפְסִים בִּידֵיהֶן הָעוֹף שֶׁקּוֹרִין אשטו"ר וְאשפרוי"ר, וּבוֹ יוֹצְאִים לָצוּד חַיָּה אוֹ עוֹף:


פרקלינין (greaves/leggings) – in the form of a hand made of leather that they carry the hunted birds when they catch the bid in their hands, that they call ASHTOR and ASHPAROIR. And with it they go out to hunt wild animals or birds.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:15:2)


**טָמֵא מִדְרָס.** לְפִי שֶׁנִּשְׁעָן עָלָיו:


טמא מדרס – because he leans upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:15:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:15:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:15:3)


**וְשֶׁל חֲגָבִים.** הַהוֹלְכִים לָצוּד חֲגָבִים וְנוֹתְנִים אוֹתָם בּוֹ:


ושל חגבים (and that of locust catchers) – those who go to hunt locusts and place them in it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:15:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:15:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:15:4)


**וְשֶׁל קוֹצִים.** לִלְקֹט קוֹצִים. וְאִית דְּגָרְסֵי שֶׁל קַיָּצִים, הַמְיַבְּשִׁים פֵּרוֹת הַקַּיִץ, כְּגוֹן הָעוֹשִׂים גְּרוֹגָרוֹת וְצִמּוּקִים בַּשָּׂדֶה:


ושל קוצים – to collect thorns. But there those who have the reading of “summer fruit,” that the summer fruit had dried, such as those who make dried figs and raisons in the field.



### Mishnah 16

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:16:1)


**סְבָכוֹת.** כִּפָּה שֶׁנּוֹשְׂאוֹת הַנָּשִׁים עַל רֹאשָׁן, עֲשׂוּיָה כְּעֵין רֶשֶׁת שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ נְקָבִים דַּקִּין:


סבכות (head-nets) – a cap that women carry on their heads, made similar to a netting that has in it thin incisions.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:16:2)


**שֶׁל יַלְדָּה.** רָאוּי לִישִׁיבָה, וּלְכָךְ טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס:


של ילדה – that is appropriate for sitting, and therefore is ritually impure through treading.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:16:3)


**שֶׁל זְקֵנָה.** מַעֲשֶׂיהָ מוֹכִיחִים עָלֶיהָ שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִישִׁיבָה. וּבַתּוֹסֶפְתָּא תַנְיָא, שֶׁל זְקֵנָה טְמֵאָה מִדְרָס, שֶׁאֵינָהּ מַקְפֶּדֶת עָלֶיהָ וּפְעָמִים יוֹשֶׁבֶת עָלֶיהָ. וְשֶׁל יַלְדָּה שֶׁמַּקְפֶּדֶת עַל כֵּלֶיהָ, אֵינָהּ יוֹשֶׁבֶת עָלֶיהָ, וּלְכָךְ טְמֵאָה טְמֵא מֵת:


ושל זקנה – her actions prove upon her that it is not fit for sitting. But in the Tosefta (Tractate Kelim Bava Batra, Chapaer 2, Halakha 10 – which teaches the reverse) it is taught that of an old woman it is susceptible for uncleanness from treading (as opposed to uncleanness from contact with a corpse), that she does not strict/particular about it and sometimes she sits upon it. But that of a young girl who is strict/particular about her vessels, does not sit upon it, and therefore it is susceptible to the impurity of contact with corpse uncleanness.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:16:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:16:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:16:4)


**וְשֶׁל יוֹצְאוֹת הַחוּץ.** סוּדָר שֶׁנּוֹתְנוֹת הַנָּשִׁים עַל רֹאשָׁן כְּשֶׁיּוֹצְאוֹת לַחוּץ. וְיֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים, יוֹצְאוֹת הַחוּץ, תַּרְגּוּם זוֹנָה נַפְקַת בָּרָא, כְּלוֹמַר סְבָכוֹת שֶׁל זוֹנוֹת:


ושל יוצאות החוץ (that of a whore) – a kerchief that women put on their heads when they go outside. But thee are those who explain/interpret "יוצאות חוץ"/as a whole. It is the Aramaic translation of a whore, a female prostitute, meaning to say, the head-dress of whores.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:16:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:16:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:16:5)


**טְהוֹרוֹת.** לְפִי שֶׁאֵינָן חֲשׁוּבוֹת כְּלִי. פֵּרוּשׁ אַחֵר, סְבָכוֹת שֶׁנִּקְרְעוּ וְרֹב שְׂעַר הָאִשָּׁה יוֹצֵא לַחוּץ, שֶׁאֵינָן מְקַבְּלוֹת רֹב שְׂעַר רֹאשָׁהּ שֶׁל אִשָּׁה:


טהורות – because they are not considered a vessel. Another explanation. Head-dresses that were torn and most of the hair of woman extends outward, for they do not hold the majority of the hair of woman’s head.



### Mishnah 17

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:1)


**מְהוּהָה.** בֶּגֶד יָשָׁן וּבָלוּי:


מהוהה (threadbare shred) – an old and worn-out cloth.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:2)


**שֶׁטְּלָיָהּ.** כְּמוֹ שֶׁטְּלָאָהּ. מִלְּשׁוֹן טְלַאי עַל גַּבֵּי טְלַאי. כְּלוֹמַר שֶׁשָּׂם הַיְשָׁנָה טְלַאי עַל הַחֲדָשָׁה:


שטלייה (that is patched) – like that is patched. From the language of patch upon patch (see Tractate Berakhot 43b), that is to say, that he placed the old shred/patch on the new one.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:3)


**הוֹלְכִים אַחַר הַבְּרִיאָה.** דָּנִין אוֹתָהּ כְּדִין הַבְּרִיאָה, אִם טְמֵאָה טְמֵאָה, וְאִם טְהוֹרָה טְהוֹרָה:


הולכים אחר הבריאה (they follow – the status in respect of uncleanness – of the sound one) – we judge it according to the law/status of the healthy one/sound one. If [that one] is impure, it is impure, but if it is pure, it is pure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:17:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:4)


**קְטַנָּה עַל הַגְּדוֹלָה.** בֵּין שְׁתֵּיהֶן מְהוּהוֹת בֵּין שְׁתֵּיהֶן בְּרִיאוֹת:


קטנה על גדולה – whether they are both threadbare shreds or both of them are sound.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:17:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:5)


**הוֹלְכִים אַחַר הַגְּדוֹלָה.** וְאִם הַגְּדוֹלָה נְקוּבָה כְמוֹצִיא רִמּוֹן שֶׁבִּשְׁבִירָה כָזוֹ נִטְהֲרָה, גַּם הַקְּטַנָּה הַמְחֻבֶּרֶת עִמָּהּ טְהוֹרָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא שְׁלֵמָה. וְאִם הַגְּדוֹלָה שְׁלֵמָה וַהֲרֵי הִיא מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה, אַף הַקְּטַנָּה הַמְחֻבֶּרֶת עִמָּהּ טְמֵאָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא נְקוּבָה בְמוֹצִיא רִמּוֹן:


הולכין אחר הגדולה – and if the larger one is perforated, like that of one which removes/emits pomegranates that that is breaking like this is purified, also the small one that is attached to it is pure, even though it is whole/complete. But if the larger one is complete, and behold it is susceptible to receive Levitical uncleanness, even the small one (i.e., patch) attached with it is impure, even though it is perforated like that which emits a pomegranate.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:17:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:6)


**הוֹלְכִים אַחַר הַפְּנִימִית.** אִם טְמֵאָה הַפְּנִימִית טְמֵאָה הַחִיצוֹנָה, וְאִם הַפְּנִימִית טְהוֹרָה הַחִיצוֹנָה נַמִּי טְהוֹרָה:


הולכים אחר הפנימית – if the inner one is ritually impure, the outer one is ritually impure, and if the inner one is ritually pure, the outer one is also ritually pure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:17:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:7)


**רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר כַּף מֹאזְנַיִם.** לְפָרוֹשֵׁי מִלְּתָא דְתַנָּא קַמָּא קָאָתֵי. וּבְכַף מֹאזְנַיִם שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת טְמֵאָה אַיְרֵי, דְּאִם טְלָאָהּ בְּתַחְתִּית הַמֵּחַם מִבִּפְנִים, טָמֵא הַמֵּחַם, וְאִם טְלָאָהּ מִבַּחוּץ, טָהוֹר הַמֵּחַם:


ר' שמעון אומר כף מאזים (Rabbi Shimon says: The cup of the balance) – it comes to explain [the words] of the first Tanna/teacher, and it is speaking of the cup of a metal balance that is ritually impure, for if one patched on the bottom of the vessel for heating water from the inside, the vessel for heating water is impure. But if he patched from the outside, the vessel for heating water is ritually pure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 24:17:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/24:17:8)


**טְלָיָהּ עַל צִדָּהּ.** שֶׁהִדְבִּיק הַטְּלַאי עַל דָּפְנוֹת הַמֵּחַם לֹא בְתַחְתִּיתוֹ, בֵּין מִבַּחוּץ בֵּין מִבִּפְנִים, טָהוֹר. וּמַסְקָנָא דְכֻלָּהּ פִּרְקִין וְטַעֲמָא דְכֻלְּהוּ טָמֵא מִדְרָס וְטָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת וְטָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם הָאֲמוּרִים כָּאן הוּא, דְּכָל דָּבָר הָרָאוּי לִשְׁכִיבָה, וְהוּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עָשׂוּי לִשְׁכִיבָה אוֹ לִישִׁיבָה אוֹ לְהִשָּׁעֵן עָלָיו, טָמֵא מִדְרָס, לְבַד אִם הוּא כְלִי חֶרֶס דְּאֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא מִדְרָס, דְּהָכִי יָלְפִינַן מִקְּרָא דִכְתִיב (ויקרא טו) וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּמִשְׁכָּבוֹ, מַקִּישׁ מִשְׁכָּבוֹ לוֹ, מַה הוּא יֵשׁ לוֹ טָהֳרָה בְמִקְוֶה אַף מִשְׁכָּבוֹ שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ טָהֳרָה בְמִקְוֶה, יָצָא כְלִי חֶרֶס שֶׁאֵין לוֹ טָהֳרָה בְמִקְוֶה. וְהַמַּפָּץ הֶעָשׂוּי לִשְׁכִיבָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ טָהֳרָה בְמִקְוֶה מִדִּכְתִיב (שם יא) כָּל כְּלִי אֲשֶׁר יֵעָשֶׂה מְלָאכָה בָהֶם בַּמַּיִם יָבֹא, וְהַאי לָאו כְּלִי הוּא, מִכָּל מָקוֹם טָמֵא מִדְרָס, דִּמְרַבִּינַן לֵיהּ מִקְּרָא דִכְתִיב כָּל הַמִּשְׁכָּב, כָּל לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הַמַּפָּץ, וְאֵין לוֹ טָהֳרָה עַד שֶׁיֵּחָתֵךְ וְיִשָּׁאֵר מִמֶּנּוּ פָּחוֹת מִשִּׁשָּׁה עַל שִׁשָּׁה. וּכְלֵי אֲבָנִים וּכְלֵי גְלָלִים וּכְלֵי אֲדָמָה, טְהוֹרִים מִכְּלוּם. וְכֵן כָּל דָּבָר הַבָּא מִן הַיָּם, טָהוֹר. וּכְלִי עֵץ הַבָּא בְמִדָּה, שֶׁמַּחֲזִיק אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה בְלַח שֶׁהֵם כּוֹרַיִם בְּיָבֵשׁ, נַמִּי טָהוֹר מִכְּלוּם, לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִטַּלְטֵל מָלֵא. וְכֵן דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו תּוֹרַת כְּלִי, אוֹ שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ תּוֹרַת כְּלִי וְאֵינוֹ מִמְּשַׁמְּשֵׁי אָדָם אֶלָּא מְשַׁמְּשֵׁי מְשַׁמְּשָׁיו, טָהוֹר, כְּגוֹן תַּרְבּוּס שֶׁל זֵיתִים וּמַפָּץ שֶׁל גִּתּוֹת וְסָדִין שֶׁל צוּרוֹת, דְּאָמְרִינַן בְּמַתְנִיתִין שֶׁהֵן טְהוֹרִין מִכְּלוּם, דְּלָא חֲשִׁיבֵי כֵלִים שֶׁל מְשַׁמְּשֵׁי אָדָם:


טלייה על צידה (if he patched it on its side) – that he attached the patch on ethe walls of the vessel for heating water, not on its bottom, whether from the outside or whether from the inside, it is ritually pure. But the upshot/final result of the entire chapter and the reason that everything is ritually impure through treading or ritually impure through contact with a corpse or pure from everything that are mentioned here, is that it and everything thing that is fit for lying, or that will be made for lying for or sitting or for sitting or for leaning upon is ritually impure through treading. Excepting if it is an earthenware vessel that does not defile by treading, and this we derive from Scripture, as it is written (Leviticus 15:5): “Anyone who touches his bedding [shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and remain impure until evening],” [The Rabbis] make an analogy between “his bedding” and himself, just as he has purity in a ritual bath/Mikveh, even his bedding has purification in a ritual bath, excluding an earthenware vessel which does not have purity in a ritual bath. But the mat of reeds/poor-man’s mattress which is made for lying, even though it doesn’t have ritual purity in a Mikveh, from what is written (Leviticus 11:32): “any such article that can be put to use shall be dipped in water,” but this is not a utensil/article, nevertheless it is impure through treading as we expand upon from Scripture as it is written (Leviticus 15:4): “Any bedding [on which the one with the discharge lies shall be impure],” [the word] “Any” includes the mat of reeds/poor-man’s mattress , but it ha no ritual purity/cleanliness until it is cut/severed and there remains from it less than six [handbreadths] by six [handbreadths]. But stone vessels and vessels of baked ordure and vessels of earth, are pure from everything. And similarly, everything that comes from the ocean is pure. And wooden vessels that hold the prescribed measurements, that contain forty Se’ah moist which are two Kor in dry, are also pure from everything, because they are not carried full. And similarly, anything which does not have the designation of a vessel, or that is the designation of a vessel but is not from things used by human beings, but are used by those who serve his users, is pure, such as the dresser in which olives are spread and the matting of winepresses and the sheet of frames, that we stated in our Mishnah that they are pure from everything, for they are not considered vessels that are attendant upon humans.



## Chapter 25


### Mishnah 1

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:1)


**כָּל הַכֵּלִים יֵשׁ לָהֶם אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ.** כֵּלִים שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ בְמַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִים, אִם נָגְעוּ הַמַּשְׁקִין מֵאֲחוֹרֵיהֶן שֶׁל כֵּלִים נִטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרֵיהֶן וְלֹא נִטְמָא תוֹכָן, מִשּׁוּם דְּטֻמְאַת מַשְׁקִים לְטַמֵּא כֵלִים לָאו דְּאוֹרַיְתָא, הֵקֵלּוּ חֲכָמִים בְּטֻמְאָתָן. אֲבָל אִם נִטְמָא תוֹכָן, כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּגְעוּ מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין בְּתוֹכָן, נִטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרֵיהֶם. וְהַיְנוּ דִתְנַן יֵשׁ לָהֶן אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ, כְּלוֹמַר שֶׁחָלוּק דִּין אֲחוֹרֵיהֶם מִדִּין תּוֹכָן:


כל הכלים יש להם אחוריים ותוך – vessels that were defiled through impure liquids, if the liquids came in contact from the vessel’s outsides, their outsides where defiled but not their insides, because the defilement of liquids to defile vessels is not from the Torah, the Sages were lenient in their defilement. But if their inside was defiled, as for example, that the impure liquids touched their insides, their outsides are also defied. And this is what is taught [in our Mishnah[“"יש להן אחוריים ותוך/“they have outsides and an inside,” meaning to say that the law of the outsides is separate from the law of the insides.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:2)


**כְּגוֹן הַכָּרִים וְהַכְּסָתוֹת.** וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בָּהֶן בְּתוֹכָן וּבַאֲחוֹרֵיהֶן, שֶׁרָאוּי לְהָפְכָן וְלַעֲשׂוֹת תּוֹכָן אֲחוֹרֵיהֶן וַאֲחוֹרֵיהֶן תּוֹכָן, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן חָלוּק דִּין תּוֹכָן מִדִּין אֲחוֹרֵיהֶן:


כגון הכרים והכסתות – and even though that we use their insides and their outsides, and that it is fit to reverse them and to make their insides outsides and their outsides insides, nevertheless, the law of their outsides is separate from the law of their insides.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:3)


**מַרְצוּפִין.** שַׂקִּין גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁל עוֹר שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִים בָּהֶן סְחוֹרוֹת בַּסְּפִינוֹת:


מרצופין (packing bags, leather bags – adapted for ship-loads) – large leather sacks that they cary in them wares on ships.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:4)


**כָּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ תוֹבְרוֹת.** לוּלָאוֹת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁיֶּשׁ לְמִכְנָסַיִם, תְּפוּרוֹת לַאֲחוֹרָיו שֶׁל בֶּגֶד:


כל שיש לו תוברות (all that have loops/hems/hangers) – loops, couplings, like that of undergarments/drawers, that are sewn on the outsides of the clothing.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:5)


**יֶשׁ לוֹ אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ.** דְּכֵיוָן דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ תוֹבְרוֹת לֹא חֲזִי לְהָפְכוֹ, וְתוֹכוֹ חָלוּק מֵאֲחוֹרָיו. אֲבָל כְּשֶׁאֵין לוֹ תוֹבְרוֹת, דַּחֲזִי לְהָפְכוֹ, אֵין תּוֹכוֹ חָלוּק מֵאֲחוֹרָיו, אֶלָּא כְשֶׁנָּגְעוּ מַשְׁקִים טְמֵאִים בֵּין מֵאֲחוֹרָיו בֵּין מִתּוֹכוֹ נִטְמָא כֻלּוֹ. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:


יש לו אחוריים ותוך – for since it has loops/couplings, it is not fit to turn inside out, and its inside is separate from its outside, but when they don’t have loops/couplings/hems, it is fit to turn them inside out, for its inside is not separate from its outside, but rather, when impure liquids came in contact with it whether from its outside or whether from its inside, everything is ritually impure/unclean. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yehuda.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:1:6)


**הַשֻּׁלְחָן וְהַדְּלֻפְקִי.** קָסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, כֵּיוָן דְּפָנָיו מְשֻׁפִּים וַחֲלָקִין, הַפָּנִים הָהֵם נִדּוֹנִים תּוֹכוֹ. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:


השלחן והדלפקי – For Rabbi Yehuda holds, since its walls are slanted and separate, their insides are judged as insides. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yehuda.



### Mishnah 2

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:2:1)
