**מַרְדֵּעַ.** הוּא מַקֵּל אָרֹךְ עָגֹל וְעָב שְׁלִישׁ טֶפַח, וּבְרֹאשׁוֹ הָאֶחָד בַּרְזֶל רָחָב מְחֻדָּד לַחְתֹּךְ בּוֹ שָׁרָשִׁים, וּשְׁמוֹ חַרְחוּר, וּבְרֹאשׁוֹ הַשֵּׁנִי בַרְזֶל כְּמוֹ מַרְצֵעַ, וּשְׁמוֹ דָרְבָן, שֶׁבּוֹ מְלַמֵּד הַפָּרָה לִתְלָמֶיהָ:


מרדע (handle of the plough-having on one end a broad iron blade/חרחור and on the other a spud/דרבן) – It is a long, round staff that is a third of a handbreadth thick. And at its one end, is a wide piece of sharpened iron to sever/cut the roots, and its name is חרחור/broad iron blade, and its other end is a piece of iron like an awl/borer, whose name is דרבן /spud/point, through which leads the heifer to its furrow/ridge.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:2:2)


**מִשִּׁבְעָה לַחַרְחוּר מֵאַרְבָּעָה לַדָּרְבָן.** אִם נָפְלוּ מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִים עַל הַחַרְחוּר, אֵין טָמֵא מִן הַמַּרְדֵּעַ אֶלָּא שִׁבְעָה טְפָחִים. וְאִם עַל הַדָּרְבָן נָפְלוּ, אֵין טָמֵא אֶלָּא אַרְבָּעָה. וְרַמְבַּ"ם פֵּרֵשׁ, שֶׁאִם נָפְלוּ מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִין בַּמַּרְדֵּעַ חוּץ לְשִׁבְעָה טְפָחִים מִן הַחַרְחוּר אוֹ חוּץ לְאַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים מִן הַדָּרְבָן, הָוֵי כִכְלִי שֶׁנִּטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרָיו וְלֹא נִטְמָא תוֹכוֹ, וְאוֹתָן שִׁבְעָה טְפָחִים הַסְּמוּכִים לַחַרְחוּר וְהָאַרְבָּעָה הַסְּמוּכִים לַדָּרְבָן לֹא נִטְמְאוּ:


משבעה לחרחור מארבעה לדרבן – if impure liquids fell upon the broad iron blade, it is not impure from the handle of the plough other than seven handbreadths, but if they fell on the spud/point, it is not impure other than four-handbreadths. But Maimonides explained/expounded, that if if impure liquids fell on the handle of the plough seven handbreadths outside from the broad iron blade or outside four handbreadths from the spuds, it is like a vessel whose outsides had been defiled, but its inside was not defiled, and those seven handbreadths that are next to the broad iron blade and the four [handbreadths] that are next to the spud were not defiled.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:2:3)


**אֶלָּא לַשְּׁיָרִים.** כְּשֶׁנָּתְנוּ חֲכָמִים שִׁעוּר לַחַרְחוּר שִׁבְעָה וְלַדָּרְבָן אַרְבָּעָה, לֹא נָתְנוּ אֶלָּא לְעִנְיָן זֶה שֶׁאִם נִשְׁבַּר הַמַּרְדֵּעַ וְנִשְׁאַר סָמוּךְ לַחַרְחוּר שִׁבְעָה טְפָחִים אוֹ סָמוּךְ לַדָּרְבָן אַרְבָּעָה, טָמֵא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרָאוּי לַעֲשׂוֹת מֵעֵין מְלַאכְתּוֹ. פָּחוֹת מִכָּאן, הָוֵי כְשִׁבְרֵי כְלִי וְטָהוֹר. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:


אלא לשיריים – when the Sages gave measurements for the broad iron blade of seven [handbreadths] and for the spud four [handbreadths], it was not given other than regarding this matter that if the handle of the plough was broken and there remained next to/adjacent to the broad iron blade seven handbreadths, or adjacent to the spud four [handbreadths, it is impure, because it is appropriate to do some kind of its work. Less than this, it is like the shards of a vessel and is pure. But the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yehuda.



### Mishnah 3

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:3:1)


**זוֹמָא לִסְטְרָא.** כְּלִי שֶׁרֹאשׁוֹ אֶחָד כַּף וְרֹאשׁוֹ הָאַחֵר מַזְלֵג. בַּכַּף מַעֲלִין בּוֹ מָרָק מִן הַקְּדֵרָה וּבַמַּזְלֵג מַעֲלִין בּוֹ בָשָׂר:


זומא ליסארא (soup-ladle, with a spoon on one side and a fork on the other) – a vessel that on one head is a spoon and the other head is a fork; with the spoon one raises the soup from the bowl, and with the fork one lifts with it the meat.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:3:2)


**רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אֵין לָהֶם.** אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ. טַעֲמָא דְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מִשּׁוּם דְּכָל הָנֵי כֵלִים יֵשׁ מֵאֲחוֹרֵיהֶן חֲקָק בֵּית מוֹשָׁב כְּעֵין שֶׁעוֹשִׂים לִכְלֵי כֶסֶף, וּפְעָמִים שֶׁכּוֹפֵהוֹ עַל פִּיו וּמִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בַּחֲקָק שֶׁבַּאֲחוֹרָיו:


ר' יהודה אומר אין להם – an outside and inside. The reasoning of Rabbi Yehuda, because that all of these vessels have on their outsides engraved a receptacle similar to what they do for a silver vessel, and sometimes, that they bend it on its opening and use the hollowed out area on the backside.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:3:3)


**רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר יֶשׁ לָהֶם.** לְעִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹךְ הַכְּלִי יֵשׁ לָהֶן דִּין אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ, שֶׁאִם נִטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרָיו לֹא נִטְמָא מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹךְ הַכְּלִי. אֲבָל לְעִנְיַן הַכְּלִי עַצְמוֹ אֵין חִלּוּק דִּין אֲחוֹרָיו מִדִּין תּוֹכוֹ, שֶׁאִם נִטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרָיו צָרִיךְ לְהַטְבִּיל אֶת כֻּלּוֹ כְאִלּוּ נִטְמָא תּוֹכוֹ. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:


ר' שמעון אומר יש להם – regarding the matter of what is inside the vessel, they have the law of outside and inside, for if its outsides were defiled, what was inside the vessel was not defiled But reading the matter of the vessel itself, there is no separation of the law of its outside from the law of its inside, for if the outsides had been defiled, one must immerse all of it [In a Mikveh] as if the inside was defiled. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yehuda.



### Mishnah 4

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:4:1)


**הָרֹבַע וַחֲצִי הָרֹבַע.** כְּגוֹן חֲתִיכַת עֵץ עָבָה וַאֲרֻכָּה וּבוֹ שְׁתֵּי מִדּוֹת חֲקוּקוֹת זוֹ אֵצֶל זוֹ, אֶחָד מַחֲזִיק רֹבַע וְאֶחָד מַחֲזִיק חֲצִי רֹבַע, וְדֹפֶן מַפְסִיק בֵּין זוֹ לְזוֹ:


הרובע וחצי רוצע – as for example, a piece of wood that is thick and long, and it has two measurements engraved one next to the other, one holds a quarter and the other holds half-a quarter, and there is a wall that separates between this one and that one.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:4:2)


**כְּלִי שֶׁנִּטְמָא תוֹכוֹ.** בִּתְמִיהָה. וְכִי כְלִי שֶׁנִּטְמָא תוֹכוֹ לֹא נִטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרָיו, וְאַמַּאי תְּנַן לֹא נִטְמָא חֲצִי רֹבַע, וַהֲלֹא אֲחוֹרָיו שֶׁל רֹבַע הִיא:


כלי שנטמא תוכו – in astonishment! For if a vessel whose inside was defiled, its outsides were not defiled., but why does it teach in the Mishnah that one-half of the quarter was not defiled? For isn’t its outside the quarter?


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:4:3)


**[שֶׁלֹּווֹת] קוֹדְמִין הִיא.** כָּל אַחַת מֵהֶן לָוְתָה הַקְּדִימָה מֵחֲבֶרְתָּהּ, כְּלוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם קְדִימָה זוֹ עַל זוֹ. וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁאַתָּה אוֹמֵר שֶׁחֲצִי רֹבַע אֲחוֹרַיִם לָרֹבַע, כָּךְ תֹּאמַר שֶׁהָרֹבַע אֲחוֹרַיִם לַחֲצִי רֹבַע, וּכְשֶׁנִּטְמָא הָרֹבַע, אֲחוֹרָיו שֶׁל חֲצִי רֹבַע נִטְמְאוּ וְלֹא תוֹכוֹ. וְגִרְסַת רַבּוֹתַי, שֶׁל כַּת קוֹדְמִים הִיא, לְפִי שֶׁכִּתּוֹת שֶׁל תַּלְמִידִים הָיוּ יוֹשְׁבִים לְפָנָיו שׁוּרוֹת, אָמַר לָהֶם שְׁאֵלָה זוֹ כְּבָר שְׁאָלוּהָ מִמֶּנִּי הַכַּת שֶׁל תַּלְמִידִים יוֹשְׁבִים בַּשּׁוּרָה הַקּוֹדֶמֶת, וְכָךְ הֵשַׁבְתִּי לָהֶם אוֹ שֶׁמָּא וְכוּ':


[שלות] קודמין היא (is this the class of those that takes precedence?) – each one of them, takes precedence over its partner, meaning to say, that none has precedence over the other. And just as you say that one-half of a quarter of its backsides to a quarter, so you should say that the quarter is backsides to one-half of quarter. And when the quarter is defiled, its backside of the one-half quarter is defiled but not its insides. But the reading of my teachers/Rabbis is that each group/band takes precedence, because the groups of the students would sit before him (i.e., the teacher) in rows, he asked to them this question already which was asked of me by the group of students that sits in the first row, and such is how I responded them, or perhaps [the quarter’s backside to the half-quarter], etc.



### Mishnah 5

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:5:1)


**הָרֹבַע וַאֲחוֹרָיו טְמֵאִים.** הָרֹבַע הַיְנוּ תוֹכוֹ, וַאֲחוֹרָיו הַיְנוּ הַדְּפָנוֹת הַמַּקִּיפוֹת אֶת הָרֹבַע מִבַּחוּץ. אֲבָל דֹּפֶן הַמַּפְסִיק בֵּין שְׁנֵיהֶם, בִּכְלַל תּוֹכוֹ שֶׁל חֲצִי רֹבַע, וְטָהוֹר צַד שֶׁכְּלַפֵּי חֲצִי רֹבַע. וְכֵן כְּשֶׁנִּטְמָא חֲצִי הָרֹבַע, חֲצִי רֹבַע וַאֲחוֹרָיו טְמֵאִין. חֲצִי הָרֹבַע הַיְנוּ תוֹכוֹ, וַאֲחוֹרָיו הַיְנוּ דְפָנוֹת הַמַּקִּיפוֹת חֲצִי הָרֹבַע מִבַּחוּץ, וְדֹפֶן הַמַּפְסִיק, צַד שֶׁל כְּלַפֵּי הָרֹבַע בִּכְלַל תּוֹכוֹ שֶׁל רֹבַע:


הרובע ואחוריו טמאים – the quarter – that is the inside. And the backsides are the walls that surround the quarter from outside. But the wall that forms a partition between both of them, is included in the inside of the half-quarter, and it is pure to the side that is towards the one-half quarter. And similarly, when the one-half quarter is defiled, the half-quarter and its outsides are impure. The half-quarter is the insides, and the outsides are the walls that surround that half-quarter from the outside, but the wall that forms a partition, the side that is towards the quarter is included with the inside of the quarter.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:5:2)


**נִטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרֵי הָרֹבַע.** הַיְנוּ דְפָנוֹת הַמַּקִּיפוֹת מִבַּחוּץ:


נטמאו אחורי הרובע – that is, the walls that surround from the outside.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:5:3)


**אֵין חוֹלְקִין אֶת הַגַּבָּיִים.** הַיְנוּ הָאֲחוֹרַיִם, וְכָל הָאֲחוֹרַיִם טְמֵאִין כְּשֶׁנִּטְמָא אֶחָד מִן הָאֲחוֹרַיִם:


אין חולקין את הגביים (they do not divide the hind parts/outside parts [of the utensil] – that is the outside parts, for all the outside parts are impure when one of the outside parts became impure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:5:4)


**מַטְבִּיל אֶת כֻּלּוֹ.** רֹבַע וַחֲצִי רֹבַע. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר. וְדִין דֹּפֶן הָאֶמְצָעִי מְפֹרָשׁ לְעֵיל בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק ב', דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר חוֹלְקִין אֶת עָבְיוֹ, הַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ לַטָּמֵא טָמֵא וְהַמְשַׁמֵּשׁ לַטָּהוֹר טָהוֹר:


מטביל את כולו – the quarter and one-half of the quarter. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Meir. And the law of the middle wall is explained above at the end of Chapter Two (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 2, Mishnah 7) for “Rabbi Yohanan ben Nuri says: They divide its thickness. The [half that] serves the unclean [portion] is unclean; the [half that] serves the clean [part] is clean.”



### Mishnah 6

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:1)


**כַּנֵּי הַכֵּלִים.** בְּסִיסֵי הַכֵּלִים. לְשׁוֹן וְאֶת כַּנּוֹ, דִּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן וְיַת בְּסִיסֵיהּ:


כני הכלים – the bases of the vessels. The phrase (Exodus 30:28): “and its stand,” we translate into Aramaic, “and its base.”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:2)


**וְהוֹגְנֵיהֶן.** כְּמוֹ וְאָגְנֵיהֶן, כְּלוֹמַר שִׂפְתוֹתֵיהֶן:


והוגניהן – just likeואוגניהן /its border, that is to say, its rim.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:3)


**וְאָזְנֵיהֶן.** מָקוֹם שֶׁתּוֹחֲבִין בּוֹ הַבֵּית יָד:


ואזניהן (its hangers) – the place where they insert a handle in it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:4)


**הַמְקַבְּלִין.** שֶׁיֶּשׁ לָהֶן תּוֹךְ:


המקבלין – that have an inside.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:6:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:5)


**מְנַגְּבָן וְהֵן טְהוֹרִין.** דְּלָא חֲשִׁיבֵי הָנֵי חִבּוּר לְהָבִיא טֻמְאַת מַשְׁקִין לִכְלִי שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל, וְסַגִּי בְנִגּוּב. אֲבָל לִכְלִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ תוֹךְ בָּעֵי טְבִילָה:


מנגבן והן טהורין – and these are not considered attached to bring the defilement of liquids for a vessel that has a receptacle. And drying is enough. But for a vessel that does not have an inside, it requires ritual immersion.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:6:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:6:6)


**וְאָזְנָיו וְיָדָיו טְהוֹרִין.** עֲבַדוּ רַבָּנָן בֵּיהּ הֶכֵּרָא, כִּי הֵיכִי דְלָא לִשְׂרֹף עֲלַיְהוּ תְרוּמָה וְקָדָשִׁים. וְדַוְקָא בַתְּרוּמָה עֲבַדוּ הֶכֵּרָא, אֲבָל לֹא בַקָּדָשִׁים, כְּדִתְנַן לְקַמָּן בְּפִרְקִין:


ואזניו וידיו טהורין – The Rabbis made this for recognition, for just as/in order that it won’t burn upon them heave-offering [for the Kohanim] and Holy Things, especially, it was made as a recognition for Terumah/heave-offering, but not for Holy Things, as is taught in the Mishnah further on in our chapter (see Mishnah 9).



### Mishnah 7

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:7:1)


**בֵּית הַצְּבִיטָה.** גָּרְסִינַן. מָקוֹם שֶׁאוֹחֲזִין הַכְּלִי כְּשֶׁמּוֹשִׁיטִין אוֹתוֹ מִזֶּה לָזֶה. לְשׁוֹן וַיִּצְבֹּט לָהּ קָלִי (רות ב) שֶׁפֵּרוּשׁוֹ וַיּוֹשֶׁט. וְאִית דְּגָרְסֵי, בֵּית הַצְּבִיעָה, מָקוֹם שֶׁאוֹחֵז בּוֹ בְאֶצְבָּעוֹ:


בית הצביטה (that part of the vessel by which it is seized, handle, neck, cavity for the fingers) – We have the reading [בית הצביטה ] )whereas the Mishnah has the reading of "בית הצביעה"). It is the place where we hold the vessel, when we move it to and fro. It is the language of (Ruth 2:14): “He (i.e., Boaz) handed her roasted grain, [and she ate her fill and had some left over],” whose meaning is that he handed to her. And there are those who have the reading "בית הצביעה", the place where one holds it with his finger.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:7:2)


**וְיֵשׁ לָהֶן בֵּית הַצְּבִיטָה.** שֶׁאִם נִטְמְאוּ אֲחוֹרָיו, בֵּית הַצְּבִיטָה טָהוֹר. וְאִם נִטְמָא בֵּית הַצְּבִיטָה, אֲחוֹרָיו טְהוֹרִין:


ויש להן בית צביטה – if the backsides were defiled, the place of the handle is ritually pure. But if the handle became defiled, its backsides are ritually pure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:7:3)


**לַעֲרֵבָה גְדוֹלָה שֶׁל עֵץ.** יֵשׁ לָהּ בֵּית צְבִיטָה. אֲבָל לִשְׁאָר כֵּלִים, לֹא. שֶׁבַּעֲרֵבָה גְדוֹלָה יֵשׁ הֶפְרֵשׁ בֵּין בֵּית הַצְּבִיטָה לָאֲחוֹרַיִם, שֶׁאִם יֵשׁ מַשְׁקִים בַּאֲחוֹרֵי הָעֲרֵבָה וְיָדָיו טְמֵאוֹת, אוֹחֵז בְּבֵית הַצְּבִיטָה וְאֵין חוֹשֵׁשׁ שֶׁמָּא יִגַּע בַּמַּשְׁקִין שֶׁבַּאֲחוֹרָיו וְיַחְזְרוּ וִיטַמְּאוּ אֶת הָעֲרֵבָה:


לערבה גדולה של עץ [(the distinction in the outer parts applies] only in a large wooden trough) – it has a part of the vessel by which it is seized. But not with the rest of the vessels. That the large trough has a separation between the place where it is seized and its backsides, that if there are liquids on the backsides of the trough and his hands are impure, he holds on to the part of the vessel by which it is seized, and he doesn’t worry lest he come in contact with the liquids on its backside, and once again defile the trough.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:7:4)


**רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר לְכוֹסוֹת.** אַף לְכוֹסוֹת יֵשׁ לָהֶן בֵּית צְבִיטָה:


ר' עקיבא אומר לכוסות – even for cups they have a place where he grabs hold of the vessel.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:7:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:7:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:7:5)


**לְיָדַיִם הַטְּמֵאוֹת וְהַטְּהוֹרוֹת.** יֵשׁ הֶפְרֵשׁ בֵּין בֵּית הַצְּבִיטָה לָאֲחוֹרַיִם, לְיָדַיִם הַטְּמֵאוֹת כִּדְפָרֵישִׁית, וְלִטְהוֹרוֹת כְּדִמְפָרֵשׁ לְקַמָּן כֵּיצַד. וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לְיָדַיִם טְהוֹרוֹת בִּלְבַד לֹא חָיְשִׁינַן, אֲבָל לְיָדַיִם טְמֵאוֹת חָיְשִׁינַן. וַהֲלָכָה כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא וּכְדִמְפָרֵשׁ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:


לידים הטמאות והטהורות – there is a distinction between the place where one grabs hold of the vessel and its backsides, for impure hands, as has been explained. But for pure hands, it is as it explains further on how so (see the next Mishnah). But Rabbi Yossi holds that for pure hands alone we should not be concerned, but for impure hands, we should be concerned. And the Halakha is according to the first Tanna/teacher, as Rabbi Yossi explains.



### Mishnah 8

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:8:1)


**הָיוּ יָדָיו טְהוֹרוֹת.** וַעֲלֵיהֶם מַשְׁקֶה טוֹפֵחַ:


היו ידיו טהורות – and upon them was dripping liquid.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:8:2)


**אֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ שֶׁמָּא נִטְמְאוּ.** מַשְׁקִין שֶׁעַל יָדָיו בַּאֲחוֹרֵי הַכּוֹס וְיַחְזְרוּ וִיטַמְּאוּ אֶת הַיָּדַיִם:


אינו חושש שמא נטמאו – that liquid that was on his hands [were defiled] on the outside of the cup and will return and defile the hands.



### Mishnah 9

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:9:1)


**אֵין לָהֶם אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ.** דְּהַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּאֶחָד מֵהֶן כְּנוֹגֵעַ בְּכֻלּוֹ. וְיֵשׁ לָהֶן אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ דִּתְנַן לְעֵיל, דַּוְקָא לִתְרוּמָה:


אין להם אחוריים ותוך – that a person who comes in contact with [a Holy Vessel] is like one who comes in contact with all of it. And they do have an outside and an inside as is taught in the Mishnah above (see Mishnah 7 of this chapter), and especially for heave-offering [for the Kohanim].


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:9:2)


**וְאֵין מַטְבִּילִין כֵּלִים לְתוֹךְ כֵּלִים.** כְּשֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם טְמֵאִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁכָּבְדוֹ שֶׁל כְּלִי חוֹצֵץ. וְחָשׁוּ לְקֹדֶשׁ יוֹתֵר מִבַּתְּרוּמָה:


ואין מטבילין כלים לתוך כלים – when both of them are ritually impure, because of the heaviness of an interposing vessel. And they were worried/concerned about Holy Things more than with the heave-offering.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:9:3)


**יוֹרְדִים לִידֵי טֻמְאָתָן בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה.** כְּגוֹן טַבַּעַת בְּהֵמָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה, חָשַׁב עָלֶיהָ לִתְּנָהּ בְּאֶצְבַּע אָדָם, מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה מִכָּאן וָאֵילָךְ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ. אֲבָל טַבַּעַת אָדָם שֶׁחָשַׁב עָלֶיהָ לִתְּנָהּ לִבְהֵמָה, לְעוֹלָם הִיא מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה, עַד שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה בָהּ שִׁנּוּי מַעֲשֶׂה לְשַׁנּוֹת צוּרָתָהּ:


יורדים לידי טומאתן במחשבה (see also Tractate Kelim, Chapter 12, Mishnah 1) as for example, the ring of an animal is not susceptible to receive ritual defilement, if he thought to place it on the finger of a person, it receives ritual defilement from here onwards by this thought. But, the ring of a person that he thought about to give it to an animal, it always is susceptible to receive ritual defilement, until he performs a change of action to change its form.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 25:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/25:9:4)


**וּמַחֲשָׁבָה אֵינָהּ מְבַטֶּלֶת לֹא מִיַּד מַעֲשֶׂה וְלֹא מִיַּד מַחֲשָׁבָה.** אִם לְאַחַר שֶׁחָשַׁב עַל טַבַּעַת בְּהֵמָה לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ לָאָדָם, שֶׁהִיא מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה בְמַחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ, חָזַר וְחָשַׁב עָלֶיהָ לְהַחְזִירָהּ לַבְּהֵמָה, אֵין מַחֲשָׁבָה זוֹ הַשְּׁנִיָּה מַעֲלָה מִידֵי טֻמְאָה שֶׁיָּרְדָה לָהּ בַּמַּחֲשָׁבָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה:


ומחשבה אינה מבטלת לא מיד מעשה ולא מיד מחשבה – if after he thought about the ring of an animal to make it for a person that it is susceptible to receive ritual impurity though this thought, he retracted and thought about returning it to the animal, this second thought does not lift it from the status of defilement that it descended to in the first thought.



## Chapter 26


### Mishnah 1

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:1:1)


**סַנְדָּל עִמְקִי.** סַנְדָּלִים הַנַּעֲשׂוֹת בִּכְפַר עִמְקִי:


סנדל עמקי (sandals worn in valleys) – Sandals that are made in a valley village.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:1:2)


**כִּיס שֶׁל שְׁנָצוֹת.** כְּמִין רְצוּעוֹת תְּחוּבוֹת בְּלוּלָאוֹת בִּשְׂפַת הַכִּיס וּמוֹשְׁכִים אוֹתָן אֵילָךְ וָאֵילָךְ וְהַכִּיס נִסְגָּר מֵאֵלָיו:


כיס של שנצות (a bag which is closed by means of laces) – like a species of straps inserted in loops at the rim of the pouch and we pull them this way and that and the pouch/bag is closed from itself.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:1:3)


**כְּפִיפָה מִצְרִית.** סַל עָשׂוּי מִצּוּרֵי הַדֶּקֶל. מְבִיאִין נְצָרִים וְהוּצִין וְקוֹרְעִין אוֹתָן וְעוֹשִׂים מֵהֶן כְּמִין חוּטִין וְעוֹשִׂין מֵהֶן כְּפִיפָה וַחֲבָלִים:


כפיפה מצרית (an Egyptian basket made of palm twigs) – a basket made from the bands made of palm-bark. They bring willows and palm-leaves and tear them and make from them threads and make from them a basket of osier and rope.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:1:4)


**סַנְדָּל לָדִיקִי.** סַנְדָּל שֶׁעוֹשִׂים אַנְשֵׁי לָדִיקְיָא:


סנדל לדיקי (a Laodicean sandal) – that the people of Laodicea make.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:1:5)


**הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מִטַּהֲרִין וּמִטַּמְּאִין שֶׁלֹּא בְאֻמָּן.** מִשּׁוּם דְּכָל הָנֵי יֵשׁ לָהֶן רְצוּעוֹת וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְקָשְׁרָן, אֶלָּא מוֹתֵחַ בָּרְצוּעוֹת וְהֵן נִסְגָּרִים מֵאֲלֵיהֶן, וְכֵן נִפְתָּחִין מֵאֲלֵיהֶן עַל יְדֵי רְצוּעוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת שֶׁמּוֹשֵׁךְ בָּהֶן, כְּעֵין שֶׁעוֹשִׂין לְכִיסִין בִּמְקוֹמֵנוּ. וְאִם הֻתְּרוּ אוֹתָן הָרְצוּעוֹת דְּשׁוּב אֵין רְאוּיִין לִסְגֹּר וְלִפְתֹּחַ, טְהוֹרִים. וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהֵן מֻתָּרִים, טְמֵאִין, כֵּיוָן דְּהֶדְיוֹט יָכוֹל לְהַחְזִירָם. חוּץ מִן הַכְּפִיפָה, דְּאַף הָאֻמָּן אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַחְזִירָם. וַהֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:


הרי אלו מיטהרין ומיטמאין שלא באומן – because all of thee have straps and there is no need to tie them, but he stretches them and they are closed from on their own, and similarly, they open from on their own through other straps that pull them. Like the kind that they make for purses in our places. But if those straps were left over, then they are further not appropriate to close and open with, they are pure. But Rabbi Yossi holds that even though they are permitted, they are impure, since a non-specialist can restore them. Except for the basket of osier, for even the artisan is not able to restore them. And the Halakha is according to Rabbi Yossi.



### Mishnah 2

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:1)


**שֶׁנִּטְּלוּ שְׁנָצָיו.** לְרַבָּנָן מַיְרֵי שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלוּ לְגַמְרֵי אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּתְּקוּ מִן הַלּוּלָאוֹת וַעֲדַיִן תְּלוּיוֹת בַּכִּיס. וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֲפִלּוּ נִטְּלוּ לְגַמְרֵי, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֶדְיוֹט יָכוֹל לְהַחְזִירָם:


שניטלו שנציו (whose laces were removed) – to the Rabbis, we are speaking about that they were not removed completely, but rather that torn loose from the loops, and are still hanging in the bag. But according to Rabbi Yossi, even if they were removed completely, because a non-specialist is able to restore them.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:2)


**נִפְשַׁט.** הַכִּיס וְנַעֲשָׂה כְּמִין עוֹר חָלָק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל, טָהוֹר:


נפשט(when it – the bag – is straightened out – so as to be a plain piece of leather) – the bag and it became like a kind of smooth piece of leather that has no receptacle, it is pure.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:3)


**טָלָה עָלָיו מַטְלִית.** נָתַן בְּשׁוּלָיו טְלַאי, כְּלוֹמַר חֲתִיכָה קְטַנָּה שֶׁל עוֹר חִבֵּר בּוֹ מִלְּמַטָּה, דְּדֶרֶךְ הַכִּיסִים מַכְנִיסִים עוֹר קָטָן בֵּין הַתְּפִירָה וּכְשֶׁפּוֹשְׁטוֹ נִשְׁאָר אוֹתוֹ הָעוֹר וְלֹא בָטַל קִבּוּלוֹ:


טלה עליו את המטלת (if he underlined the bag with a patch on the bottom) – he placed a patch on its rim, that is to say, a small piece of leather that he attached to it from the bottom, for the it is the manner of bags to bring in a small piece of leather between the stitches and when he stretches it out, the the leather remains and it does not annul its receptacle.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:4)


**לֹא נִטְמָא חֲבֵרוֹ.** דְּטֻמְאַת מַשְׁקִין לְטַמֵּא כֵלִים לָאו דְּאוֹרַיְתָא וְלָא חֲשִׁיב חִבּוּר:


לא נטמא חברו – for defilement by liquids to defile vessels is not according to the Torah and is not considered an attachment.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:2:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:5)


**צְרוֹר הַמַּרְגָּלִית.** מַנִּיחִין מַרְגָּלִית בְּתוֹךְ עוֹר לִהְיוֹת שְׁמוּרָה שָׁם וְקוֹשְׁרִים אוֹתוֹ, וּכְשֶׁמּוֹצִיאִין הַמַּרְגָּלִית נִשְׁאָר הָעוֹר כְּמוֹ כִיס עַד שֶׁיִּטְרַח וִיפַשֵּׁט, מֵחֲמַת אוֹתָהּ מַרְגָּלִית שֶׁעָמְדָה יָמִים רַבִּים וְנִצְרַר:


צרור המרגלית (a piece of leather in which jewels are bound up) – they place the pearl within the leather to be protected there and they tie it, and when they remove the pearl, the leather remains like a bag until one goes to the trouble and straightens it out [by stretching it] , on account of that pearl that stood for many days and was tied up.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:2:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:2:6)


**צְרוֹר הַמָּעוֹת.** כְּמוֹ צְרוֹר הַמַּרְגָּלִית. וְטַעֲמָא דִצְרוֹר הַמַּרְגָּלִית מִטַּמֵּא טְפֵי, מִשּׁוּם דְּדֶרֶךְ צְרוֹר הַמַּרְגָּלִית לַעֲמֹד יוֹתֵר מִצְּרוֹר הַמָּעוֹת, שֶׁצְּרוֹר הַמָּעוֹת רְגִילִים לְהַתִּיר תָּמִיד, מִשּׁוּם דִּלְהוֹצָאָה נִתְּנוּ. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


צרור המעות (a piece of leather in which money is bound up) – like the piece of leather in which jewels are bound up. And the reason that the piece of leather in jewels is bound up defiles more, because it is the manner of the piece of leather in which jewels are bound up to stand more than the piece of leather in which money is bound up, for the piece of leather in which money is bound up is loosened all the time, because it was given for spending. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.



### Mishnah 3

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:1)


**כַּף לוֹקְטֵי קוֹצִים.** כְּמִין כַּף יָד שֶׁל עוֹר תּוֹפְשִׂים מְלַקְּטֵי קוֹצִים בִּידֵיהֶן, שֶׁלֹּא יְנֻקְּבוּ יְדֵיהֶן בַּקּוֹצִים:


כף לוקטי קוצים (glove of thorn pickers) – like a kind of leather hand-glove that thorn pickers catch in their hands, so that they don’t puncture their hands with thorns.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:2)


**טְהוֹרָה.** דְּאֵינָהּ עֲשׂוּיָה לְקַבָּלָה:


טהורה – that it is not made for receiving.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:3)


**הַזּוֹן.** אֵזוֹר כְּמִין אַבְנֵט. וּבִלְשׁוֹן יְוָנִי קוֹרִין לַחֲגוֹר זונ"י:


הזון (girdle, laborer’s apron) – a girdle/belt like a kind of belt. And in the Greek language, we call this belt ZONI.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:4)


**בִּרְכְּיָר.** דְּפוּס שֶׁל עוֹר נָתוּן עַל הַבִּרְכַּיִם, כְּדֵי שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לַעֲמֹד עַל בִּרְכֵּיהֶן:


ברכייר (brick-layer’s cushion – on which he kneels at work; stone-setter’s knee-band) – a leather frame that is placed on the knees, in order that they would be able to stand on their knees.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:5)


**טְמֵאִים.** דַּעֲשׂוּיִים לְקַבָּלָה:


טמאין – for they are made for reception.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:6)


**שַׁרְווּלִים.** כְּמִין בֵּית יָד שֶׁל עוֹר דָּחוּק וָצַר שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים בַּעֲלֵי אֻמָּנוּת בִּזְרוֹעוֹתֵיהֶן, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִפְּלוּ בִגְדֵיהֶן הָרְחָבִים עַל יָדָן וִיבַטְּלוּ אוֹתָן מִמְּלַאכְתָּן:


שרוולים (workingman’s leather sleeve/chest protector in hot weather) – like a kind of pressed leather narrow handle that artisans place on their arms, in order that their wide clothing will not fall on their hands and annul them from their work.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:3:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:7)


**פְּרַקְמִינִין.** גָּרְסִינַן. וְהוּא דָּבָר שֶׁמְּחַתֵּל וְקוֹשֵׁר בּוֹ פַדַּחְתּוֹ:


פרקמינין (greaves, leggings) – we have the reading [פרקמינין] and it is a thing that wraps up/bandages and ties up his forehead.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:3:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:8)


**בֵּית אֶצְבָּעוֹת.** כְּמִין יָד שֶׁל עוֹר עָשׂוּי לְהַכְנִיס אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו לְתוֹכוֹ:


בית אצבעות (finger holes) – like a kind of leather hand made to put in his fingers into it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:3:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:9)


**קַיָּצִין.** מְלַקְּטֵי קוֹצִים. פֵּרוּשׁ אַחֵר, מְלַקְּטֵי פֵרוֹת הַקַּיִץ:


קייצין – those who pick thorns. Another explanation, those who pick the summer fruit.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:3:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:3:10)


**הָאוֹג.** פְּרִי אָדוֹם הַמָּצוּי בָּאִילָן שֶׁגָּדֵל בַּיַּעַר מֵאֵלָיו. וּפְעָמִים שֶׁהַמְלַקְּטִים קוֹצִים בַּיְעָרִים מְלַקְּטִים הָאוֹג וְנוֹתְנִים אוֹתוֹ בְּבֵית אֶצְבָּעוֹת, נִמְצָא שֶׁהוּא עָשׂוּי לְקַבָּלָה:


האוג (red berry of the Venus’ summachtree) – a red fruit that is found on a tee that grows in the forest on its own. And sometimes when they pick the thorns in the forests, they pick the red berry of the Venus’ summachtree and they place it in the finger-holes, as it is found that it is made for reception.



### Mishnah 4

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:1)


**וְתִקְּנָהּ טָמֵא מִדְרָס.** עֲדַיִן עוֹמֵד בְּטֻמְאָתוֹ, כֵּיוָן דְּאֹזֶן שְׁנִיָּה קַיְמָא:


ותקנה טמאה מדרס – it still stands in its defilement, because the second strap/handle exists.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:2)


**טָהוֹר מִן הַמִּדְרָס.** אַף עַל פִּי דְּנִתַּקְּנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה קֹדֶם שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה שְׁנִיָּה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם טָהוֹר, דְּפָנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת בָּאוּ לְכָאן, שֶׁלְּאַחַר שֶׁיָּרְדָה לָהּ טֻמְאַת מִדְרָס נִתְחַדְּשׁוּ לָהּ פָּנִים הַלָּלוּ, וְאֵין זוֹ הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מֵאַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְקַלְקֵל בָּהּ כְּדֵי בִּטּוּלָהּ:


טהור מן המדרס – even though the first one was repaired prior to the second one breaking, nevertheless, it is pure, for new faces came to here, for after it went down into defilement by treading, these faces were renewed, and this is not the first after it already had ben ruined in order to annul it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:3)


**אֲבָל טָמֵא מַגַּע מִדְרָס.** מִשּׁוּם דְּאֹזֶן רִאשׁוֹנָה כְּשֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה וְתִקְּנָהּ שֶׁהֵבִיא אֹזֶן אַחֶרֶת תַּחַת הַשְּׁבוּרָה וְחִבְּרָהּ לַסַּנְדָּל, נִטְמֵאת מַגַּע מִדְרָס, שֶׁהֲרֵי נָגְעָה בַּסַּנְדָּל הַטָּמֵא מִדְרָס, וְכִי נִשְׁבְּרָה אֹזֶן שְׁנִיָּה דְּפָרַח מִנַּהּ טֻמְאַת מִדְרָס אִשְׁתַּיַּר בֵּיהּ טֻמְאַת מַגָּע, דְּכָל הַסַּנְדָּל מְחֻבָּר לָאֹזֶן רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁנִּתַּקְּנָה:


אבל טמא מגע מדרס – because the first strap/handle, when it was broken/snapped, and it was repaired, that he brought another strap in place of the broken one and attached it to the sandal, it became defiled through contact with treading, for it touched the sandal that was impure through treading, but when the second strap snapped and their flowered from it the defilement of Midras/treading, there remained in it the defilement of contact, for the entire sandal was attached to the first strap that had been repaired.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:4)


**עַד שֶׁנִּפְסְקָה.** אֹזֶן שְׁנִיָּה:


עד שנפסקה – the second strap.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:5)


**טְהוֹרָה.** דְּכֵיוָן דְּנִשְׁבְּרוּ שְׁתֵּי אָזְנַיִם תּוּ לֹא חֲזִי לְמִידִי:


טהורה – for since the two straps were broken, it further was not appropriate for anything.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:6)


**עֲקֵבוֹ.** עוֹר שֶׁל סַנְדַּל הַמְכַסֶּה אֶת גֹּבַהּ הָרֶגֶל שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד שׁוֹקוֹ מֵאֲחוֹרָיו:


מפסק עקבו (if its heel was torn) – the leather of the sandal that covers the height of the foot that is corresponding to the foreleg from its backside.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:7)


**חוֹטְמוֹ.** שֶׁעוֹלֶה כְּנֶגֶד אֶצְבְּעוֹת הָרֶגֶל מִלְּפָנָיו:


חוטמו (toe piece, knotted strapplngs of a shoe) – that goes up corresponding to the toes of the foot from in front of him.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:8)


**טָהוֹר.** מִטֻּמְאָה דִלְמַפְרֵעַ, אֲבָל מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא:


טהור – [pure] from retroactive defilement, but it is susceptible to receive ritual defilement from here and onwards.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:9)


**סוֹלְיָם.** עוֹר שֶׁתַּחַת פַּרְסַת הָרֶגֶל בִּלְבַד, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עָקֵב. וּבְלַעַ"ז סול"א:


סוליים (sole, slipper) – the leather that is underneath the toes of the foot along. That it lacks a heel, and in the foreign language, SOLA.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:10)


**הָאֵמוּם.** דְּפוּס שֶׁל מִנְעָל עָשׂוּי מֵעוֹר מָלֵא שֵׂעָר:


האמום (shoe-makers last) – the frame of the shoe that is made from leather filled with hair.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:11)


**רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְטַהֵר.** דְּסָבַר לֹא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ שֶׁל מִנְעָל עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁמְטֶנָּה מֵעַל גַּבֵּי הָאֵמוּם:


ר' אליעזר מטהר – that he holds that the work of the shoe/foot-covering is not completed until it is detached from the shoe maker’s last.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:12)


**וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִין.** דְּחָשְׁבֵי לֵיהּ נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


וחכמים מטמאין – for they consider that the work was completed. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:13)


**כָּל חֲמָתוֹת צְרוּרוֹת.** נֹאדוֹת שֶׁנִּקְּבוּ נֶקֶב הַמּוֹצִיאָן מִידֵי טֻמְאָתָן וְקָשַׁר הַנֶּקֶב:


כל חמתות צרורות (all tied up goatskin) – leather skins that were perforated with an incision that removes them from their defilement and ties up the incision.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:14)


**טְהוֹרִין.** כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעָתִיד לְהַתִּיר הַקֶּשֶׁר:


טהורין – as they were, because he will eventually loosen the knot.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:15

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:15](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:15)


**חוּץ מִקֶּשֶׁר שֶׁל עַרְבִיִּים.** שֶׁאֵינוֹ נוֹחַ לְהַתִּיר:


חוץ מקשר של ערביים – which is not easy to untie.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:16

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:16](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:16)


**צְרוֹר שָׁעָה.** קֶשֶׁר הֶעָשׂוּי לְפִי שָׁעָה וְעוֹמֵד לְהַתִּיר:


צרור שעה (tied up for a time) – a knot that is made according to the hour and stands to be loosened.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:17

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:17](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:17)


**צְרוֹר עוֹלָם.** קֶשֶׁר הֶעָשׂוּי לִהְיוֹת קַיָּם לְעוֹלָם:


צרור עולם – a knot that is made to exist forever.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:4:18

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:18](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:4:18)


**כָּל חֲמָתוֹת צְרוּרוֹת טְהוֹרוֹת.** בֵּין צְרוֹר עוֹלָם בֵּין צְרוֹר שָׁעָה, וַאֲפִלּוּ שֶׁל עַרְבִיִּים. וַהֲלָכָה כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא:


כל המתות צרורות טהורות (all tied up goatskins are pure) – whether an eternal knot or a temporary knot, and even of that of the Arabs. But the Halakha is according to the first Tanna/teacher (see also Tractate Eduyot, Chapter 5, Mishnah 1).



### Mishnah 5

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:1)


**לְשָׁטִיחַ.** לִשְׁטֹחַ עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע וְלֵישֵׁב עָלָיו:


לשטיח (for a rug) – to stretch/spread on the ground and to sit upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:2)


**סְקֹרְטְיָא.** עוֹר שֶׁלּוֹבְשִׁים הָעַבְּדָנִים בִּשְׁעַת מְלַאכְתָּן:


סקורטיא (leather coat, leather apron, table cover) – leather that the tanners wear at the time of their work.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:3)


**קָטָבֹלְיָא.** עוֹר שֶׁמַּצִּיעִין עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּטָּה וְשׁוֹכְבִים עָלָיו:


קטבליא (hide spread over the bed-frame – see Tractate Kelim, Chapter 16, Mishnah 4) – leather that they spread over the bed and lie upon it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:4)


**עוֹר הַחַמָּר.** גָּרְסִינַן. וְלֹא גָרְסִינַן עוֹר הַחֲמוֹר. כְּלוֹמַר עוֹר שֶׁמֵּשִׂים הַחַמָּר עַל בְּגָדָיו כְּשֶׁמְּחַמֵּר אַחַר בְּהֶמְתּוֹ:


עור החמר (hide of an ass driver) – this is our reading But we don’t have the reading of עור החמור/the hide of the ass. That is to say, the leather that the ass-driver places on his clothes when he loads up his ass.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:5)


**עוֹר הַכַּתָּן.** עוֹר שֶׁנּוֹתְנִים לִפְנֵיהֶם אֻמָּנֵי פִשְׁתָּן כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יִדְבַּק הַנְּעֹרֶת שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן בְּבִגְדֵיהֶם:


עור הכתן (leather of the flax beater) – the leather that the flax artisans place before them in order that the hatchelled flax doesn’t stick to their clothing.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:6)


**עוֹר הַכַּתָּף.** שֶׁמֵּשִׂים הַכַּתָּף בִּכְתֵפוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יַזִּיק לוֹ הַמַּשְּׂאוֹי שֶׁעַל כְּתֵפוֹ:


עור הכתף (the leather of the porter/carrier) – the porter places on his shoulder in order that the load/burden that is on his shoulder not damage him.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:7)


**עוֹר הָרוֹפֵא.** רוֹפֵא הַחַבּוּרוֹת נוֹתֵן לְפָנָיו עוֹר שֶׁלֹּא יִטַּנְּפוּ בְגָדָיו בְּדַם הַפְּצָעִים:


עור הרופא – the doctor of the societies places before him leather so that his clothing will not be soiled with the blood of the wounds.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:8)


**עוֹר הָעֲרִיסָה.** שֶׁמְּשִׂימִים עַל עֲרִיסָה שֶׁל קָטָן:


עור העריסה (hide of the crib) – that the place on the crib of a small baby.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:9

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:9](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:9)


**עוֹר הַלֵּב שֶׁל קָטָן.** רְגִילִים הָיוּ לַחְגֹּר עוֹר עַל מָתְנֵי הַקָּטָן כְּנֶגֶד לִבּוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יַכֶּנּוּ הֶחָתוּל עַל לִבּוֹ וְיָמוּת:


עור הלב של קטן – it was customary to gird leather on the loins of a young child opposite his heart , so that the cat will not strike him on his heart and he will die.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:10)


**עוֹר הַכַּר וְהַכֶּסֶת.** שֶׁל מִטָּה:


עור הכר והכסת – of a bed.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:11

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:11](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:11)


**עוֹר הַסָּרוֹק.** עוֹר שֶׁחוֹגְרִים אֻמָּנֵי הַמַּסְרְקוֹת עַל מָתְנֵיהֶן:


עור הסרוק (leather of the dealer in hatchelled wool) – the leather that the artisans of combers gird on their loins.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:12

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:12](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:12)


**עוֹר הַסּוֹרֵק.** אֻמָּנִים הַסּוֹרְקִים פִּשְׁתָּן:


עור הסורק – artisans who comb flax.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:13

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:13](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:13)


**רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר מִדְרָס.** וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן טְמֵא מֵת. דְּהָא תְנַן בְּפֶרֶק בָּא סִימָן [נִדָּה דַּף מט] כָּל הַטָּמֵא מִדְרָס מִטַּמֵּא טְמֵא מֵת:


ר' אליעזר אומר מדרס – and all the more so, someone who came in contact with someone defiled by a corpse. For it taught in the Mishnah in chapter בא סימן/The Sign comes [Tractate] Niddah, (Chapter 6), Folio 49a (Mishnah 3): “Whatever is susceptible to Midras/treading uncleanness is susceptible to corpse uncleanness.”


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:5:14

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:14](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:5:14)


**וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים טְמֵא מֵת.** וְלֹא מִדְרָס, שֶׁאֵין עֲשׂוּיִין לֵישֵׁב עֲלֵיהֶן. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


וחכמים אומרים טמא מת – but not corpse uncleanness, or they are not made to be sat upon. And the Halakha is according to the Sages.



### Mishnah 6

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:1)


**עַב כְּסוּת.** כְּגוֹן לְבָדִין שֶׁעָשָׂה מֵהֶן כְּסוּת, זֶהוּ עַב כְּסוּת. וְכֵן עַב אַרְגָּמָן, לֶבֶד צָבוּעַ אַרְגָּמָן. כָּךְ פֵּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתַי. וַאֲנִי שָׁמַעְתִּי, עַב כְּסוּת, עוֹר שֶׁמְּכַסִּים בּוֹ הַבְּגָדִים. עַב אַרְגָּמָן. עוֹר שֶׁמְּכַסִּים בּוֹ אַרְגָּמָן:


עב כסות (thick clothing) – felt-cloaks (i.e., thick, fulled or felted stuff made of wool and hair) that one made from them clothing. This is the thick clothing. And similarly, the thick purple, to cloth that is colored purple. This is what my teachers/Rabbis explained. But I heard, “thick clothing” hide that they cover up the clothing. Thick purple – is the hide that they cover up with purple.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:2)


**תַּכְרִיךְ כְּסוּת.** עוֹר שֶׁכּוֹרְכִים בּוֹ הַבְּגָדִים:


תכריך כסות (wrapper for garments) – hide that they wrap up the clothing.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:3)


**תַּכְרִיךְ אַרְגָּמָן.** עוֹר שֶׁכּוֹרְכִים בּוֹ אַרְגָּמָן:


תכריך ארגמן (wrapper for purple) – hide that they wrap up the purple


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:4)


**חִפּוּי.** מִכְסֶה. תַּרְגּוּם מִכְסֶה, חוֹפָאָה:


חפוי – cover. The Aramaic translation of cover is חופאה/cover.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:6:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:5)


**טָהוֹר.** דְּהָכִי תַנְיָא, יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה חִפּוּיֵי כֵלִים לְטֻמְאָה, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר (ויקרא יא) אֲשֶׁר יֵעָשֶׂה מְלָאכָה בָהֶם, פְּרָט לְחִפּוּיֵי כֵלִים:


טהור – and such is taught in a Baraita, it is possible that I increase covering for vessels for defilement, as the inference teaches us (Leviticus 11:32): “any such article that can be put to use [shall be dipped in water,, and it shall remain unclean until evening],” excluding the covering of vessels.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:6:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:6:6)


**וְלַמִּשְׁקָלוֹת טָמֵא.** וְהָא דִתְנַן לְעֵיל סוֹף פֶּרֶק כָּל כְּלִי עֵץ שֶׁנֶּחְלַק, זֶה הַכְּלָל וְכוּ'‏ הֶעָשׂוּי לְחִפּוּי טָהוֹר, חִפּוּי דְּמִשְׁקָלוֹת שָׁאנֵי, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא עָשׂוּי לְקַבָּלָה, וְהַמִּשְׁקָלוֹת עַצְמָהּ אֵינָהּ כְלִי. וַהֲלָכָה כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא:


למשקלות – but it is taught in the Mishnah above at the conclusion of the Chapter [16], “Every wooden vessel that has been divided into two is clean” (Mishnah 8): “This is the general rule: [That which is made for a case is unclean.] And that which is made for a cover is clean.” But the cover of weights is different, because it is made for receiving, and the weights itself are not a vessel. But the Halakah is according to the first Tanna/teacher.



### Mishnah 7

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:7:1)


**שֶׁיֶּשׁ חֶסְרוֹן מְלָאכָה.** שֶׁעֲדַיִן חֲסֵרָה מַעֲשֶׂה וְאַחַר כָּךְ תִּתְקַיֵּם [הַמְּלָאכָה]:


שיש חסרון מלאכה – that there still is lacking action, but afterwards [the thought] is actualized.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:7:2)


**אֶלָּא הָעֻצְבָּה.** שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחֲסֵרָה מְלָאכָה, מַחֲשָׁבָה מְטַמְּאָתָהּ, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מַקְפִּידִין עַל חֶסְרוֹן מְלָאכָה שֶׁלָּהּ. וְעֻצְבָּה הוּא עוֹר הַמְכַסֶּה אֶת הַמֶּרְכָּב, וְאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה קִצּוּעַ, דְּכֵיוָן דַּעֲשׂוּיָה לְכִסּוּי אֵינוֹ חוֹשֵׁשׁ לְקִצּוּעַ:


העוצבה (fur trimmed of its ends, robe, cover) – even though it is missing work, the though defiles it, because they are not strict on its missing work. And עוצבה/fur trimmed of its ends, robe, cover is the hide that covers the riding seat/saddle, which doesn’t require trimming the ends of a skin, for since it is made for a cover, we don’t worry about trimming the ends of a skin.



### Mishnah 8

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:8:1)


**שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת.** דְּאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי לְמָכְרָן, וְעוֹשֶׂה מֵהֶן מִטּוֹת וְדוּלְפְּקָאוֹת וְטַבְלָאוֹת. חָשַׁב עֲלֵיהֶן לְדָבָר שֶׁרְאוּיִין לוֹ בְלֹא חֶסְרוֹן מְלָאכָה, מְקַבְּלִים טֻמְאָה מִיָּד:


של בעל הבית – that are not made to sell them (i.e., the hides), and he makes from them beds and delphicas and tablets [for writing]. He intended for them for something that are appropriate for hm without the loss of work, they are susceptible to receive ritual impurity immediately.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:8:2)


**וְשֶׁל עַבְּדָן.** דְּעָשׂוּי לִמָּכֵר, אֵין הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה מְטַמֵּאתָן. דַּעֲבִיד דְּמִמְּלִיךְ וּמוֹכְרָן וְהַלּוֹקֵחַ יַעֲשֶׂה מֵהֶן מִנְעָלִים, וַעֲדַיִן לֹא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתָּן לְכָךְ:


ושל עבדן (that belonging to a tanner) – that is made to sell, intention does not defile them, for he makes and in tends to sell them and the purchaser will make shoes from them, but their work had not yet been completed for this.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:8:3)


**שֶׁל גַּנָּב מַחֲשָׁבָה מְטַמֵּאתָן.** דִּקְנַנְהוּ בְיֵאוּשׁ. דְּקָסָבַר סְתָם גְּנֵבָה יֵאוּשׁ בְּעָלִים הוּא, דְּלֹא יָדְעֵי מִמַּאן לְתָבְעוֹ:


של גנב מחשבה מטמאתן – that he acquired them through despair. For he (i.e., the first Tanna) holds that mere theft is despair of the honors, for they do not know from whom to make a claim.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:8:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:8:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:8:4)


**וְשֶׁל גַּזְלָן אֵין מַחֲשָׁבָה מְטַמֵּאתָן.** וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָשַׁב עֲלֵיהֶן לְדָבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ חֶסְרוֹן מְלָאכָה. דִּסְתָם גְּזֵלָה אֵין בּוֹ יֵאוּשׁ בְּעָלִים, דְּכֵיוָן דְּיָדַע מַאן גָּזְלֵיהּ אָזֵיל וְתָבַע לֵיהּ בְּדִינָא:


ושל גזלן מחשבה מטמאתן (but of a robber, intention does not make them susceptible to uncleanness) – for even though he thought of them (i.e., the hides) for something where there is no loss of work, for a mere robbery there is no despair of the owners, for since he knew who stole from him, he goes and makes a claim against him in court.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:8:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:8:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:8:5)


**חִלּוּף הַדְּבָרִים.** סְתָם גְּזֵלָה אִיכָּא יֵאוּשׁ, דִּלְעֵינֵיהּ שָׁקַל מִנֵּיהּ וּמִחְזָא חֲזָא דְאֱינַשׁ אַלְמָא הוּא וּמִיַּאַשׁ, אֲבָל סְתָם גְּנֵבָה, סָבַר מַשְׁכַּחְנָא לֵיהּ לַגַּנָּב וְתָבַעְנָא לֵיהּ לְדִינָא וְלֹא מִיַּאַשׁ. וַהֲלָכָה כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא:


חילוף הדברים – (see also Talmud Bava Kamma 114a) – there is despair for a mere robbery. For according to his viewpoint, he (i.e., the robber) took from and it is fit and proper for he (i.e., the robber) is a strong/violent man and he despairs, but a mere theft, he (i.e., the owner) holds that the item I is found with the thief and he will make a claim against him in court and will not despair. But the Halakha is according to the first Tanna/teacher.



### Mishnah 9

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:9:1)


**עוֹר שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא מִדְרָס.** כְּגוֹן שָׁטִיחַ וְכַיּוֹצֵא בוֹ:


עור שהוא טמא מדרס – as for example a rug and things similar to it.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:9:2)


**אַף הָעוֹשֶׂה מִטְפַּחַת מִן הָעוֹר.** שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא מִדְרָס:


אף העושה מטפחת מן העור – which is impure through treading.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 26:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/26:9:3)


**טְמֵאָה.** הַמִּטְפַּחַת, שֶׁהַמִּטְפַּחַת דּוֹמָה לְשָׁטִיחַ, דִּפְעָמִים שֶׁהוּא יוֹשֵׁב עָלֶיהָ. אֲבָל אִם קָצַץ הַכְּסָתוֹת שֶׁל עוֹר הַטְּמֵאוֹת וְעָשָׂה מֵהֶן מִטְפָּחוֹת, טְהוֹרוֹת, מִידִי דַהֲוֵי אַכֵּלִים שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ. וּמִיהוּ מְקַבְּלוֹת טֻמְאָה מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא, כְּדִתְנַן לְעֵיל בְּפֶרֶק כ"ד:


טמאה – the towel/kerchief, for the towel/kerchief is similar to the rug, for sometimes he sits upon it. But if he cut the ritually impure chairs of hide and made of them towels/kerchiefs, since ) (it is something from vessels that were broken. But however, they are susceptible to receive ritual impurity from here onwards, as is taught in the Mishnah about in Chapter 24 [Mishnah 12].



## Chapter 27


### Mishnah 1

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:1)


**הַבֶּגֶד מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם חֲמִשָּׁה שֵׁמוֹת.** כְּדִמְפָרֵשׁ וְאָזֵיל, מִשּׁוּם כְּלִי קִבּוּל, מִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב, מִשּׁוּם אֹהָלִים, מִשּׁוּם אָרִיג, מִשּׁוּם שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ. וְכָל אֶחָד מֵהֶם מְשֻׁנֶּה שִׁעוּרוֹ זֶה מִזֶּה. כֵּיצַד, בֶּגֶד שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל, כְּגוֹן צְרוֹר מַרְגָּלִית דִּתְנַן לְעֵיל, אוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל שֶׁמֶן, אוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל שַׁעֲוָה, שִׁעוּרוֹ בְכָל שֶׁהוּא. [וּמִשּׁוּם מוֹשָׁב, אִם נִטְמָא] בְּמִדְרַס הַזָּב, שִׁעוּרוֹ אֵין פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים. וְאִם נַעֲשָׂה אֹהֶל לַמֵּת דִּכְתִיב (במדבר יט) וְהִזָּה עַל הָאֹהֶל, אֵין טָמֵא בְּפָחוֹת מִטֶּפַח עַל טֶפַח. וְאִם הוּא אַבְנֵט אוֹ חֲגוֹר, מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם אָרִיג, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ שִׁעוּר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה רָאוּי לְהִקָּרֵא בֶגֶד, שֶׁאֵין בְּרָחְבּוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת, אֲפִלּוּ הָכִי טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא אָרִיג. וְיָלְפִינַן לֵיהּ מִשַּׂק, מַה שַּׂק טָווּי וְאָרִיג אַף כָּל טָווּי וְאָרִיג. וְכָל שְׁאָר טֻמְאוֹת אֵין בֶּגֶד מִטַּמֵּא וְלֹא מְטַמֵּא בְּפָחוֹת מִשָּׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת עַל שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת, דְּאֵינוֹ חָשׁוּב לֹא לַעֲנִיִּים וְלֹא לַעֲשִׁירִים וְאֵינוֹ קָרוּי בֶּגֶד:


הבגד מיטמא משום חמשה שמות – as it is explained further on: because of receptacle, because of sitting, because of overshadowing [of a tent], because of a web [and] because of three fingerbreadths square. And each one of them, its measurement is different one from the other. How so? A cloth [of wool or linen] that has a receptacle, such as the piece of leather in which jewels are bound up, that is taught In the Mishnah above (Tractate Kelim, Chapter 26, Mishnah 2), or a receptacle of [olive] oil or a receptacle of wax, its measure is with a little bit., [and because of defilement by sitting, if it was defiled] though the treading of a person with gonorrhea, its measure is not less than three handbreadths by three handbreadths square. But if it became a tent of overshadowing for a corpse, as it is written (Numbers 19:18): “[A person who is pure shall take hyssop, dip it in the water,] and sprinkle on the tent [and on all the vessels and people who were there],” there is no defiling with less than a handbreadth by a handbreadth square. But if it is a belt/אבנט or a girdle/חגור, it becomes defiled because of the web, even though it does not have the measurement to be fit to be called a cloth, for it does not have the width of three fingers, even so, it is impure because it is a web. And we derive it from a sack. Just as a sack is spun and woven, even all that is spun and woven. And all of the rest of the defilements, the cloth is not defiled nor does it defile with less than three fingers square, for it is not important neither to the poor nor the rich and is not called a cloth.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:2)


**הַשַּׂק.** הוּא הָאָרִיג מִשֵּׂעָר וְנוֹצָה שֶׁל עִזִּים:


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:3)


**מִשּׁוּם אַרְבָּעָה שֵׁמוֹת.** דְּשִׁעוּר שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת [עַל שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת] אֵין בּוֹ:


משום ארבעה שמות – that it lacks the measurement of three fingerbreadths square.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:4)


**הָעוֹר מִשּׁוּם שְׁלֹשָׁה.** דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ מִשּׁוּם שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ, וְלֵית בֵּיהּ נַמִּי מִשּׁוּם אָרִיג:


העור משום שלשה – for it lacks [the measurement] because of three fingerbreadths square and because of a web.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:5)


**הָעֵץ מִשּׁוּם שְׁנַיִם.** דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ טֻמְאַת אֹהָלִים, כְּדִתְנַן בְּפֶרֶק בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין, כָּל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הָעֵץ אֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא טֻמְאַת אֹהָלִים. וְלֵית בֵּיהּ נַמִּי מִשּׁוּם אָרִיג, וְלֹא מִשּׁוּם שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ:


העץ משום שנים – that it lacks the defilement of tents, as it is taught I the Mishnah in [Tractate Shabbat, Chapter 2, Mishnah 3] the Chapter במה מדליקין/With what do we kindle [Shabbat candles]? “No product from a tree can contract “tent” uncleanness [except for flax].” And it also doesn’t have because of a web, and also because of three fingerbreadths square.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:6)


**הַחֶרֶס מִשּׁוּם אֶחָד.** מִשּׁוּם בֵּית קִבּוּל בִּלְבַד. דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ כָּל הָנֵי דְאָמְרִינַן. וּמִדְרָס נַמִּי לֵית בֵּיהּ, דִּכְתִיב בְּמִדְרַס הַזָּב (ויקרא טו) וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִגַּע בְּמִשְׁכָּבוֹ, מַקִּישׁ מִשְׁכָּבוֹ לוֹ, מַה הוּא שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ טָהֳרָה בְמִקְוֶה אַף כָּל שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ טָהֳרָה בְמִקְוֶה, פְּרָט לְחֶרֶס שֶׁאֵין לוֹ טָהֳרָה בְמִקְוֶה שֶׁאֵינוֹ נַעֲשֶׂה מִשְׁכָּב לַזָּב:


החרס משום אחד – because it is a receptacle alone But it doesn’t have all of these that we have mentioned (of the rest of the five). And it also does not have [defilement through] treading, as it is written concerning the treading of a person with gonorrhea (Leviticus 15:5): “Anyone who touches his bedding [shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and remain impure until evening].” He makes an analogy between “his bedding” to him, just as he who has ritual purity in the ritual bath/Mikveh, even all who have purity in the ritual bath, excluding earthenware that does not have purity in a ritual bath that does not become lying for a person with gonorrhea/a flux.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:1:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:7)


**אֵין לוֹ אֲחוֹרָיִם.** שֶׁאֵין כְּלִי חֶרֶס מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה מֵאֲחוֹרָיו, כְּדִכְתִיב (ויקרא יא) וְכָל כְּלִי חֶרֶשׂ אֲשֶׁר יִפֹּל מֵהֶם אֶל תּוֹכוֹ וְגוֹ'. וְאִם נָגְעָה טֻמְאָה מֵאֲחוֹרָיו לֹא נִטְמָא כְּלָל:


איל לו אחרויים – that an earthenware vessel is not susceptible to receive ritual impurity from its outside, as it is written (Leviticus 11:33): “And if any of hose fall into an earthen vessel, everything inside shall be impure [and -the vessel – itself you shall break].” If it came in contact with defilement from its outside, it was not defiled at all.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:1:8

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:1:8)


**שֶׁהוּא מִטַּמֵּא מִשּׁוּם אָרִיג.** מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּעוֹר, דַּאֲפִלּוּ חֲתָכוֹ לִרְצוּעוֹת דַּקּוֹת וַאֲרָגָן אֵינוֹ חֲשׁוּב אָרִיג:


שהוא מיטמא משום אריג – which is not the case with a hide, for even if he cut it into thin straps and wove them, it is not considered a web/weaving.



### Mishnah 2

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:2:1)


**הַבֶּגֶד מִטַּמֵּא.** לִטְמֵא מֵת וּלְכָל שְׁאָר טֻמְאוֹת חוּץ מִמִּדְרָס, מִשּׁוּם שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת עַל שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת. מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲזִי לַעֲנִיִּים, וְאִתְרַבֵּי מִדִּכְתִיב וְהַבֶּגֶד. אֲבָל לְמִדְרָס בָּעִינַן מִידִי דַּחֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה, וּבְפָחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים לֹא חֲזִי לְמוֹשָׁב:


הבגד מימטמא – for becoming defiled through contact with a corpse and for all the rest of the defilements except for that of treading, because of three fingerbreadth square, because it is appropriate for poor people, and it is derived by implication from as is it written (Leviticus 13:47): “[When an eruptive affection occurs in] a cloth, [of wool or linen fabric].” But for uncleanness by treading, we require something that is appropriate for sitting, and with less than three handbreadths by three handbreadths, it is not appropriate for seating.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:2:2)


**הַשַּׂק.** הָאָרוּג מִשֵּׂעָר וְנוֹצָה שֶׁל עִזִּים, שִׁעוּרוֹ בֵּין לִטְמֵא מֵת בֵּין לְמִדְרָס אֵין פָּחוּת מֵאַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים עַל אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים:


השק – that is woven from hair or feathers of goats, its measure whether for someone who had been defiled through contact with a corpse or for treading is not less than four handbreadths by four handbreadths.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:2:3)


**שָׁוִין.** לִטַּמֵּא טֻמְאַת מִדְרָס וּטְמֵא מֵת, שַׂק וְעוֹר וּמַפָּץ:


ושוין – to defile through defilement of treading/Midras and through defilement by contact with a corpse. A sack, or a hide or a mat.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:2:4)


**שְׁיָרָיו אַרְבָּעָה.** לְעִנְיָן זֶה נֶאֱמַר שִׁעוּרוֹ בְאַרְבָּעָה, כְּשֶׁבָּלָה וְנִקְרַע וְנִשְׁתַּיֵּר מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁעוּר אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים. אֲבָל בִּתְחִלַּת אֲרִיגָתוֹ אֵינוֹ מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה עַד שֶׁיֶּאֱרֹג כֻּלּוֹ. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר:


שייריו ארבעה – regarding this matter, it is stated [by Rabbi Meir] that its remnants are four [handbreadths]. When it became worn out and torn and there remained from it a measurement of four handbreadths, but at the beginning of its weaving, it doesn’t become susceptible to receive ritual defilement until it is completely woven. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Meir.



### Mishnah 3

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:3:1)


**הָיָה עוֹשֶׂה שְׁנַיִם מִן הַבֶּגֶד.** שְׁנֵי טְפָחִים:


היה ושה שנים מן הבגד – two handbreadths.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:3:2)


**וְאֶחָד מִן הַשַּׂק.** טֶפַח אֶחָד:


ואחד מן השק – one handbreadth.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:3:3)


**טָהוֹר.** דְּאֵין הַגָּרוּעַ מַשְׁלִים שִׁעוּרוֹ שֶׁל חָשׁוּב, דְּהַגָּרוּעַ שִׁעוּרוֹ מְרֻבֶּה. אֲבָל הֶחָשׁוּב מַשְׁלִים שִׁעוּרוֹ שֶׁל גָּרוּעַ, דַּאֲפִלּוּ בְשִׁעוּר מֻעָט הֶחָשׁוּב מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה:


טהור – for that which is inferior does not complete the measurement of that which is important, that the inferior’s measurement is greater. But the more highly regarded completes the measurement of the inferior, for even a little bit of that which is highly regarded is susceptible to receive ritual impurity.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:3:4)


**מִן הֶחָמוּר.** דְּסַגִּי לֵיהּ בְּשִׁעוּר מֻעָט:


מן החמור (more stringent) – that it is sufficient for it in a small measurement.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:3:5)


**מִן הַקַּל.** דְּבָעֵי שִׁעוּר מְרֻבֶּה. וְדַוְקָא כַסֵּדֶר הַזֶּה הַכָּתוּב בַּמִּשְׁנָה מִצְטָרְפִין לַקַּל שֶׁבָּהֶן, הַבֶּגֶד וְהַשַּׂק, הַשַּׂק וְהָעוֹר, הָעוֹר וְהַמַּפָּץ. אֲבָל בֶּגֶד וָעוֹר, אוֹ בֶּגֶד וּמַפָּץ, אוֹ שַׂק וּמַפָּץ, אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין, דְּהַמְחַבְּרָן בָּטְלָה דַעְתּוֹ אֵצֶל כָּל אָדָם. וּמִיהוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מֵהֶן טְלַאי עַל גַּבֵּי מַרְדַּעַת שֶׁל חֲמוֹר, כֻּלָּן מִצְטָרְפִין, דְּמֵאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן שֶׁיְּקַצֵּעַ טֶפַח וְיַעֲשֶׂה אוֹתוֹ טְלַאי לְמַרְדַּעַת שֶׁל חֲמוֹר, מִצְטָרֵף, דְּאֵינוֹ מַקְפִּיד לְשָׁם אִם הוּא מִשְּׁנֵי מִינִים:


מן הקל (from a category more lenient) – that requires a greater measurement. And especially like this arrangement that is written in the Mishnah, they combine to the [more] lenient of them: the cloth and the sack, the sack and the hide, the hide and the matting. But the cloth and the hide or the cloth and the matting, or the sack and matting do not combine, for one who attaches them, has annulled his thinking with regard to every person. But however, to make of them a patch on the pack-saddle/cushion – consisting of patches – of a donkey, all of them combine, that from whichever of them will trim a handbreadth and make it a path on the pack-saddle/cushion of a donkey, they combine, for he is not strict for there, if it is from two species.



### Mishnah 4

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:4:1)


**מִכֻּלָּם.** מֵאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן שֶׁיְּקַצֵּעַ טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח רָאוּי לִטַּמֵּא מוֹשָׁב. דְּהָנֵי שִׁעוּרֵי דִתְנַן לְעֵיל, הַבֶּגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ לְמִדְרָס וְהַשַּׂק אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה וְכוּ', לֹא הָוֵי אֶלָּא בַחֲתִיכַת בֶּגֶד אוֹ שַׂק אוֹ עוֹר אוֹ מַפָּץ שֶׁלֹּא חֲתָכָהּ וְתִקְּנָהּ לִישִׁיבָה, אֲבָל הַמְקַצֵּעַ דְּהַיְנוּ הַמְחַתֵּךְ וְהַמְתַקֵּן מֵאֶחָד מִכֻּלָּן טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח כְּדֵי לֵישֵׁב עָלָיו, טָמֵא מוֹשָׁב, שֶׁכֵּן לִפְעָמִים מַקְצִיעִין וְעוֹשִׂים טְלַאי מֵאֶחָד מֵהֶן לְמַרְדַּעַת שֶׁל חֲמוֹר וְיוֹשְׁבִים עָלָיו, וְלֹא הָוֵי אֶלָּא טֶפַח עַל טֶפַח:


מכולם – from any of them that he will trim (from the list provided in the first two Mishnayot of this chapter) one handbreadth by one handbreadth, it is appropriate to become defiled through sitting, For those measurements that are taught in the Mishnah above, the cloth is three [handbreadths] by three [handbreadths] square for uncleanness through treading and the sack is four [handbreadths] by four [handbreadths] square, etc., it would not other than with a piece of cloth or sack or hide or matting that was not cut or repaired for sitting. But trimming, that is cutting and repair from one of all of them one-handbreadth by one-handbreadth square in order to sit upon it, is impure through sitting, for occasionally one trims and makes patches from one of them for the pack-saddle/cushion of a donkey and sits upon it, but it will not be other than a handbreadth by a handbreadth.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:4:2)


**מִכָּל מָקוֹם.** וַאֲפִלּוּ מִן הַצְּדָדִים. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר דְּמִן הַצְּדָדִים לֹא חֲזִי לְמוֹשָׁב. וְאֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:


מכל מקום – and even from the sides. But Rabbi Shimon holds that from the sides is not appropriate for sitting. But the Halakha is not according to Rabbi Shimon [but according to the Sages – anyone who trims anywhere one-handbreadth by one-handbreadth, it is impure.].



### Mishnah 5

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:5:1)


**נָפָה וּכְבָרָה.** שֶׁל עוֹר הֵם. וּפְעָמִים עוֹשִׂים נָפָה מִשֵּׂעָר, וְדִינָהּ כְּדִין שַׂק. וְכֵן פְּעָמִים עוֹשִׂים כְּבָרָה מֵחֲבָלִים שֶׁל שִׁיפָה וְשֶׁל גֶּמִי, וְדִינָהּ כְּדִין מַפָּץ:


נפה וכברה (sifter or a sieve) – they are [made] of [leather] hides. And sometimes we make a sifter from hair, and its law is like the law for a sack. And similarly, sometimes they make a sieve from ropes of parings/shavings used for basket work and of bulrushes/reed-grass, and its law is like that of matting.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:5:2)


**עַד שֶׁיְּקַצֵּעַ.** שֶׁיַּחְתֹּךְ וִיתַקֵּן לְמוֹשָׁב. וַהֲלָכָה כַּחֲכָמִים:


עד שיקצע (until one trims it/cuts off rough ends) – that he will cut and repair for sitting (see Tractate Kelim, Chapter 20, Mishnah 4). And the Halakha is according to the Sages.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:5:3)


**אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ גָבֹהַּ טֶפַח.** וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּשֶׁל גָּדוֹל לֹא מִטַּמֵּא בִּבְצִיר מִטֶּפַח, כְּדִתְנַן לְעֵיל בְּפֶרֶק הַשֻּׁלְחָן וְהַדְּלֻפְקִי [מִשְׁנָה ג], כִּסֵּא שֶׁל קָטָן חֲזִי לִישִׁיבָה אֲפִלּוּ בִּבְצִיר מִטֶּפַח:


אע"פ שאין בו גבוה טפח – and even though it is [the seat] of an adult, it does not become susceptible to receive ritual purity until it is less than a handbreadth, as is taught in the Mishnah above in the Chapter “The Table and the Delphica” [Chapter 22, Mishnah 3], a seat for a child is appropriate for sitting even with less than a handbreadth. [Without legs, the seat is unsusceptible.]


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:5:4)


**עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בוֹ כַשִּׁעוּר.** אִם הוּא מִבֶּגֶד עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה, כְּשִׁעוּר טֻמְאַת הַבֶּגֶד לְמִדְרָס:


עד שיהיו בו כעשיר – if it is from cloth – until it will be three-handbreadths by three-handbreadths square, according to the measurement of the defilement of a cloth for uncleanness through treading.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:5:5)


**וְנִמְדָּד כָּפוּל.** שְׁלֹשָׁה לְפָנָיו וּשְׁלֹשָׁה לְאַחֲרָיו, נִמְצָא כְשֶׁפּוֹשְׁטוֹ שֶׁהוּא שִׁשָּׁה אֹרֶךְ עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה רֹחַב, אָרְכּוֹ כִפְלַיִם כְּרָחְבּוֹ:


ונמדד כפול – three [handbreadths] in front of him, and three [handbreadths] in back of him, I is found that when he stretches it out, it is six [handbreadths] in length by three [handbreadths] in width square, and its length is double its width.



### Mishnah 6

###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:6:1)


**אֵלּוּ נִמְדָּדִים כְּפוּלִין.** דְּצָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַשִּׁעוּר מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִים, כֵּיוָן דְּאוֹרְחַיְהוּ לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִים, אִי הָוֵי הַשִּׁעוּר מִצַּד אֶחָד לֹא מַהֲנֵי. פֵּרוּשׁ אַחֵר, נִמְדָּדִים כְּפוּלִים, שֶׁכָּל בֶּגֶד בִּמְקוֹם הַחֲתָךְ דֶּרֶךְ הַחוּטִים לָצֵאת מִמֶּנּוּ וּמִתְקַלְקֵל וְנוֹחַ לִקָּרַע, וְדֶרֶךְ הַתּוֹפְרִים לִכְפֹּל מְעַט סְבִיב הַחֲתָךְ וְתוֹפֵר, וְהַיְנוּ נִמְדָּד כָּפוּל דְּקָתָנֵי, דִּלְאַחַר שֶׁנִּכְפַּל צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בוֹ כְדֵי מִדָּתוֹ, וְאִי לֵיכָּא כְדֵי מִדָּתוֹ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִם הָיָה מַתִּיר הַתְּפִירָה וּפוֹשְׁטוֹ הָיָה בוֹ כְדֵי מִדָּתוֹ, לֹא מַהֲנֵי:


אלו נמדדים כפולים – that it needs the measurement to be from two sides. Since it is their manner to use them from two sides, if the measurement is from one side, it is not effective. Another explanation, that it is measured double, that a cloth in the place of cut, it is the manner that the threads go out from it and it becomes ruined and is easily torn, and it is the manner of sewers to double a bit around the cut and sew. And this is measured double as it has been taught, for after it is doubled, there needs to be enough in order to its measurement, but if there isn’t enough for its measurement, even though that if one would loosen the stitch and stretch it out, there would be enough for its measurement. It is not effective.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:6:2)


**אַנְפַּלְיָא.** מִנְעָל הַמַּגִּיעַ עַד הָאַרְכֻּבָּה. בֵּין שֶׁל בֶּגֶד בֵּין שֶׁל עוֹר:


אנפליא (socks) – socks that reach until the knee. Whether they are of cloth or of hide/leather.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:6:3)


**פְּמוֹלִינְיָא.** כְּמִין מִכְנָסַיִם גְּדוֹלִים מִמָּתְנַיִם וְעַד יְרֵכַיִם, וְיֵשׁ לְהֵן שְׁנָצִים:


פמוליניא (knee breeches/long stockings) – like a kind of large undergarments/trousers that go from the loins until the thighs, and they have straps.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Bartenura%20on%20Mishnah%20Kelim/r/27:6:4)


**וְכוֹבַע.** שֶׁבָּרֹאשׁ:


כובע – that is on the head.


###### Bartenura on Mishnah Kelim 27:6:5
